G93A finished remediation batch reports no numbers — carry the run's counts into the Jira fix-package explanation through the run-log contract
drydocs-remediationP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: RIDER ADDED AT G107's CLOSE (2026-08-25). G107's acceptance cited this item as its precedent -- "exactly as drydocs_remediation does after G93" -- but G93 had not run, so there was nothing to copy: remediation opens no run log and logs nothing at all. G107 therefore built the shape FIRST, and this item now joins it rather than minting a fifth variant. USE drydocs_core.run_log.batch_run_log, the shared context manager G107 added, not a hand-rolled open/try/finally. It yields a mutable summary dict, closes on BOTH the success and the failure path, re-raises the batch's exception unchanged, and swallows an unwritable log directory so a run log can never be the reason a batch fails. Clause (a) below ("a remediation batch opens a LoaderRunLog and closes it with its counts") is satisfied by wrapping the batch in that helper and filling the summary -- the counts clause is unchanged, only the mechanism is now decided. The four already wired are lineage's write_curated and write_rua, docmeta's two connectors, and the vendor scrape's capture; remediation is the fifth and last of the cadences Idea-152 named. REPRODUCED AT THE GROOM, sample-only (J18): render_handoff() emits Findings, Scope, Change, Equivalence evidence, Acceptance and Rollback -- and not one count of what the run actually processed. The reviewer reading the ticket cannot tell whether the batch examined nine jobs or nine hundred, so "we fixed it" carries no denominator. Meanwhile the extractors already model exactly this (ExtractCoverage.summary() with the G60 prepost_* source split, XmlDefsCoverage, findings counted by rule) -- the pattern exists, the handoff just never reads it. (a) THE COUNTS RIDE THE RUN LOG, NOT THE CONSOLE. A remediation batch opens a LoaderRunLog (drydocs_core/run_log.py) and closes it with its counts in the summary, the same contract the loaders already use; the handoff is rendered FROM that recorded summary. Console output is a view of the run, never its record. (b) NUMBERS ARE RECORDED, NOT RECOMPUTED AT RENDER TIME. HandoffPackage carries the run's counts as data; render_handoff stays a pure deterministic template (the module's existing house rule). A test proves the rendered body reports the recorded numbers even when the finding list handed to the renderer is a subset -- otherwise the explanation silently re-derives a denominator from whatever survived filtering. (c) WHAT THE SECTION CARRIES, at minimum: objects examined, objects changed, findings by rule id and by severity, the ratified / unratified split (a warn-only finding must not inflate a fix count), and anything skipped WITH ITS REASON -- unparseable is counted, never dropped. (d) ABSENCE IS EXPLICIT. A package assembled without a run summary renders the section as not recorded rather than omitting it, so a missing measurement never reads as a clean run. (e) IT DOES NOT RESTATE THE EQUIVALENCE PROOF. proven / compared jobs stay in their own section with the three-valued PASS / DIVERGED / NOT PROVEN verdict; coverage counts what the run looked at, the proof states what it demonstrated, and merging them would let a big denominator read as evidence. Zero graph writes. No new relationship type, no vocabulary entry, no gate.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-12 (targeted groom) from Idea-113, user direction the same day. Verified at the groom: render_handoff has no counts section, and nothing under drydocs_remediation/ imports run_log at all today (drydocs/cli.py is the only LoaderRunLog caller) -- so the batch-side run log is part of this item, not an assumed prerequisite. MODULE: drydocs-remediation, chosen because both change points (jira.py, the batch entry point) are there; drydocs_core/run_log.py is ADOPTED unchanged. If the run-log contract itself needs a field it does not have, that is a drydocs-core follow-up, not this item. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the support -> dev handoff of the runbook automation use case. The ticket is where a support engineer's evidence becomes a developer's instruction, and an explanation without counts cannot be audited later against the run that produced it.

G94Which standard does a job validate against? A selection resolver on job type, job role and ETL engine — and an executable proof that the DD version digit never selects one
drydocs-coreP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology
depends on: G84

Acceptance: Today the token set is selected by ONE dimension: required_tokens(JobType) over FILE_WATCHER / PUBLISHER / BOTH. User direction 2026-08-12 rules the real selection a DECISION TREE -- a FileWatcher validates against the FileWatcher standard; a COMMAND job selects on its ETL ENGINE FIRST (DPL, Ab Initio, Informatica -- names the launcher registry already classifies as invocation_type DPL / ABINITIO / INFORMATICA) and falls back to a GENERIC standard carrying only the shared tokens (the DevX project key, the EMAIL_DL contacts) when no engine is identified. (a) ONE FUNCTION, ONE ANSWER: a selector takes the derived TASKTYPE, the registered JOB_ROLE token and the launcher classification, and returns a STANDARD IDENTITY plus the token set that identity requires. Selection is separated from validation -- validate() keeps taking what it is given, so the tree can be re-ruled without touching the parser. (b) THE GUARDRAIL BECOMES A TEST, which is the point of the item: guidelines section 7.5 and G84 clause (c) rule the DD digit a grammar VERSION that MUST NOT select a template or a standard. A test asserts that the SAME job under "DD1|" and under a hypothetical "DD2|" selects the SAME standard, so the next person who reaches for the version slot as a selector reds a guard instead of shipping it. (c) THE ENGINE BRANCH IS DECLARED, NOT INVENTED. Per-engine standards get their identity and their branch; the CONTENT of each engine's token set is NOT ruled here -- an engine with no ruled set inherits the generic set and REPORTS that it did, so an unruled engine is visible rather than silently generic. Inventing per-engine required tokens in this item is out of scope and fails it. (d) THE GENERIC SET IS DERIVED, NOT RETYPED: it is the shared subset already carried in the registry (JobType.BOTH plus the FOLDER_VARIABLES entries), so it cannot drift from TOKEN_REGISTRY. (e) UNSELECTABLE IS AN ANSWER. A job whose engine cannot be classified and whose job role is absent returns the generic standard WITH a reason, and coverage counts the reasons -- the adoption-not-compliance measure G84 established. Zero graph writes; every token stays proposed; no relationship-vocabulary entry and no property term is touched. Storage of the selected standard is explicitly NOT here -- see G95.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-12 (targeted groom) from Idea-114, clause 1 (the decision tree). Verified at the groom: config/launcher-registry.yaml already emits DPL / ABINITIO / INFORMATICA invocation types through classify_executable(), so the engine dimension needs no new classifier; JOB_ROLES is already the C30 discriminator set (PUBLISHER / PLACEMENT / TRUST_INGEST); and required_tokens() is currently keyed on JobType alone, which is the gap. depends_on G84 because the selector must read the population and the version the sentinel parse produces, and G84 is where both were built. WHY THIS HALF IS BUILDABLE AND THE OTHER HALF IS NOT: choosing WHICH standard applies is derivable from data the repo already has. Choosing WHERE a standard lives, what its id is, and whether a team may hold its own profile is a contract change to the parse contract -- that is G95, and it goes to the gate first.

G106drydocs prune-logs: nothing rotates, caps or sweeps the run-log directory today — retention as a verb mirroring prune-snapshots, not a background sweeper thread
drydocs-loadP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology
depends on: G104

Acceptance: SME RULINGS FOLDED IN 2026-08-25 — read before the original acceptance below. (A) THE QA LEDGER IS NOT EXEMPT. It gets 90-day retention like everything else. The acceptance below puts the exemption question in the open ("an append-only audit ledger may legitimately be exempt, but then the exemption is in the code and in --help"); it is answered NOT-EXEMPT. The reason is the same one that sets the API audit window: 90 days of question text is what makes the ledger useful for search metrics, where an unbounded ledger is just an audit relic. Note the consequence honestly in --help -- the `run` line is the ONLY place full question text lands (:AgentRun carries sha256 + length), so sweeping it destroys the only record that turns a hash back into words. That is a deliberate 90-day horizon, not an oversight. (B) EVERY WINDOW COMES FROM THE DECLARATION, never from a literal or a flag default in this file. ADR 0014 clause 4 as amended: `prune-logs` with no arguments does the declared thing and flags are one-off overrides. Retention is per kind in config/log-kinds.yaml (G105), so `api` 90, `qa` 90, `api-debug` short, `load` its own -- this verb reads them rather than knowing them. (C) STILL OPEN, and it must not be silently defaulted: `--max-bytes` has no ruled number. The age bound is settled; the size cap is not. Either the SME sets it or this item ships age-only with the size bound recorded as deferred and its trigger named. Do not invent a cap -- a size sweep that nobody chose is how a retention verb deletes something someone wanted. A `drydocs prune-logs` verb in `drydocs/cli.py`, built as a deliberate mirror of the existing `prune-snapshots` so the two read the same at the prompt: DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT (it prints what it would delete and exits non-destructively unless an explicit apply flag is passed), bounded by both age (`--older-than-days`, defaulting to `RuntimeSettings.log_retention_days`) and total size (`--max-bytes`), and reporting a per-file table plus a total. It covers every file family that shares the log directory — the per-run `<kind>.<name>.<ts>.log` files from `run_log.py`, the SQL run logs, and `agents/common/llm_ledger.py`'s JSONL ledger — because the whole point of the finding is that three families share one directory under two naming rules and NONE of them rotate, cap or sweep. The ledger's retention is stated explicitly, whichever way it goes: an append-only audit ledger may legitimately be exempt, but then the exemption is in the code and in `--help`, not in the gap between them. A test drives the verb over a temp directory holding files of both naming shapes and asserts (a) dry-run deletes nothing, (b) the age bound and the size bound each select the expected set, (c) a file the retention policy exempts survives both. Acceptance: (a) THE THREE-WAY RULE, not a two-way one. `drydocs_lineage/writer.py` computes `unconfirmed = len(node_hosts) > 1` and stamps `identity_unconfirmed_across_hosts` without reading scope. G56 now DERIVES `storage_scope` from the collected mount table, so the flag becomes: `shared` AND the same `mount_source` on every host means CONFIRMED (one export on N hosts is one file); `shared` with DIFFERENT mount sources stays unconfirmed AND gets its own count, because two hosts mounting the same path from different exports is a real finding rather than a non-finding; `local` or `unknown` stays unconfirmed exactly as today. Implementing only the first two thirds re-creates the defect in the other direction, so the middle case must be visible in the coverage line, not folded into the general count. The reason this is not a one-line change is that `storage_scope: shared` does not by itself say two hosts see the same file. `mount_source` is stamped on every occurrence record by G56 precisely so the equality test is cheap; the item uses it and does not infer identity from scope alone. They are replaced by the rule as built. The header block near the top of the file that describes the over-flagging also stops describing a live defect. It was written against this shape and needs no edit; the item must not "helpfully" adjust it. J57Acceptance that compares TOTALS lets two sessions agree on a number and both be wrong — the port and snapshot rituals record the failing-test ID SET, and a clean claim runs the repo-wide guard family

Acceptance: (a) SET, NOT COUNT, IN THE PORT/RECONCILE ACCEPTANCE. Wherever the port and reconcile procedures today ask for a failing-test TOTAL (suite counts, Track-1 tallies, "N of N are the documented clusters"), they ask instead for the sorted set of failing test NODE IDS, and the acceptance is a SET DIFF between the baseline and the result — not an equality of two integers. The total stays visible alongside it; this is a swap of what the comparison keys on, not a removal of the number people read. (b) THE FAILURE MODE IS WRITTEN DOWN WHERE THE STEP IS. The rule carries its one-sentence reason at the point of use: two sessions independently measured the same failing-test total and treated the agreement as confirmation, but one of the failures was new and self-inflicted — agreeing on a total is not agreeing on its contents. A rule with no recorded reason is the first thing a later session optimises away. (c) THE CLEAN-CLAIM CONVENTION. A "this is clean" claim after a targeted fix is defined as insufficient on the targeted files alone: it requires a run of the REPO-WIDE guard family — module boundary, render determinism, no-render-parsing, repo-path guards — whose failures no targeted-file verification can catch. Name those guards by their test-file paths so the convention is executable rather than an exhortation, and verify each named path exists in this tree at the time of writing. (d) THE SNAPSHOT RITUAL'S GREEN-AT-HEAD CHECK IS COVERED. `snapshot.ps1`'s CI check already matches on HEAD's sha (Idea-111's fix); state explicitly whether its verdict is a count comparison and, if so, apply (a) to it — or record that it is already identity-based and needs no change. Either answer is a pass; an unexamined third surface is not. (e) THE DOCUMENTED SURFACES ARE ENUMERATED, NOT SAMPLED. The item lists every producer surface that compares totals today and states, per surface, whether it changed or why it did not. A partial sweep here reproduces exactly the class of miss the rule exists to prevent. (f) OUT OF SCOPE: changing any test, guard or CI stage. This item edits PROCEDURE — skills, prompts, the operating guide — and ships no behaviour change to the suite.

J58Governed config YAML has no required identity header — one JSON Schema for the four-key block, scoped BY FILE CLASS so template-class files are exempt, with schema coverage sequenced first
configP8chorep2sonnet / main
release-infrastructure

Acceptance: (a) THE HEADER IS ONE JSON SCHEMA, NOT N BESPOKE TESTS. The four-key identity block already in use — `schema:` / `source:` / `classification:` / `updated:`, exemplified by `config/source-mappings/design-docs.yaml` — is expressed once as a JSON Schema under `config/schemas/`, alongside the six that already live there, and every guard validates against that one file. Optional `layer:` / `domain:` keys are admitted where the vocabulary domain applies. (b) FILE CLASS DECIDES WHO MUST CARRY IT — and the classes are enumerated in the schema's own prose, not inferred by a glob nobody can find. REQUIRED on governed DATA files (source mappings, registries, taxonomy config, gate prompts). FORBIDDEN on template-class files: a hand-maintained date inside a file that a `copier` update three-way MERGES is a guaranteed update conflict, which is the ADR 0015 D4 seam. Any file in neither class is listed explicitly with its reason — a default-deny posture, matching `test_module_boundary.py`'s UNCLASSIFIED rule. (c) SCHEMA COVERAGE FIRST, `updated:` COVERAGE SECOND — as two separately-green steps inside this item. `schema:` is the TE-load-bearing key (copier migrations key on it), so it lands and goes green before any `updated:` work starts. The measured 2026-08-27 baseline to close against: of 138 non-backlog tracked YAMLs, 32 carry no `schema:` key and 104 carry no `updated:` key. Re-measure at pull time and report both the found baseline and the closed one; a drifted baseline is expected and is not a reason to skip the measurement. (d) GATE PROMPTS GET THE DATE KEY THEY LACK. The 53 gate-prompt specs are already a governed exception with their own enforced header (Module / Source / Registry ref / Classification, via `test_gate_pages`), but carry NO date key at all. Extend their required set with `updated:` under the same schema, and keep `test_gate_pages` as the enforcement point rather than adding a second guard over the same files. (e) PRESENCE AND SHAPE ONLY — FRESHNESS IS NOT THIS ITEM. The guard checks that required keys exist and match the schema. It does NOT compare `updated:` against anything; the lying-date problem is J59's, deliberately split because the check that would catch it cannot run in CI (see J59 clause (a)). (f) IT RUNS IN THE DEFAULT SUITE with no live services, and it is green on the tree as left by this item — which means every file the new rule covers actually carries the block by the time this closes, not just the ones that already did.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-28 from Idea-181 (captured 2026-08-27, Med; user review request). Split into two items plus a small Python-side chore because the entry's own persona review — `docs/reviews/persona-python-architect-idea-181.md`, run against copier / copier-pdm / ss-python / full-stack-fastapi-template — corrected two of the original prescriptions before grooming, and the corrections change the SEQUENCING, not just the wording. F1/F2 (copier updates are three-way merges keyed on `.copier-answers.yml` `_commit`, not wholesale rewrites) is why (b) scopes by file class instead of applying the block everywhere. F3 (the git-compare guard is blind in CI) is why freshness left this item entirely and became J59. Verified before grooming: `config/schemas/` holds six schemas today, so (a) adds a seventh to an existing pattern rather than inventing a location; `config/gate-prompts/` holds 53 specs. Epic release-infrastructure / module config / phase 8 follows J55, the nearest precedent (also `module: config`, also a repo-wide convention given an enforcement point). J59The one freshness key the repo has LIES — 16 of 24 dated YAML headers are stale against git, so the `updated:` field needs a check that compares it to something, and that check cannot live in CI
configP8chorep3sonnet / main
release-infrastructure
depends on: J58

Acceptance: (a) THE GUARD IS A PRODUCER-SIDE LOCAL HOOK, AND THE REASON IS RECORDED. Freshness is checked by comparing each governed file's `updated:` value against `git log -1 --format=%as <path>`. That comparison is BLIND IN CI — the workflow uses a shallow checkout with no `fetch-depth` override (verified against `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so per-file git dates are not available to the runner and a CI-hosted version of this check would report green while measuring nothing. It therefore ships as a pre-commit hook, which means creating the repo's first `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (none exists today) plus the hook script, with installation named in the session ritual. A check that cannot run where it is installed is the exact failure this item exists to avoid repeating. (b) IT SOLVES THE LYING PROBLEM, NOT THE PRESENCE PROBLEM. Presence is J58's. This one fails when `updated:` disagrees with the file's git last-touch date beyond a stated tolerance, and the tolerance is written with its reason rather than picked. Worked example to close against, measured 2026-08-27: of 24 files carrying `updated:`, 16 are stale — `PORT-MANIFEST.yaml` itself reads `updated: 2026-08-20` against a git date of 2026-08-27. Re-measure at pull time. (c) `updated:` IS A PER-SIDE FIELD AT THE PORT MANIFEST, AND THIS SAYS SO. Git dates DO NOT survive the port: disjoint histories stamp every ported file with port day, so the company's git date for a file is the day it arrived, not the day its content changed. That is precisely why the IN-FILE date is the cross-repo freshness mechanism and why `updated:` must be declared a per-side field in `PORT-MANIFEST.yaml` — the doc-source-registry field-split is the precedent. Without this clause the hook would make every ported file look freshly touched on their side. (d) THE HOOK IS ADVISORY-CAPABLE AND NEVER BLOCKS A COMMIT SILENTLY. It either fails loudly with the file list and the two dates per file, or it is bypassed with a recorded, deliberate flag. It never passes because it could not determine a date — an unresolvable file is reported, not skipped. (e) OUT OF SCOPE: adding `updated:` to files that lack it (J58 clause (c)), and the Python docstring standard (J60).

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-28 from Idea-181 (captured 2026-08-27), the freshness half. Split from J58 on the entry's own persona-review finding F3 — the git-compare guard is blind in CI — which turns "one guard" into two mechanisms with different homes. Keeping them in one item would have produced a guard that ships to CI, passes, and measures nothing, which is the same shape as the defect it is meant to catch. `depends_on: [J58]` is real, not decorative: there is nothing to compare until the `updated:` key is required and populated, and the schema J58 writes is what tells this hook which files it governs. Epic release-infrastructure / module config / phase 8 follows J58. Model sonnet; priority p3 rather than p2 because a stale in-file date is a smaller harm than a missing one, and because the hook is producer-machine-local and so cannot be enforced for anyone who has not installed it — which is itself worth stating in the close note as a known limit rather than discovered later.

J60Module and package docstrings are enforced by nothing — enable ruff's D100/D104 instead of writing a bespoke guard, and fill the modules that have no docstring at all
docsP8chorep3sonnet / main
release-infrastructure

Acceptance: (a) THE RULE COMES FROM THE LINTER ALREADY IN THE GATE, NOT FROM A NEW TEST. `[tool.ruff.lint].select` currently reads `["E", "F", "W", "I", "B", "UP", "N", "RUF"]` — no `D` rules at all. Add `D100` (missing docstring in public module) and `D104` (missing docstring in public package) to `select`, with the pydocstyle convention set explicitly so the rest of the `D` family is not switched on by accident. CI already blocks on `ruff check` (J10 stage 5), so the enforcement point is free; a bespoke docstring test would be a second, weaker copy of a check the toolchain ships. (b) THE EXISTING EXEMPTIONS SURVIVE. The vendored Anthropic skill scripts and the captured experiment records are already excluded from ruff for recorded reasons; the new rules inherit those exclusions unchanged. Tests and scripts get a per-file-ignore if the first run says they need one, with the reason written next to it in the same style as the existing entries. (c) THE MODULES WITH NO DOCSTRING ARE FILLED, NOT IGNORED. The 2026-08-27 measurement found 31 modules with no docstring; re-measure at pull time and report both numbers. Each new docstring says what the module is FOR in one or two sentences of U.S. business-technical English — not a restatement of the filename. Where the module has an obvious governing record (an ADR, a gate, a backlog id), cite it, which is what 214 of the existing docstrings already do; where it does not, do not invent one. (d) `ruff check` AND `ruff format --check` BOTH EXIT 0 on the tree as left by this item, verified locally before push, so CI's last two stages are green at the sha that ships this. (e) OUT OF SCOPE: function and class docstrings (D101/D102/D103), any date or provenance key inside a docstring, and the YAML header standard — that is J58/J59. This item adds two rules and the prose they demand, nothing else.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-28 from Idea-181 (captured 2026-08-27), prescription F4 of its python-architect persona review: enable ruff D100/D104 rather than build a bespoke docstring guard. Filed separately from J58/J59 because the language, the enforcement mechanism and the failure mode are all different — those two are JSON-Schema guards over governed YAML; this one is two lines of lint config plus the writing they oblige. Verified before grooming: `select` in `pyproject.toml` carries no `D` rules; the vendored-skill and captured-experiment ruff exclusions exist with their reasons recorded. Epic release-infrastructure / module docs / phase 8. `module: docs` rather than a code component because the deliverable is prose about modules plus a lint setting, and it spans every package rather than belonging to one — the same call J50/J52/J54 make. Model sonnet: (c) is writing, not lookup, and a haiku pass would produce filename restatements. Priority p3: nothing is broken today. The value is that a module arriving with no docstring stops being invisible, which matters most to the Team Edition reader who has no author to ask.

J61A shared checkout blocked by another live session's uncommitted file can neither pull nor push, and the branch guardrail returns EMPTY in the detached worktree that is the only way out — write the recovery down instead of improvising it once per session
docsP8chorep2sonnet / main
release-infrastructure

Acceptance: (a) THE RECOVERY LIVES WHERE THE BLOCK IS HIT. The session ritual in CLAUDE.md section 0 today opens with "Start - git pull" and says nothing about that pull failing. It gains the named recovery for the one case that actually occurs on this desktop - the pull aborts because a file the incoming merge touches is dirty from the OTHER live session in the same tree, and the abort is wholesale even though nothing the arriving session intends to touch is involved. The recipe is a command sequence, not advice - fetch, add a detached worktree at origin slash main under the scratchpad, work and stage by explicit path there, commit, push HEAD to main, remove the worktree - and every command in it is run once against this tree while the item is being written, with the observed output recorded in the close note. A recipe nobody executed is the class of thing that is wrong the first time somebody needs it. (b) THE BRANCH GUARDRAIL IS GIVEN AN ANSWER FOR THE DETACHED CASE, BECAUSE TODAY IT HAS NONE. Section 0 says to ALWAYS run the show-current branch command immediately before committing and to name the target branch. In a detached worktree that command prints an EMPTY string - measured in this groom - so the guardrail as written produces no name to check and a session following it literally either stops or waves it through. State the substitute check for the detached case and say what a correct answer looks like, so the guardrail keeps working rather than being skipped where it is needed most. Whatever substitute is chosen must distinguish "detached at the tip I intend to push onto" from "detached somewhere else", because those are the two outcomes the guardrail exists to separate. (c) THE WORKAROUND COMPOUNDS THE BLOCK, AND THAT IS STATED IN THE RECIPE. Pushing from the detached worktree advances the remote while the blocked checkout's own main ref stays where it was, so the shared tree finishes the session further behind than it started and the next session meets the same dirty file plus more commits behind it. Say plainly that the workaround unblocks the WORK and not the TREE, and that only the session holding the uncommitted file can clear it. Without this a reader reasonably concludes the recipe fixed the situation. (d) RENDERS FROM A WORKTREE ARE DECLARED SAFE AND THE FIX IS CITED. The session-close render is part of the ritual the recipe has to carry, and there is a live memory of renders written from a worktree landing in the MAIN checkout instead. J48 finished that fix. The recipe states that a default-paths board render run from a worktree writes worktree-local, cites J48 as the reason it is now true, and records the check - a render whose reported output paths all sit under the worktree root. Re-verify at build time rather than trusting this clause. (e) THE EVIDENCE IS CITED BY ARTIFACT, NOT SUMMARIZED. Two independent occurrences on 2026-08-28, hours apart, on the same file. Commit 2946de82 records the first in its own message body - a port-ledger session committed from a temp worktree because the desktop checkout was ff-blocked by a concurrent session's uncommitted ADR index edit. This groom hit the identical abort on the identical file and independently invented the identical workaround. Two sessions solving the same problem the same way on the same day with nothing written down between them IS the defect being fixed here, and the item says so. (f) OUT OF SCOPE, DELIBERATELY. Not in this item - any rule about how two sessions share one working tree, and any rule about how long an uncommitted draft may sit in it. Both are the user's call and are captured separately in the inbox rather than decided here. Also out of scope - the session-close CI check's own detached-HEAD blindness, which is U27's, already captured, and must not be re-solved here. (g) NO CODE, NO GUARD. This item edits procedure only and ships no behaviour change and no test. Say so, and say why - the failing step is a human ritual reading a document, and there is no point in the sequence where a guard could observe it.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-28 (desktop, weekly groom) from a defect observed DURING the groom rather than from an inbox entry, which is why it carries no Idea id of its own. The IDEAS.md inbox held nothing ungroomed at this run - the 2026-08-28 groom at 206bab66 had already consumed it - and this is the one thing the run itself turned up. Epic release-infrastructure / module docs / phase 8 follows J52 and J57, the two direct precedents - a verification or operating discipline learned from a specific incident and written into the guide so the next session inherits it instead of rediscovering it. Same epic, same module, same phase, and the same reason for sonnet over haiku - clause (a) requires actually running the sequence and clause (b) requires choosing a substitute check, neither of which is transcription. Clause (b) is the half worth the item on its own. The ff-block has a workaround and everybody finds it; what nobody notices is that the workaround silently disarms the ONE guardrail section 0 calls out in capitals, because the command it names returns an empty string instead of failing. A guardrail that returns nothing reads as a guardrail that passed. This item was itself written and committed through the recipe it describes, from a detached worktree at origin slash main, which is the closest thing to a pre-verification the shape allows.

K23Are ServiceNow KB articles linked at Deployment Module grain ASSERTED or DEFAULTED? -- the check that decides whether the kb_* family is a real pull candidate
taxonomyP9taskp2sonnet / main
seal-attribution

Acceptance: A recorded verdict in knowledge/upgrade-plans/servicenow-replica-evidence.md, where open questions 8 and 9 already sit, answering ONE question with evidence rather than plausibility: is the KB-article-to-Deployment-Module link ASSERTED by an author, or DEFAULTED by the form the way transactional records default their module? The check comes FIRST because the defect it looks for would hit KB articles identically to Changes and Incidents, and a graph built on a defaulted foreign key attaches documented fixes to the wrong deployment while looking perfectly populated. On the strength of that verdict, a RECOMMENDATION -- promote the kb_* family from ring 3 to a pull candidate, or leave it in ring 3 with the reason -- routed to the gate that rules the pull scope, never enacted here. NOTHING ACTIVATED: no source row written to config/source-registry.yaml, no loader, no edge. Any edge the recommendation implies is registered status: planned and goes through docs/RELATIONSHIP_GUIDE.md and the HITL gate. AMENDED 2026-08-19 by the export profile below. The ASSERTED-vs-DEFAULTED dichotomy is MOOT for the designed columns, because they are not populated at all -- an empty field is neither asserted nor defaulted. The live question the verdict must now answer is narrower and sharper: given that the only working SEAL link is at APPLICATION grain with 44% coverage and owning-not-subject semantics, does the kb_* family leave ring 3? The original question survives only for u_correlation_id itself: is that value authored per article, or defaulted from the article's owning base/content owner? The illustrative rows suggest the latter, which is exactly the defect this item was written to look for -- arriving on a different field than the one it was aimed at.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-11 from Idea-102's separate thread. The SME called KB articles at deployment grain "more meaningful", and a documented fix attached to the deployment that has the incident is squarely what a production-support knowledge graph is for -- which is why it earns an item rather than a line inside K22. Deliberately an ASSESSMENT and not an ingestion: ring 3 is where the family sits today, and the value of the item is that it is allowed to come back "leave it there" with evidence. EVIDENCE ARRIVED 2026-08-19 (SME screenshots; profiling ran on the SME's own machine against a dated CSV export of the KB view, NOT in this tree -- the file is not present here and these numbers could not be re-derived producer-side, J18). Shapes only per the publish boundary: the view's real db/schema, the SEAL id values, the KB article numbers, the content-owner SID and the support-group names all stay out of this repo. Registry grammar for the object is snow@[db].[schema].v_kb_knowledge. THE HEADLINE, and it lands on K23's premise rather than beside it: EVERY purpose-built SEAL/attribution column is 0-of-200 filled -- u_seal_id, u_do_you_have_seal_id, u_business_application, u_product_owner, u_assignment_group. The designed linkage does not exist in the export. Deployment grain in particular is unreachable: evidence-doc Q7 established that a deployment link shows as the composite app:deployment name (or the CI id), and every populated value here is a BARE app id with no deployment segment. So the SME's "KB articles at deployment grain" premise is not merely unconfirmed -- this export cannot express it. WHAT DOES CARRY A LINK: u_correlation_id, 88 of 200 (44%), 77 distinct values, all numeric and 4-6 digits, i.e. SEAL-shaped at APPLICATION grain. 112 of 200 (56%) have no SEAL link on any field. Secondary signals, none of them a substitute: the KB base field is 100% filled with 15 distinct values (a base grouping, at best a coarse owning-domain proxy, and the top 3 hold 131 of 200); u_content_owner 48% as free text (person / SID / group, so it reaches an app only indirectly via the support group); ownership_group 4.5%. THE CAVEAT THAT DECIDES THE VERDICT: u_correlation_id looks like the OWNING app's SEAL, not the article's SUBJECT SEAL. Two sampled rows cite a different SEAL inside the article title than the one in u_correlation_id. If that generalises, then even the 44% is answering "who owns this article" rather than "what is this article about" -- and an edge built on it would attach documented fixes to the wrong application while looking well populated, which is the K23 defect exactly, one grain up from where the item expected it. NOT SETTLED, and the write-up must say so: whether the 200-article export is the whole KB or a projection (the same completeness doubt as evidence-doc Q9, one level down), and whether the owning-vs-subject reading holds beyond the two sampled rows. A subject-precise mapping would require parsing the SEAL out of the article title or body, which is a different and much weaker capture than a structured foreign key. DIRECTION OF TRAVEL: this evidence points at "leave the kb_* family in ring 3, with the reason recorded" rather than at promotion. The item is NOT closed by it -- the acceptance puts the verdict in knowledge/upgrade-plans/servicenow-replica-evidence.md beside Q8/Q9. VERDICT RECORDED 2026-08-19 as evidence-doc section 11 -- 11.1 why the ASSERTED-vs-DEFAULTED question dissolved, 11.2 what the export does carry, 11.3 the recommendation, 11.4 the surviving use case. Section 7.4's NOT-TAKEN row now points at it, so a reader of the pull scope meets the ruling rather than the deferral. RECOMMENDATION: leave the kb_* family OUT as an attribution source, with the REASON recorded rather than the deferral -- routed to the gate that rules pull scope, not enacted here. Nothing activated: no registry row, no loader, no edge. K23 STAYS OPEN AND ITS SCOPE HAS MOVED (user direction 2026-08-19). The attribution question is answered; what remains is the named use case that keeps the family alive. THE REMEDIATION MODULE searches the existing KB for articles covering the same defect, DOWNLOADS them for reference and archiving, and only then authors a new article. That consumer is untouched by everything the profile found: it wants the article as a DOCUMENT to find, read, cite and retain, not as a node to attach to an application, and the KB SQL that already exists matches on short_description with a body-text fallback while ignoring the SEAL columns entirely. So the 0-of-200 finding does not reach it, the owning-vs-subject caveat does not reach it, and 44% coverage stops being a blocker because the denominator is articles that MATCH THE DEFECT, not articles that carry a key. WHAT THIS ITEM NOW OWES, per section 11.4, none of it settled: the READ PATH (the Snowflake view vs the ServiceNow API vs an offline export -- different freshness and permission consequences); WHERE A DOWNLOADED ARTICLE LANDS, which is a publish-boundary question with a ready answer -- a KB body is company prose, so it belongs in the out-of-repo data root as a DECLARED landing zone (drydocs_core/landing_zones.py) rather than an ad-hoc download directory; whether the archived copy is a CITATION (a convenience) or a SOURCE a fix package quotes (evidence, carrying a retention obligation -- the different ruling, and the one with consequences); and the DUPLICATE TEST, since "search before authoring" implies a bar for "already covered" that a LIKE pattern over short_description is a weak instrument for. MODULE NOTE: the work has moved out of taxonomy and into drydocs-remediation (detect -> transform -> prove -> Jira, ADR 0002-B). Left at module: taxonomy for now because re-homing an item is a groom decision, not a side effect of recording a verdict -- flagged here so the next groom moves it deliberately. QUESTION 3 RULED 2026-08-19 (SME) -- recorded as evidence-doc section 11.5. The articles expected back are RUNBOOKS, FOUND BY CONTROL-M FOLDER, which is what the existing KB SQL already does: it builds its LIKE patterns from the folder/job name. A batch EXTRACTS the runbook, saves it to the fix Jira as a BASELINE, REPLACES it, and captures ACCURACY and STALENESS metrics to gauge cleanup effort and progress. So the archive is a SOURCE, not a citation -- three independent reasons, any one sufficient: it is the before-half of a before/after pair; the original is REPLACED, so the archived copy becomes the only surviving record of what the runbook said; and the metrics are measured against it, so a score that cannot be re-derived from the artifact it scored is an assertion rather than a measurement. THE RETENTION OBLIGATION IS STRONGER THAN THE EMAIL-EXTRACT PRECEDENT. That pair is a system of record because the upstream purges on a 6-18 month cycle; here WE overwrite the upstream ourselves, deliberately, as the last step of the fix. Two ordering rules follow: CAPTURE BEFORE REPLACE, treating a failed capture as a failed step (a batch that replaces a runbook it did not archive has destroyed its own baseline), and the archived copy is IMMUTABLE once written. Question 2 is decided by this rather than open beside it: the archive belongs in the out-of-repo data root as a DECLARED landing zone (drop_dir_base: data_root, guarded by tests/unit/test_landing_zones.py) -- a baseline a port-time git clean can reach is a baseline that disappears without a log. THE METRICS NEED DEFINITION AND ONE IS NEARLY FREE. The cheap reading of staleness is the one the SME already rejected -- Q11's problem statement is that stale versions are distinguishable only BY DATE. A measured staleness is available because G68 profiles a folder set into four where-used censuses (shape, identity/FIDs/run-as/SEAL, variables, contacts), which is a ground truth for the same folder the runbook documents: ACCURACY = of the entities a runbook names, how many still exist and still mean what it says; STALENESS = the drift between the runbook's picture and G68's current one. That also gives cleanup a DENOMINATOR, which is exactly G93's defect on the documentation axis -- so it should ride G93's run-log contract, not grow a second reporting path. HANDS TO Q11, AND SOMEONE SHOULD DECIDE WHETHER TO AMEND THAT PROMPT: the document-supersession gate's clause C asks who ASSERTS supersession -- a capture pipeline OBSERVING a replacement, or an SME RULING two captures are versions of one thing. Remediation is neither: it PERFORMS the replacement, so it does not infer supersession, it KNOWS it, and can name the fix id as the basis. That is the most reliable assertion class the edge will get, and clause C would be ruled without it unless the prompt is amended before signing. NOT amended here -- Q11 is done and its prompt is the deliverable, so touching it is a decision, not a side effect. HANDS TO G68: a candidate FIFTH census -- documentation, i.e. which folders in the set have a runbook, which do not, and how each scores. Proposed to that item, not assumed. STILL OPEN AFTER THIS RULING: the scoring rules (entity existence is tractable, "still means what it says" is a judgement -- rule the tractable subset and say the rest is unscored rather than inventing a similarity number); whether a folder with NO runbook at all is a finding, which is a GAP report rather than a staleness one and is arguably the more valuable output; and the section 11.4 question 4 duplicate/coverage bar, now sharper because a false negative in the LIKE search silently becomes "this folder has no runbook" in that same gap report.

GATED BEHIND the fix-diff surface existing (it reviews a diff; without one it reviews nothing). Precedents: the Q&A console for the answer surface; docmeta for citation handling.

O44Ownership reconciliation ALLUVIAL diagram (a Sankey variant): four ordered columns — employee hierarchy | SEAL/TOM contacts | ServiceNow queues + technicians | PAT structure — with ribbons where an entity appears in both, and a terminating ribbon where it does not
drydocs-webP12requirementp2sonnet / main
web-console
depends on: G35

Acceptance: THE DIAGRAM TYPE IS NAMED, and it is not decoration: this is an ALLUVIAL diagram — the Sankey family variant for CATEGORICAL data across several ordered dimensions, where the same entities are re-partitioned column by column and ribbons carry membership from one partition to the next. (SME 2026-08-05, correcting this item's first draft, which described the shape and never named it.) Sankey is the family; alluvial is the member, and the distinction decides the data contract — a general Sankey moves a QUANTITY between distinct nodes, an alluvial moves the SAME ENTITIES between categorizations. Build to the alluvial contract: nodes = (column, category), links = (source category, target category, the entity set that is in both). A console pane rendering FOUR ordered columns over the same applications and people, each column a different system's view of who owns what, with a ribbon drawn ONLY where the entity is actually present in both adjacent columns' lists (the SME framing). THE TERMINATING RIBBON IS THE PRODUCT. An entity that appears in one column and not the next does not fade out quietly — a flow that stops IS the finding, and it must be visually distinct from a flow that continues. That is what makes this the reconciliation surface for G35 §D: a SEAL contact with no ServiceNow counterpart is a roster disagreement made legible, and a diagram that only draws matches would hide precisely the case it exists for. (1) EMPLOYEE HIERARCHY, filterable by manager. (2) SEAL/TOM CONTACTS, filterable by SEAL id, LOB, product line, product and contact role. (3) SERVICENOW: the queues/assignment groups matching the applications in column 1's list, showing their technician roles. (4) PAT STRUCTURE with its SEALs. SHIP IN PHASES, and the phase boundary is a DATA boundary, not a UI one — columns 2 and 4 are buildable today, columns 1 and 3 are not (see notes). Phase 1 acceptance is columns 2+4 with the cross-column relationship drawn and the two missing columns shown as EXPLICITLY EMPTY WITH A REASON, never omitted: a four-column pane silently rendering two columns is the failure this acceptance exists to prevent. Every column names its source system and the freshness of its load. Full suite green.

Notes: SME direction 2026-08-05, in-chat during the G35 gate draft. This is the surface where G35 §D's roster disagreement becomes VISIBLE rather than inferred — §D3 proposes recording which surface an attribution came from, and this pane is what consumes it, which is why it depends_on G35 rather than merely citing it. DATA STATE, measured 2026-08-05 (this is the whole reason it ships in phases): * COLUMN 2 (SEAL/TOM) — EXISTS. Attribution/TOMRole/Employee load today, and every requested filter is backed by a real node: CatalogLOB, ProductLine, Product, BusinessApplication, and the contact role itself. The K11 steward cascade already implements Product Line -> Product -> Business Application, so the filter chain is a reuse, not a build. * COLUMN 4 (PAT) — EXISTS. Product/AreaProduct/DevTeam load via pat_product_mapping.cypher + area_products.cypher, and pat:people-report carries team-scoped seal_ids. Caveat recorded at C17: the people report projects Sponsoring Product Line as a NAME ONLY, so that grain stays unmodelled and the column cannot filter on it. * COLUMN 1 (EMPLOYEE HIERARCHY) — DOES NOT EXIST. :Employee is a node class (prov:Agent) with NO Employee-to-Employee edge anywhere in the relationship vocabulary: no REPORTS_TO, no manager edge, no source feeding one, and no backlog item that would create one. The manager filter is the column's whole point and there is nothing to filter on. G35 §B7 defers hierarchy placement to "a later pass" on SME direction; this item is the first consumer that makes the missing owner concrete. * COLUMN 3 (SERVICENOW) — NOT INGESTED. snow:cmdb-ci-classes is registered (Q4 ruling, 2026-07-31) but confirmed: false, adapter: ~, and it is a header-only capture of CMDB CLASSES — not queues, not assignment groups, not people. The "SEAL technician roles" the SME describes appear in the repo only as prose: the runbook skill's template-spec cites AO/RE Snow queues with a Technician role, and internal/remediation names a SNOW technician group + CTASK. That is enough to know the concept is real and not enough to build a column. RIBBON WEIGHT IS AN OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, flagged rather than assumed: in a Sankey the ribbon THICKNESS encodes a quantity, and this diagram has more than one candidate — count of people, count of applications, or unweighted equal-width membership bands. Pick before building; retrofitting a weight changes the layout engine's input, not just a style. NO LIBRARY IN THE STACK DOES THIS. web/package.json carries @xyflow/react (node-and-edge graphs, not flows) and d3-force (force layout). An alluvial needs d3-sankey or a hand-rolled SVG with a crossing-minimisation pass — readable column ordering is most of the work in this diagram, and it is the part a naive implementation gets wrong. A new dependency also lands in the software registry, which is the third-party ledger, so it is a registration as well as an install. NOT SPLIT INTO SEPARATE ITEMS on purpose: the two missing columns are SOURCE questions (does DryDocs ingest the HR hierarchy and the SNOW queue export, producer-side or company-side?) and that is a user decision, not an agent's. Both are inboxed against this item rather than groomed into speculative work. If the answer is company-side for either, this item's phase 1 IS its final scope and the acceptance says so.

O58A console surface for docs-verify: which declared corpora are actually loaded and where - the answer a single-database QuerySpec cannot give

Acceptance: A console surface answers "which declared doc corpora are actually loaded, and in which database" with the same six states drydocs/docs_verify.py computes — loaded | missing | stale | wrong-db | unshaped | db-absent — and renders wrong-db as the alarm the CLI's non-zero exit means. THE TRANSPORT IS THIS ITEM'S REAL CONTENT, and it must be chosen and written down, not defaulted: the reconciliation is inherently MULTI-database (it sweeps drydocs, dddocs and ddcontext precisely so a corpus sitting in a database it did not declare is visible, a result unobtainable from any single one of them), while a registered QuerySpec carries exactly one `database:` field by construction and SPEC_DATABASES does not even admit dddocs — so this cannot be a plain spec-backed page. The item names ONE of: (a) a server-side sweep endpoint in drydocs_api reusing docs_verify.verify(), whose `run(database, cypher, params)` is already its only I/O seam, making the reuse exact; (b) N registered specs, one per swept database, joined client-side with the join rule written down; or (c) a generated JSON artifact refreshed by the session ritual, the /software precedent. Whichever is chosen, the commit body records the choice AND its cost against ADR 0005 — option (a) adds a non-spec read path to an API whose standing rule is that /raw-cypher is the only interactive Cypher surface, and that is a boundary change, not a detail. Two things are never invented: a database that was not queried renders "not queried", never 0 (the O56 honesty rule); and a guard asserts the surface's state set against docs_verify.py's constants, so a seventh status cannot appear in the CLI and silently miss the page.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-17 (targeted groom -- the UI / docs/design/ui-exploration inbox entries only) from Idea-123: the SME supplied a real captured example (screenshot + transcription machine-local at internal-local/ui-examples/, real SEAL ids/hosts/repo URLs -- never committed). This is the concrete output target for the Ask route: report form of the same job -> pipeline -> asset chain O60 draws as a swimlane diagram -- the pair is deliberate, one chain, two presentations. module drydocs-web with the QuerySpec half explicitly in scope the way other O-series frames bind specs; if the spec grows past a straightforward reviewed traversal, splitting a drydocs-api item out is the builder's call to record. Whether this report also becomes an Ask-agent tool answer (the Idea-125 named-verbs direction) is NOT decided here -- this item renders the report; the agent-tool question stays in the inbox. OBSERVED 2026-08-21 (desktop, live Ask session `ask-jdoe4821-wjtacr8x`) — a real user ran this item's use case against the current surface, so the shape is no longer only the SME's captured example. The user asked for a file name, `OS_Job_parameters.htm`, and the answer was correct: document `controlm-os-job-parameters`, 16 chunks, GROUNDED/External. HOW it was correct is the finding worth pinning to this item: the router chose registered spec `docs.documents.v1`, whose Cypher applies NO search filter — it lists every `:Document` with a chunk count — and the answer LLM picked the match out of 27 rows by title similarity. So the retrieval was a full-corpus scan narrowed by the model, not a search, and `d.source_page` was never read even though the user named that property. That works at 27 documents and degrades as the corpus grows, which is a direct argument for this item's clause that the traversal binds via a REVIEWED read-only spec: the spec has to do the filtering, or the honest-absence clause cannot mean anything either (a full listing can never render "not found via <spec>"). No spec in `drydocs_api/query_specs.py` currently accepts a search term — `docs.chunks.v1` returns headings without text and takes no filter — so a term-accepting doc/file-name spec is a real prerequisite, not an assumed one. Two sibling runs in the same session missed entirely, both answering "not ingested" while the corpus held the document; that evidence and the per-hop reasoning are recorded on R18, the trace item, rather than duplicated here.

O63Service reachability, surfaced twice from one probe: Ask diagnoses its own failure instead of printing a bare "Failed to fetch", and the admin page carries a service-status strip at the top
drydocs-webP12taskp2sonnet / main
web-console

Acceptance: When an Ask request fails, the surface runs a STAGED self-diagnosis in place of the single red line it shows today, in this order: (a) The originating error renders FIRST and VERBATIM — "Failed to fetch" stays "Failed to fetch". It is never re-worded, prefixed or "friendlied": that exact string is what the user will paste into a search or a support ticket, and the browser's own wording is the honest report of what the browser saw. (b) A `checking…` state appears immediately and is visibly distinct from both success and failure, so a slow probe never looks like a verdict. (c) The console pings the ADK agent server (VITE_ADK_URL, default http://localhost:8000 — `GET /list-apps` is the cheapest liveness call and needs no session) and renders RED or GREEN. Green additionally asserts the `graph_qa` app is in the returned list: a server that is up but does not serve this agent is not a green for this page's purpose. (d) If the transport is green, the NEXT stage's error is surfaced AS-IS — the worked example is `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set (agents/.env)`, which is `providers.ProviderConfigError` text raised server-side. Verbatim matters twice here: the string names the exact key AND the exact file to put it in, and any paraphrase loses one or both. (e) The ladder ends with a `contact DryDocs support` hand-off once the checks stop being self-serviceable. (f) THE ADMIN PAGE CARRIES A SERVICE-STATUS STRIP AT THE TOP, driven by the SAME probe the ladder uses — one implementation, two surfaces. It reports each service the console depends on: drydocs-api (:8001), the graph behind it (reachable + which database), the ADK agent server (:8000, green only when `graph_qa` is in `/list-apps`), and whether the agent's provider is configured. Ask's ladder is the reactive view — it runs because something already failed — and the strip is the standing one, answering "is anything missing?" before a question is asked rather than after. ON DEMAND AND TIMESTAMPED, NOT A LIVE MONITOR. DryDocs is deliberately not a real-time system, and the strip must not imply otherwise: it checks when the page loads and when a refresh control is pressed, shows `checked HH:MM` beside the verdict, and never polls on a timer. A stale-but-dated verdict is honest; a green dot that silently stopped updating is the failure this repo keeps refusing elsewhere. This is the same reason the console renders committed artifacts rather than live-deriving them. THREE RULES THE LADDER MUST NOT BREAK: 1. NEVER INVENT A GREEN. A probe that could not run renders "not checked", never green and never 0 — the O56 honesty rule, applied to liveness instead of counts. 2. The two failures are DIFFERENT and must not collapse into one message: nothing listening on :8000 (transport down — the agent service was never started) versus the service up and its provider misconfigured. Both printed "the Ask page is broken" before this item; only the second is fixable by editing a file. 3. NO SECRET EVER REACHES THE PAGE. The diagnosis reports that a key is unset — never its value, length, prefix or a masked form of it. ADR 0005's reason for VITE_NEO4J_PASSWORD applies to any value a bundle could inline. A test covers the ladder's STATE MACHINE (error -> checking -> probe verdict -> next error -> hand-off) rather than its copy, and the ui-tests.yaml TS-ASK suite — declared but empty today — gains its first cases from whatever is actually watched working. The strip is covered by the same probe's tests plus a case asserting it renders "not checked" rather than a verdict before its first run.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-20 from a live failure in the ui-workstream session, and the sequence in the acceptance is the debugging path a human actually walked, turned into the page's own behaviour. WHAT HAPPENED, because it is the whole argument for the item: the console came up with Neo4j, the API and Vite all green, every other view live against the graph. Ask returned "Failed to fetch" and nothing else. The cause was a FOURTH service nobody had started — the ADK agent server (`cd agents && adk api_server --allow_origins http://localhost:5173`), which only the Ask spoke talks to; every other page goes through drydocs-api. Starting it moved the failure to "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set (agents/.env)" — a completely different problem with a completely different fix, reached only by reading source and grepping .env files. "Failed to fetch" is the browser's generic network-error text. It is TRUE and nearly useless: it cannot distinguish a service that was never started from a crashed one, a CORS rejection, or a wrong VITE_ADK_URL. The console already knows which URL it dialled and can simply ask — which is what turns a dead end into a two-line answer. THE ADMIN STRIP (clause f) was added 2026-08-20 on the user's direction, with the reason stated as a property of the project rather than a preference: "the DryDocs project itself is not meant to be realtime intentionally", so the console needs service checks with status at the top of the admin page. That framing is what keeps the strip from drifting into a health dashboard — the requirement is an ANSWERABLE question ("is anything missing right now?"), not continuous monitoring, and the timestamp is what makes the difference visible to the reader. Scoped onto this item rather than a new one because it is the same probe: building it twice is how the two surfaces would end up disagreeing about what "green" means. DELIBERATELY NOT SPECIFIED: whether the ladder renders inline in the answer pane or in a collapsible diagnostics panel, and whether it re-runs on demand or once per failure. Both are page design and belong with the builder. Same for the strip's placement within AdminConfigRoute — "at the top" is the requirement, the exact chrome is not. ONE THING TO RULE WHEN BUILDING, not at the groom: `contact DryDocs support` is a placeholder string for the producer console, where "support" is the person reading the screen. If it should resolve to a real destination it becomes config (the VITE_RUNTIME_VIEW_URL_TEMPLATE precedent — unset means no affordance renders), and a company hostname is never committed here. Ties to Idea-141 (should agents/ stop carrying its own venv) without depending on it: that entry argues the service is easy to forget because it is installed differently from everything else. This item makes forgetting it cheap to diagnose rather than preventing the forgetting. NOT gate-bound: nothing here touches edge semantics, the ontology, or a graph write. The page stays read-only (O20).

O68The admin page should show the log estate: directory, path, size and capacity per kind — and must not render debug-tier Cypher until that display is reviewed
drydocs-webP12taskp2sonnet / main
web-console
depends on: G111

Acceptance: (a) THE PANEL. The admin configuration page (O12) gains a log-estate panel: per declared kind and per declared zone, the directory, the resolved path, the file count, the total size, and the declared retention. It is a PANEL on that existing surface, not a new page — the SME placed it there rather than in a new epic. (b) THE DATA MOSTLY EXISTS, SO MOST OF THIS IS WIRING. G109 shipped a zone inventory returning present/absent plus a file count per declared zone, and the landing-zones command already emits manual and declared zones as one document with path, mode, base, in-repo, exists, file count and empty. The panel needs a read endpoint over that, not new collection. The ONE genuinely missing field is capacity — the inventory counts files and does not sum bytes — so a total-bytes value is added beside the count in CORE, not computed in the API and not in the browser. (c) THE DEBUG TIER IS REPORTED, NEVER RENDERED. ADR 0014 clause 6 as ruled splits the lean, longer-retention API log from a verbose short-retention debug log that carries Cypher text and request detail. CAPTURING that text is ruled; SURFACING it in a console is NOT, and they are different risks — a short-lived file on an operator's disk versus a rendered page. This panel may report the debug kind's SIZE and RETENTION like any other kind and MUST NOT render its contents. Anything that would display it is blocked on the SME review, which is a separate ruling and not this item's to make. (d) IT DOES NOT SHIP A KNOWN-WRONG ROW. G111 is a hard dependency, not a courtesy: today the run-logs zone resolves to the default whenever the log-directory variable is set, so a panel built before that fix would confidently show the wrong directory for exactly the kind the SME most wants to see. (e) WHY A PANEL AND NOT JUST THE CLI, stated in the panel's own copy or its PR note: the command exists so "my extracts are gone" is a one-command answer, and the person most likely to ask is on a machine where the CLI is not the habitual surface. Post-retention it answers the same question for logs — days declared against days actually on disk.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-26 from Idea-172 (SME direction 2026-08-25, given alongside the ADR 0014 retention rulings). Epic O and the admin page are the SME's own placement. Module `drydocs-web` recorded as a choice: the item spans three modules — the total-bytes field is core, the read endpoint is api, the panel is web — and it is filed against the surface the SME asked for. Whoever takes it should keep the core slice in core (clause b) rather than letting a byte sum drift into the API layer, which is the seam the module boundary exists to protect. The Cypher-display question in clause (c) is an SME review, parked as a question in the inbox at this groom and named in the groom report; the item is complete without it and stays blocked on it for that one behaviour only. p2/sonnet: the data exists, the acceptance names the one new field, and the single hard rule (no debug content) is stated in the negative so it is testable.

O69NVL graph canvas: first-party Neo4j visualization components over QuerySpec results — the console gets a real graph surface, fed only through the read API
drydocs-webP12taskp1sonnet / main
web-console

Acceptance: Written as ORDERED STEPS for the UI worktree session (branch off main, screenshots in the PR note, session ritual per CLAUDE.md §0). (1) DEPENDENCY + LICENSE RECORD. Add @neo4j-nvl/base and @neo4j-nvl/react to web/. NVL enters config/taxonomy/software-registry.yaml as a product of the existing Neo4j vendor row before the first import lands. The license was RULED acceptable at this groom (SME 2026-08-27, in-chat); the step that remains is mechanical: record the license identifier the installed package actually declares in the registry row, so the ruling and the artifact agree on the record. A mismatch with the ruling's basis is a stop-and-report, not a silent proceed. (2) THE DATA SEAM — API RESULTS IN, NEVER BOLT. One mapper module (web/src/lib/nvl-mapping.ts or equivalent): QuerySpec result rows -> NVL nodes/relationships. A pre-build survey found a HARD dependency the item never recorded. "Rescrape is a QUEUED refresh artifact — AUTO-RUNNABLE for SYNTHESIZED corpora" needs something that can actually refetch, and the producer has NO fetcher: the web + filedrop connectors are Q6's deliverable ("Port A: bkup scrapers -> the producer docmeta component"), Q6 is todo and parked on physical media confirmed absent on both machines, and its web connector is additionally gated on Q12's page-count refusal. Building the queue anyway would ship a queue nothing can drain and an "auto-runnable" path that cannot run — worse than not building it, because the surface would claim a capability that does not exist. Q6 therefore added to depends_on. What is NOT blocked, and why a SPLIT is the obvious alternative for the user to rule rather than for an agent to assume: clauses (a) the :Document freshness fields + status lifecycle, (b) staleness flagging on citations, and (d) full re-chunk on a changed sha are all buildable today against the existing loaders — only the auto-run rescrape and the Ask spoke's round-trip need the fetcher. Splitting freshness-now from rescrape-later would unblock roughly three quarters of this item. One further gap the survey turned up, cheap to fix inside whichever shape wins: `agents/graph_qa/pipeline.py` hardcodes `"chunks": 0` in two places with the comment "doc-chunk retrieval arrives with R7 corpora wiring", so the agent currently has no Document-sourced SourceRecord at all. (b) THE DOCTRINE IS IN THE CONTRACT, not only in prose: an empty result set is not evidence of absence when the causes say the walk could not see. (d) CONSUMERS RE-READ ONE FIELD: the Ask spoke (R5) and any exported spec render the label as given rather than inventing their own wording for it. R18Ask debug trace: opt-in verbose decision log correlated to run_id and session_id
drydocs-agentsP15requirementp1sonnet / main
agentic-qa
depends on: R3 R5

Acceptance: (a) An explicit opt-in `--debug` / `--verbose` runtime option (or the equivalent documented service setting for the ADK server) enables an append-only diagnostic trace for one Ask run, correlated on every record by the existing `run_id` and `session_id`. (b) The trace captures the observable decision path: normalized question, router outcome and candidate/spec rationale, schema/vocabulary inputs selected for text2cypher, generated Cypher, validation/fix attempts and errors, executed row counts, answer inputs, and final envelope status/timing. It must not capture hidden chain-of-thought or provider secrets. (c) Default behavior remains the current minimal telemetry contract; debug is off unless explicitly enabled, and sensitive question/answer content follows the existing local-log classification and retention rules. (d) An admin can retrieve or download the trace by run_id/session_id and distinguish one question from concurrent sessions; the Ask UI links the visible run id to the trace when debug is enabled. Unit tests cover correlation, disabled-by-default behavior, redaction, and a full router -> query -> answer trace.

Notes: Follow-on to R3, which is DONE and already writes per-call JSONL plus the :AgentRun summary, and R5, which exposes the safe per-step Cypher in the Ask UI. This item fills the current gap between those surfaces and the richer diagnostic evidence needed to explain routing and generated-query decisions. "Thinking" means an auditable decision trace, not unrestricted model chain-of-thought. VERIFIED 2026-08-21 (desktop, live Ask session `ask-jdoe4821-wjtacr8x`, three runs, `qa.graph_qa.20260821.jsonl` + `agents/graph_qa/.adk/session.db`) — the gap this item names is REAL and is larger than a logging change. Read at the code, not inferred. WHAT EACH HOP KEEPS TODAY, transcribed as observed: - router — kept: `spec_id` and `ms` on the StepRecord, nothing else. Dropped: the prompt, and the ENTIRE raw reply. In `_route()` (agents/graph_qa/pipeline.py, the `raw = self._llm(...)` call) the reply is a local, handed to `_extract_json`, reduced to `spec_id` + `params`, and lost when the function returns. `StepRecord` (agents/graph_qa/envelope.py) has no field that could hold it. - text2cypher — kept: the generated `cypher` string, plus `database`, `rows`, `truncated`, `fix_retries`, `error`. Dropped: the schema/vocabulary prompt built by `build_schema_prompt`, and any prose the model wrapped around the JSON. The kept Cypher is the ONE genuinely diagnostic intermediate that exists today. - answer — kept: `ms` on the step; the output text lands in `envelope.answer`. Dropped: the system prompt and the rows JSON it reasoned over. WHY, and this is the part that changes the build: there are TWO independent causes, and neither is fixed by writing more log lines. 1. No rationale is ever GENERATED. `ROUTER_SYSTEM` closes with a JSON-only instruction whose object has exactly two keys, `spec_id` and `params` — there is no `reason` field, so the model is never asked to explain the choice. The telemetry confirms nothing was emitted and suppressed: router completion tokens were 17, 17 and 30 across the three runs, which is the size of those JSON literals alone. Clause (b) asks for "router outcome and candidate/spec rationale"; the outcome half is already recorded, the rationale half requires a CONTRACT CHANGE to the router prompt plus a `StepRecord` field, not a capture change. 2. Nothing below the pipeline could carry it either. `LiteLlmProvider.complete` (agents/graph_qa/providers.py) reads only `response.choices[0].message.content`, passes no thinking parameter, and runs at temperature 0 — so a provider-side reasoning block would be discarded before the pipeline ever saw it. This is consistent with the notes above: the item wants an auditable decision trace, and clause (b) fences off hidden chain-of-thought. SINK BOUNDARY, pinning clause (c) to a specific place: full prompt and reply text belongs in the DRYDOCS_LOGDIR ledger that R3 already owns, NOT in the envelope. `Envelope` deliberately reduces question text and caller identity to sha256-plus-length so neither is persisted in a payload or in-graph, while R3's run line is already the sanctioned home for full question text. A trace that widened the envelope would cross a boundary this repo drew on purpose. WHAT THE THREE RUNS SHOWED, as the worked example a builder can test against: same session, same user, one subject — BMC Control-M OS job parameters. Run 1 routed to text2cypher and generated `(d:Document)-[:HAS_CHUNK]->(c:Chunk)` filtered on `d.name`; the corpus edge is `(:Chunk)-[:PART_OF]->(:Document)` and `Document` carries `doc_id`/`title`/`source_page`, so two independent defects each produced 0 rows. Run 2 routed to text2cypher and read the same words as an OPERATIONAL question, generating a valid `ControlMFolder`/`ControlMJob` traversal on `task_type` — 0 rows, right schema, wrong domain. Run 3 named a graph property in the question, routed to spec `docs.documents.v1`, and found the document — `controlm-os-job-parameters`, 16 chunks, GROUNDED/External. So the corpus held the answer the whole time and two of three runs told the user it was not ingested. Today a reviewer can reconstruct WHAT ran from the kept Cypher but nothing says WHY the router read the same subject three different ways, which is precisely the evidence this item exists to produce. TIES: O62 is the search-side sibling — run 3 is a real user performing its file-name search use case, and it is worth noting there that `docs.documents.v1` applies no search filter at all (it lists every Document and the answer LLM picked the match out of 27 rows by title similarity), so the retrieval was approximate even though the answer was right. R13 concerns growth of the same `.adk/session.db` this evidence was read from, and R23 (groomed 2026-08-22 from Idea-155) is the cleartext credential in that same store — cited here as "Idea-151" when this note was written, which is the BRANCH-side number for that report; on `main` Idea-151 is the unrelated stale-render entry that became Y5.

R19Ask clarification loop for unresolved acronyms and graph-label intent
drydocs-agentsP15requirementp1sonnet / main
agentic-qa
depends on: R2 R5

Acceptance: (a) When the initial question contains an acronym, label, or domain term that does not resolve to a registered QuerySpec, active vocabulary row, live label/property, or approved acronym sense, the agent does not silently choose a near match; it returns a structured clarification request with the unresolved term, the detected candidate senses/labels, and one or more concise choices. (b) The Ask UI renders the clarification as an actionable question, preserves the pending question/session, and submits the user's selection or free-text clarification as the next turn. A confirmed clarification is visible in the trace and is used for the subsequent router/text2cypher decision. (c) If the user declines or no clarification is possible, the answer states the ambiguity and does not present a zero-row near-match as a definitive answer. Existing clear questions remain single-pass and unchanged. (d) Tests cover unknown acronym, ambiguous label with multiple candidates, user selection, cancellation, session persistence, and the no-clarification regression path.

Notes: Requested as a companion to R18 after the Tower/TOMRole mismatch: the Explorer's synthesized Tower concept was silently mapped to the real TOMRole label. This is a disambiguation contract, not permission for the agent to invent ontology or relationship meanings; unresolved meaning still routes to the SME/HITL path.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-18 from a module-ownership read of drydocs/. drydocs-plan, drydocs-docgen and drydocs-port are DECLARED in `modules:` and enforced as logical groups by test_module_boundary.py, but they are the only components with no physical directory — every other one was extracted (drydocs_api, drydocs_lineage, drydocs_deepdoc, drydocs_docmeta, drydocs_remediation). G2 extracted core and stopped, so drydocs/ still carries five components' worth of loose modules and the boundary test compensates with a curated list of module names. NOT into drydocs_core, and the reason is what core is FOR: models, adapters, neo4j lifecycle, config/precedence/source_registry, ontology, schema DDL, orchestration — the DOMAIN core, whose value is that importing it carries no opinion about presentation. An HTML renderer and a headless-Chromium shell-out would spend exactly that guarantee. Sibling packages follow the precedent every other component already set. Cheap by construction: design_doc and doc_pdf are pure stdlib; doc_outline and plan_board are yaml plus one drydocs_core import; plan_roadmap and plan_ideas import siblings. No graph access, no loader coupling, no component imports. Dependency direction after the move is drydocs_plan -> drydocs_docgen -> stdlib/core: one edge, pointing the right way. The sweep is ~11 tracked importers, not S9's 31 — but score the sweep before committing to an effort number, which is the lesson S9 recorded the hard way. depends_on S8 so cli.py is a thin composition root with per-domain sub-apps BEFORE the files move; the other order makes S8 split a CLI across three packages instead of one. Not a hard blocker on correctness — if S8 stalls, this can be re-scored and run first. port_preflight rides along ON PURPOSE: identical position (own group, own declared component, stdlib + subprocess + one repo_paths import), and extracting two of the three guarantees a repeat visit. Cut it from scope only if the SME rules drydocs-port folds into another component. S7 is what makes this a rename rather than a preference: module names name COMPONENTS, directories name CODE ROOTS, and they must coincide for first-party Python packages precisely because test_module_boundary.py classifies by package root. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: one drydocs_docs/ package holding all three groups. Fewer top-level entries, but it invents a fourth component name that the ledgers, runbooks, guards and backlog `modules:` list do not know, so every one of them would need updating for no structural gain. Follow the declared components.

U23Nothing joins a loader to the Cypher it executes — draft the gate rider for a loader-to-cypher-file edge, the .cypher nodes that carry zero edges

Acceptance: A gate rider is DRAFTED and nothing else. Drafting decides nothing (the G27 / W1 / N10 / G95 precedent): no vocabulary entry leaves `planned`, no edge is written, and if the gate does not sit, the drafted rider IS the deliverable. VIA THE GATE is the whole point -- a new relationship type is an ontology decision under CLAUDE.md section 6, never an import convenience. It carries four things. (a) THE FACT, RE-MEASURED rather than copied from the 2026-08-02 note that raised it: `drydocs/loaders/` holds .py loaders, their .cypher files and their .sql side by side; the .cypher files are :CodeModule nodes with NO edges at all, while each loader names its Cypher as a literal path in Python (the CYPHER_DIR / "<name>.cypher" idiom). The prompt states the current counts and the date it counted them. (b) THE EDGE QUESTION, put as a question: what does the edge MEAN -- "executes", "reads as a resource", something narrower -- and does the .sql beside it carry the same edge or a different one? Direction, cardinality, and whether one label with a role property beats two labels (the documented RUNS_ON-overload risk is the standing worked example on this side). (c) THE EMITTER, because the edge has nowhere to come from today: the depgraph scanner does not emit it, so the prompt says where it would -- a static read of the CYPHER_DIR literal, in the instrument (the sibling repo, which means an expected_commit bump) or in the loader that reads the snapshot -- and what each costs. This is the clause that stops the rider being signed with no path to a first row. (d) WHAT IT UNLOCKS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT, stated plainly so the item is never judged against a promise it did not make: gate `self-documentation-code-graph` section H5 already records that :CodeModule to the OPERATIONAL graph -- "which module loads this Control-M job" -- is NOT delivered by that gate and needs a second item, precisely because the module-to-label mapping lives in the loaders' Cypher rather than in their imports. A loader-to-cypher edge is the FIRST half of that join and not the join; the prompt says so.

The emitter change the rider scopes is drydocs-load / graph-infra work and belongs to whatever item the gate produces, not to this one. p3 on the entry's own Low priority -- the nodes have sat edgeless since 2026-08-02 with no consequence beyond an unanswerable query, and the H5 question it feeds is not scheduled.

Acceptance: (a) THE BRANCH PIN: the caller asks CI about the branch it is actually on — `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in place of the literal `main` (line 166 at this groom: `gh run list --branch main --limit 10 --json ...`). Today the script fetches main's ten newest runs and matches the LOCAL HEAD sha against them, so from a worktree, an epic slice, an agent fork or any `feat/` branch — exactly the sessions CLAUDE.md tells you to branch for — HEAD is never in the answer and every run takes the yellow "no run yet for HEAD" path until merge. The worked example is the branch this was filed from: CI was GREEN on `feat/ui-workstream` and invisible to a query pinned to `main`.
