(b) FIVE FIXTURES FOR `Get-CiVerdict`, which its own design comment already claims is "a pure function of (runs, head) so every branch is exercisable without a network" and which has NO tests: green-at-head, failed-at-head-with-an-older-success-in-the-list, in-progress-at-head, no-run-yet-for-head, and EMPTY runs. The empty case is the one that would have caught the 2026-08-20 false GREEN. (c) THE TESTS MUST NOT BREAK CI: there is no Pester in this repo and the CI runner's PowerShell availability is not established, so the check SKIPS CLEANLY where no PowerShell is present, with a message naming what is missing (the U26 precedent for `test_probe_instrument.py`'s skip). The mechanism is the implementer's — pytest invoking pwsh with the function dot-sourced, or extracting the verdict so it can be driven directly — the five named cases are the acceptance, not the harness. (d) WARN-ONLY IS UNCHANGED (U24 clause d): this reports, it never blocks the snapshot. (e) VERIFIED BY RE-RUN, NOT BY READING, with the venue named (J18): one snapshot run FROM A BRANCH whose printed verdict line is quoted in the close note, plus one from the main checkout.

K16FID directory census: measure the demand-set pull scope on ONE application, and the registration-vs-attribution disagreement rate
configP9taskp2sonnet / main
seal-attribution

Acceptance: For ONE application, three counts are reported (counts ONLY — never a row dump; the output is Internal and lands company-side): (a) total directory rows for that application; (b) |demand set ∩ that application|, where the demand set is the union of run-as owners in the Control-M extract, distinct STG_APP_FACT fact_value rows with fact_type='FID' the K2 resolver currently counts unresolved, and account names in registered adhoc evidence; (c) the breakdown of (a) minus (b) by the directory's own type/status columns. PLUS the §Q0 measurement the gate cannot sign without: of the accounts in the demand set, how many have a directory application assignment that DISAGREES with the Control-M-derived folder attribution, and the by-case split of those disagreements into "different subjects, both correct" vs "stale directory" vs "wrong folder attribution" (§G5). Doc 09's phase table is updated with the real numbers. No pull beyond the demand set; no rows loaded.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-05 (desktop) from the 2026-08-05 IDEAS entries. THIS RUNS BEFORE THE GATE, not after: "about two hundred accounts per application" is the estimate the gate cannot rule on, and the census turns it into "N of ~200, and here is what the other rows are". The §Q0 disagreement breakdown is the part that decides whether the directory is a trustworthy ownership source with expected consumer divergence, or a lagging record needing remediation — a question raised only after the gate was drafted, which is why it sits in a separate item rather than inside the gate page. module: config (a source-scoping measurement, not a loader). Producer-side this repo carries the METHOD; the counts themselves are Internal. PRODUCER HALF DELIVERED 2026-08-07 (laptop), and the item is BLOCKED rather than done because its acceptance asks for real counts this repo structurally cannot produce — it holds no directory extract, which is the whole point of the demand-set pull. Shipped: drydocs/fid_census.py (pure — opens no file, contacts no database, writes nothing; every input injected), tests/unit/test_fid_census.py (14 tests, all synthetic), and docs/company-prompts/k16-fid-census-company-prompt.md following the 2026-08-07 company-pack convention. Doc 09 gains a "The numbers" table with every cell marked pending, and an explicit note that an empty cell means NOT MEASURED, never zero. TWO DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE COUNTS ARRIVE. (1) COUNTS-ONLY IS ENFORCED BY THE RETURN TYPE, not by discipline: FidCensus holds int and dict[str,int] fields only, so a row dump is UNEXPRESSIBLE, and a test pins that structurally. That is what lets the result travel back into this repo at all — a later field carrying account names would leak Internal values into a producer-side artifact. (2) THE §G5 READING IS NEVER COMPUTED. The gate says the three readings are distinguished per case and never globally, with a human ruling each — so the census counts disagreements mechanically and parks every one in `unruled` until an SME ruling is injected. The number still sitting in `unruled` is itself reportable: the never-silent rule applied to the report rather than to a load. THE BLOCKER'S REASON CHANGED 2026-08-12 (SME evidence) — still blocked, much smaller ask. The FID directory is not an external system needing an export or an onboarding: it is `psgmgr.HR_PHONE_EXP`, functional rows `EMP_TYP_CD = 'FCT'`, in the replica ALREADY IN SCOPE and already the Control-M source. So the census is a SINGLE-SCHEMA JOIN — demand set (i) from CM_DEF_VJOB.OWNER against the directory in the same schema — and no new source crosses the boundary. Status stays blocked because the counts are Internal and this repo has no psgmgr access, which is unchanged; what changed is that satisfying it no longer waits on a source onboarding, only on someone running the query company-side. RUN Q6 FIRST (gate fid-identity-and-scope): whether CM_DEF_VJOB.OWNER holds the NAME or the ID decides the join key, and the two keys give different demand sets. Measuring with the wrong one produces a confident wrong number. module: config is kept as the WORK AREA; the code module classifies as drydocs-review in test_module_boundary.py (it loads nothing and configures nothing — it produces the counts an SME rules from, the same reasoning that puts source_mappings there). TWO-SOURCE EVIDENCE 2026-08-19 (desktop; SME captures made on the SME machine, moved to the data root fid/screenshots/ per the G42 precedent — J18, shapes only in this repo). The SME establishes TWO pull surfaces, recorded as doc 09's new "Two sources, two grains" section. (A) the HR employee-data custom solution — the FID NAME (no application id in the row) carried as a functional-type HR entry with the MANAGER field repurposed as the account's owner; profiled at 227 rows / 23 cols, every id unique, only 54 distinct names, ONE agent-account name registered 171 separate ways (75%) each to a different manager+cost center — so the grain is (account id, owner), exactly what fid_census.py was built for, and this source answers WHO OWNS, never WHICH APPLICATION. SME clarification 2026-08-19: that 171-way name is the Control-M PLATFORM user (jobs running as Control-M itself), a run_as CLASS the plan had not separated — and it is cross-platform (Informatica carries several such accounts for business-application jobs). Doc 09's two-source section carries the consequence; K25's detector now classifies run_as by class first. (B) the id-owner application searched BY application id — record id / FID / type / purpose / name; measured by-application totals 555, 500, 209, 59 across four captures (the "about two hundred" estimate spans an order of magnitude); SME caveat -- a by-application listing carries ALL environments and ALL subtypes including ids that connect to OTHER applications, app-to-app, and human shared accounts, so census (a) is an upper bound by construction and the gate's §D filters decide the rest. The join between the sources is the NAME (the key §A rules unsafe as identity) — name is the join, id is the identity, and the census can measure the join's lossiness. Census row (a) in doc 09 now carries the four measured totals. ALSO delivered -- knowledge/standards/technology/functional-id-concepts.md, the firm's FID doctrine transcribed generically (identity-not-account, record/legacy ids, id taxonomy, FID-vs-accounts 1-to-many, owner roles, individual vs catalog-role assignment, the succession cascade that rewrites ownership with no FID-side event — the §B3 as-of argument, now sourced). K25 direct-added for the cross-application run_as class. Acceptance: (a) EVERY MAPPED FIELD'S ABSENCE IS LOUD, NOT ONLY THE REQUIRED ONES. Today `_project` raises `ProjectionError` for the three `REQUIRED_FIELDS` (`team_id`, `product_id`, `relationship_type`) and merely RECORDS the rest on `ProjectionReport.missing_optional`, which `scripts/project_pat_team_report.py` never turns into a non-zero exit or a warning stream. Verified producer-side: `seal_ids` is mapped to the header `"SEAL IDs"` and marked PINNED, and it is NOT in `REQUIRED_FIELDS` — so a real export spelling that column differently degrades to an empty value for every row, the `PatProductMapping` rows carry no SEAL ids, and a run that prints a success summary writes zero dev-team-to-application edges. After this item, a mapped header that the raw report does not carry produces a loud, non-zero-exit failure or an explicit acknowledged-absence flag; there is no third path where it is quietly empty. Cover it with a test that drives `_project` with `seal_ids` absent and asserts the loud behaviour. (b) THE HEADER MAP AND `KNOWN_DROPPED` ARE RE-PINNED FROM THE LANDED HEADER LIST, NOT FROM RELAY. The company session that measured and fixed this defect class on their side lands the header facts as a citable file carrying that cluster's SME review status. Do the edits FROM THAT FILE once it is in this tree (or in `internal-local/` with its path recorded in the close note) — never from a chat summary of it. `DEFAULT_HEADER_MAP` and the 12-entry `KNOWN_DROPPED` set are corrected and extended against the recorded schema-of-record section; every entry that changes says in a comment which spelling it replaced, so the previous belief stays legible instead of being overwritten silently. (c) `jira_board_id` IS RESOLVED, ONE WAY OR THE OTHER. It currently maps to `"JIRA Board"`, a header this report does not carry — it lives in a sibling export. Either drop it from `DEFAULT_HEADER_MAP` (and record where the field really comes from), or keep it and mark it explicitly acknowledged-absent under (a) so it does not trip the new loudness rule on every run. A mapped field pointing at another file's column is exactly the condition (a) is meant to make impossible to ignore. (d) THE FIXTURE STOPS AGREEING WITH THE CODE BY CONSTRUCTION. `tests/unit/test_pat_projection.py` writes its synthetic header row in the SAME believed spellings the code looks for (it writes `"SEAL IDs"`), so code and test can be wrong together and the suite cannot tell. Re-pin the fixture headers against the RECORDED header list from the review status, not against `DEFAULT_HEADER_MAP`. Add a guard asserting the fixture's header row is drawn from the recorded list rather than from the module's own constant — that structural link is what closes the trap; a hand-corrected fixture would only move the coincidence. (e) THE LEDGER FOLLOWS. `config/source-mappings/pat-team-report.yaml` was authored from the projection's own header map (G82 deliverable 4), so every correction under (b) propagates to it; its `pinned:` flags flip only for spellings the landed list actually confirms, and the ones it does not cover stay `pinned: false`. (f) NO REAL VALUES, AND NO ESTATE VOLUMETRICS. Header NAMES are mechanism and commit (03-hitl-sme-flow: column names commit, values never). Row counts for the real estate stay out per the volumetrics fence — the close note reports fixture counts and the shape of what changed, not how many teams the company has. (g) BLOCKED-NOT-STARTED IS A LEGITIMATE OUTCOME FOR (b)/(d). If the landed header file is not in the tree when this is pulled, do (a) and (c) — which are fully producer-verifiable today — and set the item `blocked` with a note naming the missing artifact, rather than re-pinning from memory. Guessing the spellings is the exact defect being fixed.

RE-REFERENCED 2026-08-09 (desktop, SME direction with vendor-doc evidence in hand): the terminal stage is PROVISIONED, not SNOWFLAKE — title corrected, and the same correction applied to docs/restructure/roadmap.yaml, which carried the old set. THE ERROR CLASS IS ONE THE SME ALREADY CALLED ONCE, one level down: at C25 the ruling was that Snowflake is a TARGET DB PLATFORM and the 'Snowflake ETL' label names the loads-into-Snowflake JOB FAMILY, not a software product. Same mistake here — a consumption TARGET was promoted into a STAGE slot, so the vocabulary asserted that every dataset's final stage is one particular warehouse. PROVISIONED is the stage; Snowflake is one of several platforms a Provision pipeline can write to (the internal DPL documentation's consumption zone lists relational and MPP targets alongside it). THE REPO ALREADY KNEW, which is why this is a correction rather than a discovery: the 2026-07 DPL ingestion-leg trace in IDEAS.md states 'PROVISIONING DB-load lands the consumption target (Provisioned ≠ an S3 prefix)' — B5's title simply never caught up, and roadmap.yaml inherited the stale set. That is also the substantive point for the capture: RAW/TRUSTED/REFINED are S3 zone PREFIXES while PROVISIONED is not a prefix at all, so the four names are not four of a kind and a flat enum would misrepresent the last one. NEW FINDING the capture must settle, from the same evidence: there appear to be TWO zone vocabularies, not one — an on-prem set (conformed / semantic / analytic) and an off-prem S3 set (trusted / refined), converging on a shared provision stage. So 'the estate's canonical stage set' may not be a single list, and the gate should rule whether they are one vocabulary with platform-scoped names or two that map onto each other. SOURCE BOUNDARY: the evidence is company-internal documentation; only the stage/zone MECHANISM is recorded here — the site, its URLs, and every identifier on it stay company-side (PUBLISH-BOUNDARY.md).

THE FACT EXPOSED A LIVE DEFECT the rider never asked about: our node keys are strings, pydantic v2 does not coerce int -> str, and every catalog id field was a bare str — so a numerically typed read of the real feed rejects EVERY catalog row, not some (verified against the shipped models before the fix). attribution.py already carried this coercion for the Control-M keys; the catalog loaders never got it. _catalog_id refuses a fractional id rather than rounding, and normalizes integral floats (a nullable numeric column via pandas arrives float64, where a blind str() keys '12345.0' and MERGEs a duplicate beside the real node). NOT DECIDED: the Sub-LoB grain the same fact reveals (we model none) is an ontology decision belonging to the parked company-catalog back-flow item. Gate-log carries a PARTIAL RULING entry — the seal-app-ref-edge-reshape gate as a whole remains unsigned. Suite 1296. The two sponsoring ID columns appear CO-POPULATED rather than exclusive — cypher §3a/§3b already fire independently, so the loader is right; confirm the model intends both. Notes: Groomed 2026-08-05 (desktop) from the 2026-08-05 IDEAS entries. Sibling of C12/C14 (the other USES_SOFTWARE rulings) — hence epic ontology-mapping, phase 2, not the K-series. model: fable: it registers a new vocabulary entry and rules a MERGE key. THE TWO THINGS THE GATE EXISTS TO PREVENT, both defects in the opening proposal: (1) Neo4j cannot attach a relationship to a relationship, so evidence attaches by property pointer, node-grain edge, or a reified assertion — never as an edge hung off the USES_SOFTWARE edge; (2) the evidence rows are (fid-name, install-path) rows, so writing the app-level edge directly bakes a mutable ownership join into a fact and discards the only grain at which it can later be re-derived. SEPARATELY WORTH KNOWING (corrected 2026-08-05 — an earlier draft of this note called it "a better USES_SOFTWARE source than this email", which overclaimed it): the Control-M SUB-APPLICATION field (PR<Appcode>-<Platform App Code>) declares WHICH PLATFORM an application runs on — documenting the platform is the naming standard's intent — so it is a standards-backed app→platform source at estate scale, good for a first-pass C1 container diagram. It is NOT a substitute for this email: it carries PRODUCT and never VERSION, so it does not touch the fact this gate is about. And it must be deduped to one edge per (application, product) — an app has many sub-applications all naming the same platform, so fanning them in at sub-application grain builds a super node on the product. Inboxed, not in this item; needs two software-registry product rows (DPL, Snowflake — see the correction below) first. MERGED IN 2026-08-05 (desktop, Idea-65's open residue): those TWO PRODUCT ROWS are now this item's prerequisite rather than a floating inbox line, because the gate cannot rule §C on a product vocabulary with holes in it. Two of the six framework codes have no `config/taxonomy/software-registry.yaml` row — DPL (the standing gap `invocation_patterns` already records, now with a name and a framework table behind it) and the SFS/Snowflake row. Registering them is taxonomy capture, reversible, and does not pre-empt any §C ruling: a product row says the product exists, not that any application uses it or at what version. CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (user, in-session): AWS Snowflake is a TARGET DB PLATFORM, not an ETL product — same family as AWS S3, AWS Glue tables, and AWS Iceberg tables. The DAT SRE table's "Snowflake ETL" label names the loads-into-Snowflake JOB FAMILY the SFS code marks, not a software product. So the missing registry row is `snowflake` the data platform (a DBMS-family category, sibling of `oracle-db`), never a "Snowflake ETL" tool row — and any app->platform edge derived from the SFS code reads "loads into Snowflake," not "runs a Snowflake ETL framework." DONE 2026-08-09 (desktop, SME in session): gate software-version-context SIGNED OFF for sections A-E and G; F NOT signed, still blocked on fid-identity-and-scope (K17). Full transcription in config/gate-log.md; the prompt's status flipped awaiting-sme -> signed-off with the decision block filled. THE HEADLINE, and it is the reason A2 is asked of the COMPILER rather than reasoned from the document type: A2 ruled USAGE, against this page's own recommendation, which said a readiness review usually inventories availability and cited the K7 OWNER-NOT-USER round as the warning. So A3 did NOT fire, USES_SOFTWARE is the right verb, and no second availability entry is needed. Had the gate reasoned it out instead of asking, it would have paused wrongly. CONFIRMED AS DRAFTED: A1, B1-B4, C1, C2, C4, D1, D3-D5, E1-E4. THREE RULINGS extended or differed from the draft: C3 never pads a missing component (absent is not zero -- 4.3.2 stays three components; version_raw keeps the verbatim token, and ragged comparison is the cost, paid openly); C5 adds an `evidence:` pointer block to the abinitio product row, because C2 correctly forbids observed versions from editing the curated ledger but left a row empty-because-nothing-is-known reading identically to empty-because-unreviewed (a pointer is not a version); D2 takes option (a), the evidence_doc_id property pointer -- (b) rejected as asserting the fid was sourced from the email rather than that THIS version claim was, (c) named as the upgrade path if a recurring feed arrives, with the pointer being what makes that migration mechanical. Q2 answered PARALLEL INSTALLS ARE REAL, which upgrades B2's multi-edge model from provisional to permanent: G3's 1:N holds, no uniqueness constraint, and NO `current` discriminator is needed -- the other answer would have shipped the load with a named gap. Q3 DEFERRED with its consequence stated rather than guessed: a symlinked estate would make install_path a poor MERGE key and move identity to (fid, version), a re-key, so the answer is worth having before the loader is built. PREREQUISITE DELIVERED FIRST (the notes' condition -- the gate cannot rule C on a product vocabulary with holes in it): `snowflake` and `dpl` product rows registered as taxonomy capture. DPL turned out not to be new modeling but a MISSING POINTER -- it was already an ETLProcess `engine` value (abinitio|dpl) while Ab Initio carried both an engine value AND a products: row, and that asymmetry had already cost the 2026-07-27 G26 guard catch, which removed the abinitio-dtlaunch-wrapper pattern row because dtlaunch.sh is the DPL spine and coverage_policy forbids a pattern row without a product id. SME supplied the expansion (DPL = Data Pipeline Library, registered in the acronyms block for the same reason AIS is there) and the mechanism (prepare/ingest/transform/provision pipeline types; Zilo is Spark-based, refining the 2026-07-16 note; EKS/GKP with Hortonworks heritage). versions: [] on dpl is deliberate -- the base image is datapipeline-apache-spark-3.5.1 tagged with the DPL image version, so 3.5.1 is the EMBEDDED SPARK and writing it here would record a dependency's version as the product's. VENDOR MODEL: new `in-house` vendor with NO publisher_url; a placeholder URL was considered and rejected as a value that resolves to nothing and is indistinguishable from a stale link. Guard narrowed to third-party vendors via an explicit allow-list, plus a second guard that a product of an exempt vendor must be type: internal so the exemption cannot launder a missing URL. Both PROVEN to fail on their defect -- and the FIRST proof round was worthless and is recorded as such: the registry file is CRLF, the injection patterns were LF, so neither defect was ever injected and both tests 'passed' against unmodified input. NOTHING LOADED, no loader built; reg_appuser_uses_software registered status: planned. Follow-ups carried out: the adhoc loader build, the C1 pattern rows (now unblocked for DPL), F re-run once K17 signs, and a PORT RELAY -- the producer is canonical for the two product rows, the in-house vendor and the DPL acronym; the SME began the same expansion company-side 2026-08-07 and stopped so the two would match. It must carry: (a) the SCOPE LADDER -- flow-invariants at SMART-folder scope, dataset identity at sub-folder scope, only per-job values on the job -- presented as making explicit the split the generator already performs via the folder AUTOEDIT block it assumes but never emits, with the BMC resolution order as the warrant and the VARIABLE_INC_SEC caveat stated (folder scope resolves for job processing parameters; resolving inside a job SCRIPT needs the server setting); (b) the HYBRID NAMING rule -- file-name components keep the names that map 1:1 to the CM_JOB_FILE_NAME_STANDARD columns so the SQL parse is a straight column copy, while short derived handles carry the composed path into commands, generalizing the idiom REQ-3 already uses; (c) the CANONICAL rule -- one name per concept, UPPER_SNAKE, with the variable name, the STG_APP_FACT fact_type, the SQL column and the ontology property stem being the same token, and the launcher FLAG recorded as a per-framework binding, never as the variable's name; (d) a before/after variable register per job type, every row citing both the live value it replaces and the generator builder that emits it; (e) the description token set per job type under the rule that the description carries only facts with no runtime role and no other home -- which drops the corpus's per-job EMAIL_DL tokens, drops PDN_SNOW_QUEUE, retires the INBOUND/OUTBOUND route pair on watchers because a watcher is inherently inbound, and renames the watcher's ENV to FTS_ID because ENV already means the deployment environment on the command jobs; (f) the pipelineId carrier ruling -- the CMDLINE literal is the carrier, any PIPELINE_ID variable is removed, and the DPL join key is recovered by a single anchored -pipeline extractor declared as an exception to NFR section 10 rather than a reopening of it; (g) contacts recorded as documentation-only for runbook extraction, with the support-tier versus Production-Delay-Notification split preserved as distinct contact kinds, and with the open REQ-2 question -- whether DOMAIL is removed alongside SHOUT -- left for the SME rather than assumed. Publish-boundary check clean: the live screenshots add a service account, a run-as, a SEAL, a FID, an author SID and two GUIDs to the strings that may never leave internal/.

Notes: Claimed 2026-08-11 (desktop) from SME direction with five live Control-M screenshots attached. THE REFRAME THAT MATTERS, and the reason this is not simply "fix the live folder": reading the generator capture before the live folder reverses most of the critique. The generator emits the canonical spellings (DATAFLOW, IMAGE, PROID, TIMEOUT) and orders DS_ID/DS_VER correctly; the live folder has the drifted ones. Every defect is hand-edit drift away from generator output, and it happens because the generator emits a PARTIAL job that depends on a folder AUTOEDIT block nothing declares -- so people hand-add the missing variables job by job and diverge. Fix the contract, not the instances. SME rulings recorded during design and binding on the write-up: notification is being REMOVED (the ServiceNow incident is the call to action, so nothing may wire a DL to a DOMAIL DEST or bind the unset NOTIFY); PDN is Production DELAY Notification to downstream business users and is not a support tier; no ServiceNow queue belongs in a Control-M variable because the escalation DB owns technician routing; the post-execution cat is TOK/CTL only and never a data file; and the live folder was mid-edit when captured, so some watcher findings are an unfinished conversion rather than deployed breakage and must not be written up as production defects.

C34dcat:theme — declare the EXISTING lob-product-team tree as a SKOS concept scheme and draft its gate, instead of minting a second subject vocabulary
ontologyP2taskp1opus / main
ontology-mapping

Acceptance: THE FINDING THAT SHAPES THIS ITEM, verified before it was raised rather than assumed: the hierarchy the SME proposed for subject classification -- LOB, Product Line, Product -- ALREADY EXISTS as config/taxonomy/lob-product-team.yaml (CatalogLOB > ProductLine > Product > DevTeam, B3, captured 2026-06-20), and the SME's vernacular examples are already ProductLine rows in it. This item does NOT mint a subject vocabulary; it declares the one that exists. (a) THE SKOS DECLARATION -- taxonomy, layer 1, NO gate, lands immediately. The file is a concept scheme in all but name: classification_only, hierarchical via parent_lob / parent_product_line, id-keyed, labelled. Declare it a skos:ConceptScheme with the parent links as skos:broader so dcat:theme has something standards-valid to point at. SKOS is already precedent in this very file, which cites skos:closeMatch for RECONCILES_TO. (b) THE GATE PROMPT, drafted not signed -- dcat:theme is a MEANING edge. It must pose: (b1) RESIDENCY, which BLOCKS the cross-corpus half. The design puts structured and unstructured context in TWO DATABASES, and a Neo4j relationship cannot span databases (Q8 -- the same constraint blocking G32's estate join), so one edge cannot reach one shared Concept from both sides. Three shapes: duplicate the scheme per database with identical concept IRIs; hold the scheme in one and carry the theme on the other as an IRI-valued PROPERTY joined application-side; or single database (ADR 0011). DECIDABLE NOW REGARDLESS, and the prompt says so: make the concept IRI the join key and keep it stable, so the vocabulary is portable whichever way residency rules and no work is stranded. (b2) IS a Product a skos:Concept, or does it HAVE one? ProductLine and Product are business entities with owners, teams and applications; dual-typing them is legal RDF and muddies what the node is. The alternative is a concept per product with skos:exactMatch. Rule it -- do not let a loader decide by accident. (b3) ANNOTATION DEPTH is the real control on grain: annotate at ONE level and derive the rest by skos:broader, so tagging a folder at Product yields its ProductLine and LOB free. That stops a deep vocabulary from multiplying annotations, and it beats capping vocabulary size, which forces a lie the moment the business genuinely has more rows than the cap. (b4) THE CARDINALITY ASK IS PREMATURE AT THE TIER NAMED, and the prompt must say why rather than silently declining. The SME asked for a limit under 5 at the AreaProduct level; lob-product-team.yaml records area_products: 0 and carries a STANDING OPEN QUESTION (area-product-missing) on whether that tier applies outside production PAT at all. Rule the tier before capping it. What CAN be ruled now is the ANNOTATION cap -- how many themes one subject may carry -- enforced as a DETECTOR, not a schema constraint, because a folder carrying six themes is evidence the folder does too much or the tagger hedged, and that is a finding worth reading rather than a write to refuse. (c) UNCLASSIFIED IS FIRST-CLASS, and out-of-scope is a DIFFERENT value from not-yet- classified. External-vendor and unrelated pages are permanently out of scope; an unclassified internal page is pending. Collapsing them makes coverage unmeasurable, because the number stops distinguishing backlog from scope. Same discipline as resource_pool.classify returning unknown with no label and a WARN. No graph writes, no ratification: the scheme declaration ships, the edge is the gate's.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 from an SME design session that began on Idea-105 and opened a second thread. THE ORIGINAL INTENT: folder-level runbooks are >90% automatable, and the roll-up axis was going to be "Data Series" -- an entity that is not commonly defined. Teams think in source name instead, which is why the existing ProductLine tier fits: it is both the vernacular people already use AND already captured. The roll-up therefore falls out of the concept scheme without Data Series ever being defined, which is the part to protect in review. WHY IT REACHES THE CONTEXT GRAPH (SME observation, and it is right): a theme is a PROJECTION AXIS, so "everything in this subject, right now" becomes a layer-4 slice instead of needing a new entity to hang it on. Themes are multi-valued by nature, so a process serving two subjects appears in both slices with nothing duplicated -- which a single Data Series field could never have done. SCOPE FENCE: declares and drafts. Does not populate real values (Internal), does not write the edge, does not build UI. AMENDED 2026-08-20 (user direction, the theme-search ruling). THREE UPDATES: (1) QUESTION (b1) IS ANSWERED BY THE G102 FOLD — the residency blocker was written against the two-database design, and content + structure are ONE database since 2026-08-18, so dcat:theme can be a plain edge to a shared Concept; the prompt should record (b1) as answered-by-fold, not pose it. (2) THE EVIDENCE UPGRADED: the firm's Taxonomy Framework (v21) and its sibling standards are now VERBATIM-captured (the 2026-08-19 live fetch, cdo-frameworks row) — the scheme declaration can cite the published standard directly instead of a partial transcription. (3) THE CONSUMER IS NAMED: the retrieval capability over this scheme is THEME SEARCH (dcat:theme-scoped retrieval over the standards corpus) — deliberately NOT "context search"; the naming rule and its three-senses census live in config/taxonomy/context-types.yaml's header. Groom the theme-search build as its own item once this gate signs; "context" never appears in its ids.

Notes: Raised at the business-application-identity gate §F2 (SIGNED OFF 2026-07-27). SME reason, verbatim in substance: the glossary will for the most part be internal unless there are industry-standard acronyms or names, and doing the scaffolding producer-side now means the internal ports do not collide later with either a name or a backlog item. That is a PORT-SEQUENCING argument, not an ontology one — which is why reservation is the whole deliverable. WHY IT IS AN ITEM RATHER THAN AN ACT OF THAT GATE: the identity gate's §A1 states it "creates no relationship-vocabulary term". Registering the edges inside it would have falsified A1 and re-opened a ruled scope item, so the registration was pushed here, where `status: planned` needs no gate of its own. Substance this feeds: F2's finding that the durable home for what an acronym MEANS is a CatalogBusinessTerm-shaped glossary, the same conclusion the reopened gate-log Q6 acronym question circles, plus the Unity Catalog takeaway that a controlled vocabulary needs an enforcement point or it rots. The identity gate is itself the evidence: "SEAL" was found carrying THREE distinct meanings across three homes (the issuing authority, the source id, and an ecosystem referencing convention used in Control-M CMDLINEs), and nothing in the repo recorded that they were different things. MERGED IN 2026-08-05 (desktop, Idea-35 — the acronym-catalog line): that entry is CONTENT for this scaffold, not a second home, and it names the shape the scaffold should be able to hold — which is worth knowing while building the empty version. Its requirement: key by acronym, carry MANY senses per key, and tag each sense with its scope (`area`, `business-domain`, `technical-domain`, `industry` — what an outsider would assume). Plus, wherever a misreading has actually happened, an explicit **does-NOT-mean** note; that note, not the expansion, is the protective sentence. AIS is the worked example and the reason: "as-is" (a standard modeling idiom) vs "Application Integration Streaming" (an org platform family), with our own `:AisTool` label having meant NEITHER. Today `software-registry.yaml#acronyms` is a one-key section with no scope dimension, so it can record expansions but not COLLISIONS — and collisions are the failure mode that bites. This is a SKOS job (prefLabel / altLabel / definition / scopeNote, senses as concepts in a scheme); SKOS is declared in reference/standards/README.md but has NO fetched local copy yet, unlike prov-o / w3c-org / dprod-ekgf / sosa-ssn — fetching it belongs with the content pass. SCAFFOLD-ONLY STILL HOLDS: this item defines no terms, so nothing above changes its acceptance. The content pass stays parked on its own trigger, the gate-log Q6 ruling (which decides whether `#acronyms` survives at all), and lands INSIDE this scaffold. DONE 2026-08-21 (desktop): reservation landed — 4 node classifications + 3 planned edges (42-local-catalog.yaml), map entry catalog-business-term (proposed), config/glossary/ (schema, Internal-Public) + internal/glossary/ (definitions, Internal, empty). SME scope caveat recorded: the company runs a dedicated acronym tool; this glossary holds ONLY terms that correlate to what DryDocs ingests, first producer = drydocs_deepdoc (epic MM). No term defined, no loader, no gate.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-18 from a prefix census of the vocabulary fragments run against §B3's own enumeration. The census matches the gate exactly on all eight epoch tags (21/5/1/5/1/4/1/4), so the vocabulary has not drifted since 2026-08-12 -- which is what makes the seal_ omission an omission rather than drift. Found while confirming for the user that the m3_ -> scheduler_ rename was already backlogged; it is, as G87, and this is the sibling gap that read of G87 surfaced. The one entry in the fragment that already conforms is business_application_port_has_contact_point, and the whole point of "domain-derived" (§B1) is that the prefix is mechanically the `domain:` field -- an abbreviation makes it a memorised lookup and reintroduces precisely the opacity m3_ had. It is 12 characters cheaper on ids that reach 43 characters, and that is a real cost, but it would (i) contradict §B1 of a SIGNED gate, (ii) make the one already-conformant entry non-conformant, and (iii) break the derivation rule for a saving on a string nobody types -- ids are join keys read by machines, not identifiers typed at a prompt. Kept separate because G87's scope is a SIGNED census and quietly widening it past what §B3 enumerated would make the item stop matching the ruling it cites, which is the audit trail. Notes: Split out of G28 at its close (2026-07-26) — G28 bundled this with the naming cleanup and they are different kinds of decision: G28 was mechanical drift against an already-ruled convention, this one changes WHERE curated lineage data lives. Measured: drydocs_lineage/writer.py line 70 pins DATABASE = "drydocs" and refuses any other database (TrustBoundaryError, an allowlist — so this is a correctness and emptiness problem, not a safety one); drydocs_api/query_specs.py declares database="ddlineage" on four specs (lines 417, 540, 565, 589). Those four specs therefore query a database that is provisioned by 01_databases.cypher and written by nothing. Not urgent — the lineage writer is gate-bound anyway (its vocabulary is status: planned, so write_curated refuses a live load until the HITL gate flips it), so nothing is silently producing wrong answers today; it would bite on the first live curated write. Ties to the lineage live-load gate parked in IDEAS. DONE 2026-07-26 — RULED (b): the four specs repoint to `drydocs`; ddlineage stays provisioned + composite-aliased but documented as provisioned-for-later. The ruling is written up in ADR 0002 as a "Residency clarification" — NOT an amendment, because D1/D2 already say drydocs-lineage writes ground truth to `drydocs` and were never amended when G1 provisioning added a fourth database two days later. Each half of the codebase had followed a different source and both cited one, which is why neither looked wrong alone. Three grounds: (1) the stated reason for the DB boundary is the TRUST axis, and curated lineage is VERBATIM/GROUNDED — the same tier as the main load, so splitting it serves nothing; (2) 0002-C §5 already carries a ticked, tested "writes ground truth only" gate; (3) decisive — write_curated MATCHes :ControlMJob nodes the M3 load owns in `drydocs` and deliberately never MERGEs them (a lineage-created stub would break m3-verify's "every job has a folder"). A transaction cannot span databases, so from ddlineage those MATCHes would match nothing and every job-endpoint edge would vanish SILENTLY — an unmatched MATCH yields zero rows, not an error. Option (a) is therefore a design (a :ControlMJob proxy spine in ddlineage), not a constant flip. Deferring is also the cheap direction: ddlineage is empty, so choosing it later costs a design, not a migration. Named trigger to revisit, as an ADR amendment through the gate: the docmeta gate (ADR 0006 §b) adopted `dddocs` on the same component-per-database pattern and re-targets the bmc-docs corpus out of `drydocs` — if that proves out and lineage grows its own proxy spine, reopen. Notes: Design session 2026-07-26 (after G30). SME direction: THREE databases — structured / unstructured-content / derived — for separation of loads and wipe blast-radius during testing, both of which hold independently of retention. Retention turned out NOT to be an argument either way (see Q10). THE COST, to be accepted explicitly rather than discovered later. `ddall` federates reads but a relationship can NEVER span databases — a composite query is a join on returned values, not an edge walk (see the shape in provisioning/smoke_drydocs_all.cypher: chained `CALL { USE ddall.x }` blocks). So known-shape questions still work, restated as explicit joins, and every QuerySpec is fine. What is lost across the boundary: shortestPath and variable-length paths, all GDS (centrality, community, similarity), and a single vector index over reference AND content chunks — which becomes two index queries plus a client-side rerank, notable because the Essential GraphRAG corpus was ingested to do exactly that kind of retrieval. Also harder: text2cypher (Epic R / ADR 0007) must generate correct USE clauses and business-key joins rather than a plain MATCH. If those matter, the mitigation is a single-database analytical projection, and that should be decided here rather than improvised later. Blocks G31 (the spine cannot be sized until the database set is known) and through it Q9/Q10/Q11. Clause (e) merged at the 2026-07-27 groom from the 2026-07-26 deepdoc-scope inbox entry (user question; NOT covered by the database ruling alone). Rider: the graph-seeded-retrieval shape is the SECOND application of the same idea (first: the 2026-07-23 HR-hierarchy graph-seeded resolution) — name it as a reusable pattern in the ruling instead of re-deriving it. Until (e) is ruled, do not build the deepdoc scaffold against either stale charter. CLOSE CHECKLIST — WORK THESE BEFORE FLIPPING THIS ITEM done. Added 2026-08-07 (laptop) on the user's ruling, because each one is a real consequence of this ruling that has NO item of its own and would otherwise be found only by re-reading prose. (1) Q16 CLAUSE (b) HAS NO SUCCESSOR ITEM. Q16 closed `done` on 2026-08-07 as an explicit PARTIAL: its clause (a) shipped (drydocs docs-coverage), but clause (b) — the product->documentation pointer reaching the GRAPH so an agent can traverse from a product to the docs describing it — did NOT, and is blocked behind Q14 (the term) which is blocked behind THIS item. Its only forward trace today is prose in Q16's close note pointing at Idea-88. So: when this signs, either mint the successor item or record in the sign-off that (b) is declined — do not leave it traceable only by prose. The ruling decides which: if doc corpora land in the registry's database, (b) becomes buildable and DESCRIBES may need nothing new (Q16's own "cheapest possible answer, check FIRST"); if the boundary hardens, (b) is re-scoped as a business-key join and its acceptance changes shape. (2) THE `not queried` LABELS GO STALE THE DAY THIS SIGNS. Two surfaces render "dddocs is not provisioned (G32)" from the declaration — web/src/software/softwareModel.ts (inGraphLabel) and the docs-coverage detail lines. tests/unit/test_load_map_json.py:: test_the_not_queryable_target_db_set_is_pinned pins that set to exactly {dddocs} and WILL FAIL when this ruling lands, which is deliberate: it is the alarm that forces both surfaces to be revisited rather than quietly lying. Treat that failure as a task, not a break. (3) THE ONE WORKING TRAVERSAL DIES OR SURVIVES BY THIS RULING. The 27 live (:Document)-[:DESCRIBES]->(:SoftwareProduct) edges exist ONLY because bmc-docs is loaded in `drydocs` while declaring target_db: dddocs — the residency accident this item exists to end. vendor_docs.cypher already refuses to write that edge for exactly this reason. Say explicitly in the ruling what happens to those 27 edges at the move; docs-coverage reports the state as `traversable-until-move` precisely so it is not mistaken for a durable capability.

G53Contingency plan: fold every database into one if multi-DB is ever unavailable

Acceptance: A written consolidation plan (an ADR 0002 amendment or its own ADR) that answers each of these with a concrete mechanism rather than an intention: (1) HOW THE TRUST BOUNDARY SURVIVES — ADR 0002 D1 rejected the single-DB option because it commingles trust, so name the label namespace, the trust property, and the guard tests that would replace the transaction domain, and state plainly what protection is lost (the ADR's own words: multi-DB moves the guarantee "from discipline to physics", and one DB moves it back); (2) HOW ddschema's EXEMPLAR NODES COEXIST WITH drydocs' NODE KEYs — exemplars carry real labels WITHOUT the properties those keys require, which is the stated reason ddschema is its own database (G51), so this is a hard constraint conflict, not a naming collision; (3) WHAT REPLACES ddall — an enumeration of every QuerySpec, loader, and console route that names a non-default database or federates through the composite; (4) THE CONFIG CHANGE POINT — dev-environment.yaml's db-name map, and whether one map can serve both topologies so the fallback is a config switch rather than a code fork. Plan only: no provisioning, loader, or schema changes land from this item.

Notes: Worst-case contingency, groomed 2026-08-04 on the user's direction after the laptop's Neo4j Enterprise 30-day eval trial expired (2026-08-01). THE EXPIRY IS NOT THE TRIGGER and is explicitly out of scope — it is a local-testing license matter, the server keeps running, and writes were verified working after it (laptop, neo4jtest, drydocs DB: 2218 nodes, an Enterprise-only existence constraint created then dropped, six user databases online). What this plans for is Enterprise becoming genuinely unavailable — a company-side edition constraint or a cost ruling — because Community allows exactly ONE user database. That would collapse drydocs + ddlineage + ddcontext + ddschema into one store and remove the ddall composite entirely. ADR 0002 already priced this option and rejected it: "Community single DB + reliability property + :Candidate label namespace" is a listed D1 alternative, rejected because it commingles trust and "one bad query promotes noise". So this item does NOT re-open the decision — ADR 0002 stays accepted. It writes down the fallback we would otherwise have to improvise under duress, while there is time to think about it properly. The honest output may well be "consolidation costs us X and here is the sequence"; a plan that concludes the trust guarantee cannot be preserved in one database is a valid and useful result, provided it says so explicitly instead of papering over it.

G54provision.ps1 cannot run as documented on a Docker-only host: it shells out to cypher-shell on the host PATH
graph-infraP6bugp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A host running the neo4jtest container with NO local Neo4j install can provision the topology by following the script's own header. Exactly one of two resolutions: (a) the script becomes exec-aware — detect that cypher-shell is absent from the host PATH and fall back to `docker cp` of the .cypher file plus `docker exec … cypher-shell -f`, reading the container name from config/dev-environment.yaml rather than hardcoding it; or (b) the header's REQUIRES block stops presenting host cypher-shell as satisfied by "bundled in the Neo4j Docker image" — it is bundled INSIDE the image, which is not the host PATH — and documents the docker-exec invocation as the supported Docker-host form. (a) is preferred, since the header already owns the `docker run` commands and therefore already assumes Docker on this path. Either way the fix respects and states the J29 trap: do NOT pipe file content into `docker exec`; copy the file in and use `-f`, because a PowerShell 5.1 pipe injects a UTF-8 BOM that cypher-shell then rejects.

Notes: Reported 2026-08-04 from the desktop M3 reload, where the documented invocation failed and the session worked around it with docker cp + docker exec cypher-shell -f. VERIFIED at the groom (laptop, static read — no database needed): the REQUIRES block at provision.ps1:6 says "cypher-shell on PATH (bundled in the Neo4j Docker image and tarball)" while the runner at :57 invokes bare `cypher-shell -a $Uri … -f`. On a Windows host whose only Neo4j is the container, that binary is not on PATH and the script cannot complete. The BOM half of the original inbox report was WRONG and is already closed: J29's byte-scan proved every tracked .cypher and .sql is clean, and the BOM came from the PS 5.1 pipe rather than from the repo. That is exactly why the trap belongs in this item's header text — the workaround shape and the encoding standard are one lesson, and J29's own close note says this gap "stays inboxed separately". p2 rather than p1: both machines already hold working topologies, so nothing is blocked today. What is broken is the documented path for a fresh host. WORKAROUND DOCUMENTED 2026-08-04 (does NOT close this item — the script itself is unchanged): the provisioning README now carries the explicit per-file docker cp + docker exec -f block, verified end to end (laptop, neo4jtest, 2026.05.0 EE — six cypher-shell calls exit 0, smoke federates 2218/0/46). G56Collector captures the mount table, so shared-vs-local storage is DERIVED instead of declared (bundle schema v3)
drydocs-lineageP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A bundle answers "is this path on shared storage?" without asking a human. The collector emits an OPTIONAL mounts section capturing actual mount state — `findmnt -rn -o SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE,OPTIONS` with `/proc/mounts` as the no-findmnt fallback, both read-only and runnable as the service account with no privilege change. NOT lsblk and NOT /etc/fstab alone, and the script says why in a comment: `server:/path` is an NFS mount spec and NFS is not a block device, so it never appears in lsblk; and fstab is configured INTENT, not actual state (autofs/systemd/manual mounts are mounted without appearing there, stale lines appear without being mounted). COLLECTOR_VERSION bumps to v3. The extractor parses the section when present and files it under the EXISTING `sections_optional_absent` contract when absent, so every v1 and v2 bundle stays fully ingestible — the same discipline scripts.tsv already follows. Each staged path resolves against the LONGEST matching mount target to yield `mount_root` + `fstype`, and `storage_scope` derives from fstype — nfs/nfs4/cifs shared, xfs/ext4 single-host unless gfs2/ocfs2 clustered, anything unrecognised `unknown` and COUNTED, never guessed. Synthetic fixtures only (real mount specs carry live server names); tests cover a shared-NFS bundle, a local-only bundle, a mounts-absent v2 bundle, and an unrecognised fstype.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-06 (laptop) at the G22 session, from SME direction. THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES: a deployment path may be shared — the SME's case is roughly 20 VSI hosts against one shared filesystem — and then the same path on N hosts is ONE FILE SEEN N TIMES, not N deployments. Today that is not derivable from any bundle we hold: the collector captures no mount table at all, the envelope carries scan_roots but never which filesystem a root sits on, and the ownership sweep's -xdev stays on one filesystem without recording which. THE CORRECTION THAT SHAPES THE ACCEPTANCE, made at the session: "on the SAN" does not mean shared. Twenty hosts each with their OWN LUN from one array is twenty separate filesystems and twenty files that genuinely drift; twenty hosts mounting ONE NFS export is one file seen twenty times. Sharing follows from FSTYPE, never from the array — which is why the type column is load-bearing and why lsblk alone would actively mislead. WHY NOW IS THE CHEAP MOMENT (SME, same session): nothing has been loaded yet and the company-side twin collector is NOT present, so a schema bump costs no convergence debt. The earlier T14 caveat is WITHDRAWN on that correction. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REMOVE: bundles already collected stay scope-unknown, so the G22 D-amendment rule stands either way — `unknown` never defaults to independent, it SUPPRESSES the corroboration claim. This item reduces how often that state occurs; it does not retire it. NOT gate-bound: capturing a fact is an instrument change, not a decision about what an edge MEANS. It was deliberately NOT edited at the gate because the collector runs on production hosts. DONE 2026-08-25 (desktop). Built exactly the acceptance, and the seam it lands on turned out to already exist: G23's writer does `props.setdefault("storage_scope", "unknown")` and G58's archival report reads `storage_scope` off the occurrence records, so stamping on the record completed both with ZERO edits to either. COLLECTOR: v3, `mounts.tsv` emitted UNCONDITIONALLY (read-only and instant — "optional" is the INGEST contract, not a config knob), `findmnt -rn -o SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE,OPTIONS` normalised to tabs by awk, `/proc/mounts` the fallback, and `meta.txt` records `mounts_captured` + `mounts_source` so which tool answered is a fact. Fields travel verbatim — findmnt's \040 escapes are NOT decoded, so a space-bearing target simply fails to match and shows up as `mount_unresolved` rather than as a wrong mount silently claimed. The why-not-lsblk / why-not-fstab reasoning is in the script per the acceptance. ONE TRAP CAUGHT: `usage()` renders the header block by LINE RANGE (`sed -n '2,41p'`), so the header growing by four lines would have silently truncated `--help`; the range moved to 2,45 and the render was checked. EXTRACTOR: presence dispatch, never the `schema=` tag (the scripts.tsv discipline); absent files under the EXISTING `sections_optional_absent` contract. `None` (no table) and an unmatched path are DIFFERENT states and stay different: a v1/v2 bundle stamps NOTHING and comes out byte-identical, while a v3 bundle whose table misses a path stamps `unknown` and counts it. Longest-match is BOUNDARY-AWARE (`/opt/app2` must not match `/opt/app`) with equal targets resolving to the last row (mount order). The fstype map is EXACTLY the amendment's set — nfs, nfs4, cifs, gfs2, ocfs2 shared; xfs, ext4 local; everything else `unknown`, counted, AND NAMED in `mount_fstypes_unrecognised` so the review queue can say which. Stamping happens BEFORE the occurrence copy, which is the D2 tie-in and is asserted. TWO DELIBERATE ADDITIONS beyond the literal acceptance, both cheap-now/expensive-later on the amendment's own mount_root reasoning: `mount_source` is stamped (shared fstype alone does NOT prove two hosts see the same file — they can mount nfs4 at one path from different exports — and SOURCE equality is what a future identity-confirmation pass needs), and a G103-style contract test pins the collector's header literal against `_REQUIRED_COLS[MOUNTS_TSV]` so a renamed column cannot surface as "a bad bundle". TESTS: 9 new in `tests/unit/test_lineage_rua.py` — the four the acceptance names (shared-NFS, local-only, mounts-absent v2, unrecognised fstype) plus boundary-awareness, present-but-unmatched, malformed rows, the collector/extractor column contract, and the scope map itself. Synthetic fixtures only. The shared case doubles as the longest-match proof (`/` is xfs and would read LOCAL; `/home/svc_synth` is nfs4 and is the answer), and both properties were MUTATION-CHECKED: naive-startswith fails 1 test, first-match-wins fails 4. NOTE ON THIS ITEM'S OWN `inputs`: it lists `tests/unit/test_lineage_inventory.py`, which is the Control-M oracle — a groom slip; the rua tests live in `tests/unit/test_lineage_rua.py` and that is where these went. NOT DONE, ON PURPOSE — Idea-175: writer.py's `identity_unconfirmed_across_hosts` is still `len(node_hosts) > 1` with no scope check, so it over-flags the shared case. Out of scope here (this item's inputs are the collector and the extractor; that is a claim-layer change carrying the mount_source caveat above), but its two "until G56" comments were re-pointed at Idea-175 in this commit rather than left reading false — comment-only, no logic moved. Collector verified live on THIS DESKTOP under Git Bash/MSYS (not RHEL): a real run over a synthetic $HOME produced a 4-row tab-separated `mounts.tsv` via the `/proc/mounts` fallback with escapes intact. Full suite 2441 passed / 10 skipped, ruff check + format clean.

G58Dead-script archival report: three dispositions, a stated coverage precondition, and the already-archived count
drydocs-lineageP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology
depends on: G23

Acceptance: The report G22 §E3 named as the usage axis's use case — identifying unused, deprecated code for archival and removal — ships WITH the safety properties the gate ruled, and a test proves each one. (a) COVERAGE IS STATED ON THE REPORT ITSELF, never a footnote. Every run declares its body-copy coverage, and a run over a metadata-only bundle says so in its own output. A test asserts that a report generated from a body-less fixture carries the coverage statement AND that its unreferenced rows read "no CMD_LINE reference" rather than "nothing calls it". (b) THREE DISPOSITIONS, not two, each separately counted: genuinely dead (archive and remove), MISDEPLOYED (relocate, never delete — §E1's caveat that a script may have been deployed to the wrong server), and unreferenced-but-dynamically-called (keep). A test proves the three are distinct buckets and that no candidate is silently absent from all three. (c) THE MISDEPLOYMENT BUCKET IS SCOPE-GATED: emitted only where storage_scope is `local`, because under shared storage every host sees ONE file and the finding is meaningless. Unknown scope suppresses it and COUNTS the suppression (the never-silent house rule). (d) ALREADY-ARCHIVED IS REPORTED, not only deletion candidates: scripts carrying a code-repo occurrence and NO current server-extract occurrence are counted as already archived — the progress measure toward the target state. The inverse (server occurrence, no repo occurrence) is G24's existing never_committed bucket: cross-referenced, never recomputed. (e) NO AXIS PROVES ABSENCE (§H1): every "absent on axis X" row reads as "not observed by feed X", and the active_unknown count appears in the report rather than being dropped. Full suite green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-07 (laptop) from Idea-80 + Idea-82 on user instruction to groom the two TOGETHER. They are one item rather than two because they turn on the SAME argument: an absence observed by one feed is not an absence in the world. Idea-80 supplies the dispositions and the coverage precondition; Idea-82 supplies the already-archived measure and the reason it needs no new flag. WHY IT IS SEPARATE FROM G23: G23 LOADS the bundle facts; this READS them. Folding the report into the loader is how a deletion-driving output gets built as a loader detail — the same distinction that keeps G55 separate from G23, and for the same reason. WHY (d) COSTS NO NEW VOCABULARY: after G22 §D2 ruled reified occurrence nodes carrying `origin`, "archived" is a SHAPE rather than a status — repo occurrence present, current server occurrence absent. That keeps it DERIVED FROM EVIDENCE rather than declared, the same move §G1 made when it put identity in the business key and made the URN a render, and it stays honest when a file comes back. DryDocs' existing word for the artifact-level fact is the TOMBSTONE (`removed_from_source_at`, the D7 sweep ruled at U13, live on :CodeModule today) — reuse the concept, and note that on :CodeModule it is a TIMESTAMP, not a status. THE SAFETY BAR IS WHY (a) AND (c) ARE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES RATHER THAN GOOD PRACTICE: the output drives DELETION, so a false positive removes live code. §H2 ruled active=true-but-unreferenced "the most dangerous false positive available" precisely because §E3's blind spot (no body copies, so script-to-script calls are invisible) is exactly what hides the caller. ONE QUESTION DELIBERATELY NOT GROOMED INTO AN ITEM: what to CALL the estate-level end state ("the production server holds only actively used code"). It is a property of the ESTATE, not of any node, so a formal graph-side term would be a vocabulary decision riding the HITL gate — and NOTHING NEEDS ONE YET. Minting an item for a decision no build depends on is how the backlog inflates. Surface it at this build if the report wants a term; the plain-English statement of the goal is L24's job and needs no gate. Explicitly DO NOT reach for the 00-header.yaml lifecycle (planned|active|deprecated|removed): that enum governs vocabulary ENTRIES (edge meanings, i.e. schema) and a script on a server is an INSTANCE — reusing the four words would put `removed` = "deleted an edge definition" and `removed` = "deleted a file off a server" in one repo, the two-things-one-spelling collision §A2 caught on `group` and J32 made a standing rule. HOME: drydocs_lineage/review.py is the lineage SME surface (CLI `drydocs lineage-review`, ported at ADR 0002-C) — the same surface §A3's signed ruling already sends same-basename multi-mount duplicates to for SME merge, so the curation ladder exists. PRIORITY NOTE: Idea-80 carried an agent-PROPOSED `prio? High` that the user never ruled. Filed p2 for coherence with its own dependency chain (G22/G23/G55 are all p2) — it cannot start before G23 regardless. Raise it if the archival drive lands before the rest of the chain. DONE 2026-08-07 (desktop, same session as G23): BUILT as drydocs_lineage/archival.py — archival_report() over the staged LineageGraph, PURE, writes nothing; findings are review material (H2/P5), surfaced as an optional section on the lineage-review page (to_html archival=..., the E3 curation-ladder surface). Every acceptance clause has its test (tests/unit/test_lineage_archival.py, 9 tests): (a) coverage stated ON the report — metadata-only runs say METADATA-ONLY RUN in their own output and dead rows read "no CMD_LINE reference observed", never a nothing-calls-it claim; (b) three distinct buckets (dead / misdeployed / dynamically_called via the who-references split: job-src rels = CMD_LINE feed, script-src rels = body-visible callers) + in_use counted, nothing silently absent; (c) misdeployment emitted ONLY under storage_scope local (all-records-local, conservative), unknown AND shared suppressed and counted; the row notes node_target polymorphism for the SME; (d) already-archived = G24 repo_only CROSS-REFERENCED from the CorroborationReport (never recomputed), never_committed likewise; no corroboration -> "archived-state not observed", not zero; (e) active_unknown passthrough (None = "registry axis not observed on this run"). The estate-level end-state TERM the notes deliberately left unminted stayed unminted — the report needed no term, plain counts suffice (L24 owns the prose goal). Suite 1698/3/5 — the 3 are the Idea-83 rich-ANSI env failures, untouched.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-07 (pm) from Idea-21. The anti-pattern itself is already codified (_FW-really-API plus design principle 8 — intent from resolved flow, flag the name-token disagreement); what is NOT settled is either gap class, and both are keying/meaning decisions, so they route through the gate rather than through a build. Drafted config/gate-prompts/script-provenance-gaps.yaml -- ONE page, both gap classes as its two ruling sections (3 sections, 13 confirmations, format guard green, loads via gate_pages). Drafts only; the sign-off is a separate SME session. TIMING TURNED OUT TO MATTER: both of the laptop's same-evening closes feed this draft. G97 (the m7 payload build) made gap (b)'s GUID-vs-path boundary OPERATIONAL -- GUID-keyed DPL targets stay :ETLProcess on INVOKES, path-shaped payloads land :Script on USES_ARTIFACT -- so §B2 asks the SME to RATIFY a boundary the build is already running on, with G97's bucket counts as the named re-verification if re-drawn. And G56's mount capture is what makes path identity DECIDABLE: §B3's proposed key is (storage_scope, normalized_path), collapsing to path alone on shared mounts, with the path-only alternative laid out for explicit rejection (wrong on local storage, where two hosts' identical paths are different files). GAP (a) -- the flag: §A proposes TRI-STATE scm_status (tracked | deployed-only | unknown, default unknown), attached to :Script (not the job, not the edge -- the artifact is the absent thing), carried with scm_checked_at + scm_search_scope (O24/A3 no anonymous assertions; K17 as-of -- an SCM absence is true as of the search and within its scope). §A4 states the may/may-not-conclude lists ON the term; §A5 argues deliberately that this is NOT :Uncertain -- a grounded negative observation with its basis on the node is not an unestablished finding, and blurring the two teaches consumers to discount the one flag §A4 wants acted on. GAP (b) -- identity: §B1 names the uncomfortable current truth -- :Script has NO uniqueness constraint and a GUID-less script has NO key at all, so two loads can mint two nodes for one script -- and proposes amending the lineage model's standing note from 'path is never identity' to 'never identity WHERE A GUID EXISTS'. §B4 keeps content hash a property (drift, version), never the key. §B5 states the sign-off blast radius honestly: a constraints.cypher addition, an EXPECTED_CONSTRAINTS bump, and the S3 null-ignoring-uniqueness backfill hazard, with the migration a groomed follow-up. REGISTRATION SHAPE, and why it differs from C28's: no new edge and no new node class exist to reserve -- both gaps are property/identity questions on the existing :Script. The acceptance's 'registered planned' lands as TWO map rows proposed in 50-mappings-architecture.yaml (script-scm-status, script-identity-binding; summary 9->11); the §0b property-term bindings CANNOT precede the gate -- the envelope-property-terms (M4) rule is that decided_by names a SIGNED gate -- so §C3 makes their at-sign-off registration an explicit clause instead of a silent omission. Four censuses, each carrying WHERE-USED rather than bare distinct values, because the SME's next question is always which jobs: (a) SHAPE -- folders, sub-folders, job counts by type (file watcher / placement / trust / other), and the datasets inferred from the sub-folder ladder; (b) IDENTITY -- distinct FID, RUN_AS, SEAL and application values with the jobs carrying each; (c) VARIABLES -- every declared name by scope with its distinct-value count, reference count, and its R30/R31 state inline, so the census and the defect list are one table and not two the reader has to join by hand; (d) CONTACTS -- every EMAIL_DL_* value and every DOMAIL destination found, split by contact kind (support tier vs Production Delay Notification consumer) and labelled documentation-only, since R40 now deletes the block that would have used them; (e) INVOCATIONS (merged from Idea-140, 2026-08-19) -- distinct invoked script paths derived from cmd_line, each with its JOB FAN-OUT (how many jobs share the wrapper) and, for every SHARED wrapper, which parameters/variables VARY per job -- the identity-grade candidates. Motivation: on the Informatica platform the invoked .ksh wrappers are the same generic few for ALL business applications (SME 2026-08-19), so script-path identity distinguishes nothing, and the G12 wrapper-payload family (Ab Initio/DPL: kind-scoped token, path never identity) likely needs a third kind -- WHICH parameter is the token is a LINEAGE-GATE ruling this census must inform, never make. A wrapper with fan-out 1 is reported too: one-to-one wrappers are the evidence that script-path identity IS sufficient for that kind, which is as decision-relevant as the converse. Then the half the census cannot produce: a SUBSTITUTION SLOT list -- the facts the XML does not carry and only the SME can supply (DEVX_KEY, the MFTS set FTS_ID / REC_ID / USER / DELIVERY_MECHANISM, EMAIL_DL_L2 / L3 / PDN, SOURCE_CONTACT). Each slot names its current value or records it ABSENT, its vocabulary or shape rule from the guidelines page, and the jobs it would apply to. A slot with no current value is "not supplied", NEVER a default: inventing one is how a proposal becomes a wrong fact nobody re-checks. The profile ASSERTS NOTHING about meaning -- it is a census, findings stay detect_all()'s output and ride alongside, and nothing here ratifies or writes a graph (the module's standing invariant). Committed fixtures are synthetic, since real FIDs, SEALs and DLs are Internal. The TRANSPORT is named in the item's commit rather than defaulted, per the O58 precedent: a CLI verb writing a JSON artifact is the recommended first pass, because remediation writes no graph (so QuerySpecs are out by construction) and no upload path exists yet -- but if an API endpoint is chosen instead, the commit body records the choice and its cost against ADR 0005.

XmlDefinitionFormat.dump() still raises pending the vendor schema, and the profile plus the SME's substitutions are a PROPOSAL, which is what the equivalence proof already consumes. A live legacy-LOB folder shows the FileWatcher job running as the Control-M platform account while the folder default runs as the application account — job-grain class split that a flat run_as census would blur into "two accounts". The FileWatcher x platform-account pairing is the designed pattern; a payload job on the platform account is the finding. TRANSPORT NAMED, per the item's O58 clause: a CLI verb `drydocs profile-folder-set <export-dir> -o <json>` writing a JSON artifact. Cost against ADR 0005 is NIL rather than merely acceptable — that ADR governs the browser-to-Neo4j access path, and this reads no graph and writes none; QuerySpecs were out by construction, not by preference; and changedoc.py/jira.py are the existing artifact-writing precedent in this component, so the shape is not new.
