G69R41-R44: the four fan-out defect classes get their registry entries and their detectors in the SAME change, so neither can exist without the other
drydocs-remediationP6taskp2opus / main
component-topology
depends on: C32

Acceptance: Four defect classes C32 observed with no rule to hold them are registered AND detected in one change. The pairing is the item: the registry is the single source for both the validate gate and the greenfield gate, so a detector with no entry emits findings nothing can rank, nothing can turn into a fix, and -- the real problem -- nothing can SIGN OFF on. The entry is the thing that gets ratified. (a) R41 DUPLICATE DECLARATION IN ONE SCOPE -- one name declared twice in the same container with different values. Live: RPATH twice in one folder, a relative path and an absolute one. Severity must-fix, not should-fix: which value wins is an ordinal accident, so the job runs against whichever declaration happens to be last, and the reader of the folder sees both and cannot tell. (b) R42 FOLDER-NAME DELIMITER DRIFT -- one folder set mixing separators between the same positional fields, so a SQL parse splitting on the delimiter returns different field counts per folder. Live: two folders of one set using an underscore where their siblings use a hyphen. This is the rule whose finding must name the PARSE consequence, not the cosmetic one. (c) R43 CARRIER COLLISION -- one name resolved by two different resolvers in one command line: a Control-M %%VAR beside a shell ${VAR}. THE ENTRY MUST RULE WHICH CARRIER OWNS THE NAME BEFORE THE DETECTOR SHIPS, because the greenfield action differs completely by answer -- rename one carrier, or declare the shell export -- and a detector that fires without that ruling produces findings no one can act on. If the ruling is not available, R43 is registered status OPEN with no detector and the item says so; it does NOT ship a detector against an undecided rule. (d) R44 STALE AUTHORED PROVENANCE -- an authored "created by" field that travelled with a copied job, so it names the template's author rather than the job's. Detectable as one value across jobs whose independent audit trail names different users. Advisory severity, and the finding must say what to read INSTEAD (the creation/modification audit fields), since the value is not wrong so much as answering a different question. All four land status PROVISIONAL and emit ratified=False, per the module rule that only ratified rules may change a definition. Each gets its entry in the existing registry shape (check / engine / severity / status / source / greenfield action), a detector in the conformance pass, and a case in the drifted fixture -- with the greenfield fixture still raising ZERO findings, which is the assertion that the standard stays reachable. Suite green, ruff clean, publish-boundary clean.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) at SME request, immediately after C32 listed the four classes and deliberately did not build them. THE REASON THIS IS ITS OWN ITEM RATHER THAN A WIDENING OF G67: G67 shipped R30-R40 as a closed set with a signed-off shape. Adding rules to it means either reopening a done item or quietly growing it, and the second is exactly how a rule set stops matching the registry that is supposed to govern it -- the failure the pairing rule exists to prevent, committed by the change that implements the pairing rule. SCOPE DISCIPLINE, stated because three of these are easy and one is not: R41, R42 and R44 are mechanical and would ratify quickly. R43 is a genuine question about which carrier owns a name, and its answer changes what a fix even looks like. Do not let the three easy ones carry the hard one over the line -- shipping R43 as provisional-with-detector when the ownership question is open would put a finding in front of an SME that has no defensible action attached to it. NOT IN SCOPE: ratifying any of them. That is the HITL gate's, and it wants real findings from a real folder set rather than fixture hits -- which is what G68's profile run produces. The governance walk-through these four are the worked example of lives in drydocs_remediation/overview_readme.md. DONE 2026-08-25 (desktop, same session as G68). Registered AND detected in one change — except R43, and THAT IS THE ITEM'S OWN INSTRUCTION rather than a shortfall. THE R43 CALL, made on evidence not convenience: the acceptance says ship no detector unless the carrier-ownership question is ruled, so it was searched for — the governance corpus, the guidelines page and the gate prompts carry NOTHING on shell-vs-Control-M carrier ownership. So R43 lands `status: OPEN` with no detector, is absent from CONFORMANCE_RULE_IDS, and a test PINS both — the scope-discipline clause working as designed, because the three mechanical rules were exactly the pressure that would have carried the hard one over the line. R43's entry also records what it is NOT: R33 is one FACT carried by both a literal and a variable; R43 is one NAME resolved by two engines. Different question, different fix. R41 (must-fix): duplicate declaration in one scope with DIFFERENT values — a repeat of the same value is noise. The message names the ORDINAL ACCIDENT, which is the severity's justification: the job runs against whichever declaration is last and a reader sees both. The detector walks the RAW layer definitions and a test pins that, because `_declared` resolves the chain into a dict and would make the rule structurally unable to fire. R42 (should-fix): cross-folder, over the folder list; a set of one cannot disagree with itself. The finding names the PARSE consequence — mixed separators do not make the split FAIL, they make it return a different field count, so the positional read silently lands on the wrong field. ONE finding however many delimiters break, since it is one defect in the set's naming. R44 (advisory): one authored value spanning jobs, message pointing at the creation/modification AUDIT fields. THE HONEST LIMIT IS IN THE MESSAGE AND THE ENTRY, not left to be discovered: the rule as written wants the value standing against an independent audit trail, that trail is a DB-side feed a definition export does not carry, so the detector reports the pattern and says it cannot confirm it. That gap is why the rule is advisory. SCOPE NOTE, stated because it went past the item's named inputs: R44 had NO FEED. Nothing in the XML extractor, the bridge protocol or JobDefinition carried an authored field, so the detector would have been decoration — which is the same failure the pairing rule exists to prevent, read from the other side. It was plumbed end to end (xml_vocab.AUTHORED_BY_ATTRS -> XmlJobRecord -> StagedJob -> JobDefinition) as a SYNONYM SET rather than one spelling, because the authoritative element schema is still unacquired and that is exactly the treatment DESCRIPTION and POSTCMD already get. FIXTURES: the drifted XML gains one case per shipped rule — a name declared twice with two values, a sibling folder separating the same positional fields with the other character, and one authored value on two jobs. The R42 folder is deliberately EMPTY so it adds an R42 case and disturbs no other rule's expectations. The greenfield fixture still raises ZERO findings, which is the assertion that the standard stays reachable. TESTS: 9 new (27 in the file). Three mutations checked — and the SECOND ONE FOUND A REAL GAP: making R44 fire on a SINGLE job passed, because the greenfield fixture carries no authored value at all and was therefore clean by OMISSION rather than by the rule. The test now asserts on sets that do carry one (lone job = no finding, shared value = finding, distinct values = no finding) and the mutation is caught. NOT RATIFIED, and nothing here tries to be: all four are PROVISIONAL emitting ratified=False, and the HITL gate wants real findings from a real folder set — which is what G68's profile run, landed in this same session, now produces. The governance walk-through in overview_readme.md gains these four as its worked example, written around the R43 split rather than the three easy ones. Publish-boundary clean: no live folder, path, variable or user string from the C32 capture reached committed code or fixtures (swept explicitly). Suite 2481 passed / 10 skipped, ruff clean, CLI gates green.

G75Back-flow the two homeless Control-M parsing mechanisms the company adapter carries: BMC compact-timestamp normalization and the PL-/PG- condition-scope rule
drydocs-coreP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: Two pure functions the company's controlm_xml_adapter.py carries and the producer has NO equivalent of (verified 2026-08-11 by search, not assumed) land in drydocs_core/orchestration/controlm/ as mechanism, with the reasoning that makes each one correct written down rather than reconstructed later. (a) BMC COMPACT-TIMESTAMP NORMALIZATION. A BMC XML export stamps audit times as YYYYMMDDHHMMSS optionally suffixed with a zone token (UTC / Z / +hhmm) -- a form Neo4j datetime() cannot parse. The port must preserve all four decisions, because each one is a failure mode someone already hit: UTC and Z both normalize to Z while a NUMERIC offset is kept verbatim; an 8-digit date-only value becomes midnight; a value that is NOT the compact BMC form is HANDED THROUGH UNTOUCHED (the Oracle projections already deliver "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" and the loaders' Cypher handles the space->T itself); and anything else unparseable returns None so the loaders' existing null-guard drops ONE ROW rather than a malformed string reaching the driver and aborting the whole load. That last clause is the one worth a test of its own -- it is the difference between a bad row and a dead load. (b) CONDITION SCOPE FROM THE NAME PREFIX. PL- = LOCAL (resolves within the emitting folder's DATACENTER) and PG- = GLOBAL (resolves across DCs by name), anything else UNKNOWN. The consequence is the part that must survive: two LOCAL conditions sharing a name in different data centers are DISTINCT, so any key derived from a condition name is incomplete without the data center, and UNKNOWN must stay a returned value rather than a raised error. Both are pure, both get unit tests covering every branch including the pass-through and the None, and neither writes a graph. NO company values: the two prefixes are a documented BMC naming convention, not internal data, and the docstrings cite the capture rather than quoting a real condition or pool name. THE THIRD MECHANISM IS DISPOSITIONED, NOT BUILT. The company adapter's folder pseudo-job (JOBISN=1, so folder-level PL-<folder>-OK OUTCONDs attach to a real node instead of dangling) is a LOADER idiom and needs a graph-write context the producer does not have -- there is no producer XML-to-graph adapter to put it in. It is recorded in the reconcile-port divergence ledger with its trigger (the first producer-side loader that models folder-level conditions), per J39's disposition rule. Recording it is the deliverable; building it here would mean inventing the caller.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) at SME request, from the 19-screenshot capture of the company's three XML processors. WHY THESE TWO AND NOT THE ADAPTER: the adapter itself is the wrong base and the capture says why -- it encodes the description-token model C30 retired (INBOUND_ROUTE / OUTBOUND_ROUTE, ENV in its transfer-instance meaning, PDN_SNOW_QUEUE), it flattens the C30 scope ladder into one dict per job, and its FOLDER_ORDER_METHOD filter skips manual-order folders, which is right for a live-graph load mirroring the Oracle USER_DAILY IS NOT NULL filter and WRONG for a conformance pass, where hand-built and inactive folders are the whole drift population. That is not theoretical: the SME's own 22-job export carries no FOLDER_ORDER_METHOD, so the adapter would skip the folder entire while the lineage extractor stages all 22 jobs. So the adapter is scaffold, per the SME's framing -- "use it for the scaffold not the goal, ontology and mapping have changed" -- and these two functions are the parts that are mechanism rather than ontology, correct whatever era they came from, and currently reachable only through a module we are declining to adopt.

G76Reproduce the Quantitative Resource pool classifier producer-side as a mechanism/values twin: the grammar and the ordered rule table are ours, the pool vocabulary is not
drydocs-coreP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A producer drydocs_core/orchestration/controlm/resource_pool.py reproducing the company classifier's MECHANISM with its vocabulary supplied as DATA. A QUANTITATIVE element on a job declares that the job consumes N slots from a named pool, and pool names follow <APP_CODE>-<SUBSYSTEM>[-<MODIFIER>]*-<KIND>; the classifier parses that into a frozen PoolClassification (name, category, app_code, subsystem, kind_suffix, secondary_label) with no I/O. THE SPLIT IS THE ITEM. The company module compiles its vocabulary into the source -- the match regexes name real target-database, controller, distribution and host tokens, and the app-code regex hardcodes a real two-letter prefix. Those are Internal and may not land in the repo. The producer copy carries the grammar, the classification contract and an EMPTY or synthetic rule table, with the real table loaded from config (the values twin lives under internal/). A test proves the module classifies correctly against a synthetic table and returns unknown for everything when the table is empty -- which is also the honest default for a repo that does not have the vocabulary. THREE PROPERTIES ARE LOAD-BEARING AND MUST SURVIVE THE REWRITE, each with its own test: (a) RULE ORDER IS CORRECTNESS, NOT STYLE. Rules are first-match-wins and one of them matches a token ANYWHERE in the name, so it must be evaluated after the more specific ones -- a pool that satisfies both reads as the earlier category. A config table must therefore be an ORDERED SEQUENCE; a mapping keyed by category would silently lose the ordering and the loss would be invisible until a misclassified pool reached the graph. (b) unknown IS A FIRST-CLASS OUTCOME, NOT AN ERROR. It returns with secondary_label None so the loader adds no label and logs a WARN, which is how misses surface in CI. Same aliases-suggest / values-decide discipline the FACT_REGISTRY next door follows. classify() always returns, including on empty and whitespace input. (c) A SPECULATIVE CATEGORY STAYS LABELLED SPECULATIVE. The company's business_app fallback has never fired -- its own comment says "None observed yet, but reserve the slot so the contract is complete". Carry the branch WITH that honesty or drop it; keeping the branch and losing the comment ships a never-observed category as though it were evidence. One inconsistency is RULED here rather than copied blind: subsystem and kind_suffix are both derived from the same token split, so a two-token name yields the same token in both fields. Decide whether that is intended and say so in the docstring; do not reproduce it silently. No graph writes; the loader-side CONSUMES_FROM_POOL edge and the five secondary labels are NOT in scope -- the labels are an ontology decision and go through the HITL gate, not a back-flow. This item ships the classifier and its contract only.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) at SME request, from a complete 130-line capture the SME supplied specifically so this could be reproduced. The module has NO producer counterpart, and neither does controlm_quantitatives.py, which consumes it -- verified by path check. WHY IT IS WORTH REPRODUCING WHEN THE ADAPTER IS NOT: this one is a parser plus a lookup table, and the era problem that disqualifies the adapter does not apply -- pool-name grammar is not the description-token model and did not change at C30. It also gives a SECOND, INDEPENDENT platform signal: C32 established that a quantitative pool names the target platform separately from the job name, so the two cross-check, and a job whose name and pool disagree is a finding neither source could raise alone. That is the standing use for it, and it is why the classifier is worth having before the loader edge exists. The company docstring cites a company-side path for its design rationale, so the producer copy needs its own written warrant rather than a dangling citation.

G77One theme vocabulary, two corpora: dcat:theme on the Control-M folder block AND the scraped-document envelope, joined by concept IRI

Acceptance: One vocabulary classifies BOTH corpora -- that is the point, and it is what ties the structured estate to the unstructured one. (a) CONTROL-M, folder scope: a THEME token inside the DD1| folder block (guidelines section 7.5), registered in TOKEN_REGISTRY like any other token, multi-valued on the documented inner separator, values checked against the concept scheme with an unrecognised value RETURNED as a finding rather than raised -- the standing aliases-suggest / values-decide discipline. This is the folder-level block C29 originally intended for a Data Series roll-up that was never commonly defined. (b) SCRAPED DOCUMENTS: the same field on the document metadata envelope. The two-corpus architecture already rules that the vendor and Confluence corpora stay EPISTEMICALLY SEPARATE and merge only through a shared metadata envelope -- a theme is exactly such a field, which is why it fits rather than being bolted on. THE DISCIPLINE THAT MUST BE WRITTEN DOWN OR SOMEONE WILL BUILD PAST IT: the join is at the CLASSIFICATION, never the content. A document and a folder sharing a theme are both ABOUT that subject; that is not an assertion that the document describes the folder, and no edge may imply it. Trust tiers do not merge because two things share a subject. (c) The unclassified / out-of-scope split from C34 (c) is implemented on the scraper side, where it actually bites, and coverage reports the two apart. (d) Joined by CONCEPT IRI, never by label -- so this item works unchanged under one database or two, and label drift between corpora cannot fork the join. Zero graph writes: the field, its validation and the coverage split. The edge waits on C34.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 with C34, same session. Depends on C34 because a theme field populated against an undeclared scheme is free text with a schema-shaped name. DELIBERATELY NOT RAISED YET: the SME-facing classification UI, which the session described as possibly two pages. Building a classification surface before C34 rules residency and the Product-vs-Concept typing is the O59 mistake in a new place -- a widget built against a shape that turns out otherwise is thrown away. It grooms once C34 signs, and the two-page question then answers itself from the residency ruling rather than from taste. RAISED AT THE 2026-08-12 GROOM, and the reason depends_on grew: clause (a) reads a THEME token "inside the DD1| folder block", and nothing in the parser knows what that block is. G84 builds the block gate; this item registers a token on top of it. Without the dependency, two sessions implement the same sentinel differently in one file. DONE 2026-08-21 (desktop; sample-reproducible, zero graph writes). ONE READER FOR BOTH CORPORA: new drydocs_core/ontology/concept_scheme.py loads the lob-product-team `concept_scheme` block (C34 (a)) and mints concept IRIs in the gate's confirmed §A2 form `urn:drydocs:scheme:lob-product-team#<notation>` (17 concepts over the three tiers; dev_teams excluded per not_concepts); `resolve()` accepts a full IRI or a bare notation and NEVER a label (d); `resolve_all()` RETURNS unrecognised values; `broader_closure()` is the parent_* link read as skos:broader. (a) CONTROL-M: `THEME` TokenSpec in TOKEN_REGISTRY — multivalued on ';', `concept_scheme=` field on TokenSpec drives resolution in the parse loop, unknown values land as VALUE_NOT_IN_VOCABULARY findings. Registered under a NEW `JobType.FOLDER` plus a new `optional` flag: FOLDER never matches a job-level `_registry_for`, and `required_tokens()` skips optional — so the watcher/publisher required sets and the G83 registry-vs-standard agreement test are untouched, and a tagged folder without THEME is pending, not a defect. `ParsedDescription.theme_iris()` + `theme_coverage()` (classified / unclassified / unread reported apart). (b) SCRAPED DOCUMENTS: `PageRecord.themes` (IRIs) + `theme_status` on the docmeta capture manifest; `CaptureManifest.build(themes=…)` resolves at capture, drops what does not resolve, `theme_findings()` surfaces it; pre-G77 manifests read as unclassified (round-trip guarded). (c) `ThemeStatus` = classified | unclassified | out_of_scope decided ONCE in `theme_status()`: an External source is out of scope permanently whatever its theme field says; `CaptureManifest.theme_coverage()` reports the three apart and `ratio` = classified ÷ in-scope. THE DISCIPLINE is written in three places (concept_scheme docstring, description_tokens docstring, guidelines §7.5 new THEME paragraph): the join is at the classification, never the content; no edge follows from a shared theme; trust tiers do not merge. G78A load step that cannot find its input MUST FAIL — today it silently skips, and a default run loads synthetic fixtures while reporting success
drydocs-loadP6bugp0opus / main
component-topology

Acceptance: TWO DEFECTS, one failure. (1) A chain step whose expected input file is absent logs "No sample for ..., skipping" and the run reports SUCCESS. (2) refresh-reference's only input option is --samples-dir, which DEFAULTS to the bundled fixture directory, so a run with no arguments loads synthetic rows into a real graph and calls it done. Together they produce the worst outcome available: not a failed load, a load that SUCCEEDED with the wrong data -- the confidently-wrong-row class promoted to the load. REPRODUCED ON BOTH SIDES, not theorised. Producer: REFRESH_REFERENCE_CHAIN expects seal_application_data__sample.csv and seal_contact_data__sample.csv and NEITHER EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THIS REPO (find returns nothing), so the SEAL half of the reference load has never run on bundled fixtures and nothing has ever said so. Company-side: the same skip dropped dev_teams, and a real-data run silently loaded fixtures instead (SME session 2026-08-11). FIX, in three parts: (a) A missing REQUIRED input FAILS the step, naming the file and the path searched. A step may declare an input optional; optional then means written down, not inferred from a file's absence. (b) Real runs stop defaulting to the fixture directory. Production data must not have to be named *_sample.csv in a directory called samples to be loadable -- that is a semantic contradiction the operator is currently forced into. Implement the interface the TDDs ALREADY DESCRIBE and neither side built: --source <source-id> resolving its location from config/source-registry.yaml, with --samples-dir retained for fixtures only. THE CORRECT BEHAVIOUR IS ALREADY IN THE REPO, ONE VERB AWAY, and this clause is closer to making two commands agree than to designing an interface (SME-confirmed 2026-08-11: "--csv works fine changing to a different path"). `drydocs load <name> --csv <path>` takes an ARBITRARY path -- no directory convention, no filename convention, no fixture default -- and when neither --csv nor --sql is given it PRINTS AND EXITS 2 rather than guessing. It also runs the confirmed-gate before any write. So the defect is not "loaders cannot take a path"; it is that the SEQUENCED chain verb behaves worse than the manual verb beside it. Copy the single-loader contract up into the chain: explicit path or fail, never a plausible default. Do NOT rebuild what `load` already does correctly. (c) The run summary states, per step, WHICH path it read and how many rows it loaded, so "it succeeded" is falsifiable at a glance. (d) COVERAGE RIDER, merged from Idea-119 at the 2026-08-13 groom and scoped to this item's own blast radius: the loaders whose step contract this change touches gain a DIRECT test import. FIVE have none today -- drydocs/loaders/business_segments.py, controlm.py, controlm_dependencies_derived.py, controlm_hosts.py and seal_contacts.py (A5 measured 2026-08-13 at bb9788b6: 31 package modules with no direct test import, of which these five are loaders). A test that imports the loader and exercises the missing-input path satisfies this clause and the guard below at once. NOT a general coverage sweep: five named files, because the tests belong with the fix that touches them. Guard: a test proves a chain step with a missing required input FAILS BY NAME, and that a run against the fixture directory is distinguishable in the summary from a run against a declared source.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) from a company-side diagnosis the SME relayed, then reproduced producer-side. p0 because it is silent, it is live on both machines, and every downstream claim about what the graph contains rests on it. Independent of the naming epic -- this is correctness, that is generalization; do not couple them. THERE IS A WORKING ESCAPE HATCH TODAY, and an operator blocked on this should be told rather than left waiting for the fix: `drydocs load <name> --csv <arbitrary path>` loads a single loader from any location, gated, with no fixture fallback. It is per-loader rather than per-chain, so a full reference load is several invocations, but it is CORRECT where the chain verb is not. That also bounds the item: the contract to copy already exists and is one verb away, so this is two commands being made to agree, not an interface to design. MERGED 2026-08-13 (targeted groom) from Idea-119, whose own proposed disposition was to fold the five untested loaders into this item rather than file a coverage sweep. Read A5 for what it is: a DIRECT-IMPORT proxy, so fixture-driven and subprocess coverage do not show in it. Clause (d) therefore asks for an import-bearing test on the path this item changes, not for proof that a loader was untested in every sense. STANDING DIVERGENCE FOUND WHILE CONFIRMING IT, and it is load-bearing for any shared fixture: the producer convention is DOUBLE underscore (catalog_lobs__sample.csv), the company convention is SINGLE (catalog_lobs_sample.csv) -- confirmed by the SME. The same file therefore cannot serve both sides, and a file copied across is silently skipped rather than rejected. Record it in the port-prompt divergence ledger at this item. DONE 2026-08-21 (desktop). New drydocs/chain_inputs.py (load; pure path resolution): a chain's every input is resolved BEFORE the first write. (a) A missing REQUIRED file raises MissingChainInputError naming step, file and the directory searched, for every missing step at once, with the way out (build_seal_samples.py for the generated SEAL fixtures); the verb exits 2 and never opens the graph (guarded: the patched _client is not called). Optional = written down on the ChainStep, never inferred. (b) refresh-reference has NO default any more: --samples-dir <dir> = FIXTURE run, --source <id> (repeatable) = REAL run reading <step>.csv from the source's declared landing zone (config/source-registry.yaml acquisition.drop_dir under DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT, via drydocs_core.landing_zones -- the interface ADR 0012 / N12 already declared); steps bound to an unselected source are reported NOT SELECTED (an operator's written choice, not a missing file); no mode / both modes / unknown source = exit 2 with the declared zones named. `load --csv` untouched -- its contract was copied up, not rebuilt. ingest-controlm keeps its bundled default because sample mode IS its documented mode (the e2e chain and runbooks run it; the real run is --use-oracle, not a different directory) but now prints a FIXTURE RUN banner and preflights every stage by name. (c) The closing table: step | mode (fixture / source:<id>) | path read | rows | rejected, plus NOT LOADED rows with the reason -- a fixture run and a source run are distinguishable at a glance. (d) tests/unit/test_chain_inputs.py (14) imports business_segments, controlm (re-export module), controlm_dependencies_derived, controlm_hosts and seal_contacts and exercises the missing-input path for each loader class. Divergence recorded in the reconcile-port ledger: producer double-underscore vs company single-underscore fixture names, and why the resolver must not be loosened back to a skip. repo-README + MODULE_MAP updated. Suite 2274 passed. G81 (paths declared in config, the overlap invariant, no silent data root) is the sibling one layer down and per its own notes is planned with the architect persona alongside G79 -- not picked up here. DISCHARGED 2026-08-27 (laptop, G121): the "`load --csv` untouched" caveat above is closed. The verb now resolves its path through data_zones.read_zone_containing(): a declared read zone loads and the run record names the zone; an undeclared path exits 2 naming landing-zones, unless --allow-unzoned is passed, and that override is recorded in the run record and the disk log (flag, path, operator). Guarded by tests/unit/test_load_csv_acquisition.py.

G79Split refresh-reference by SOURCE — one command per subject, and wire the two loaders that belong to no chain at all
drydocs-loadP6taskp1opus / main
component-topology
depends on: G78

Acceptance: refresh-reference bundles SEVEN loaders across THREE unrelated sources with different natural refresh cadences. That bundle has no organising principle, which is why a loader can fall out of it and nothing notices. Split it so each command covers ONE source. (a) The split, by subject rather than by chain accident: the product catalog tier (catalog LOBs, product lines, products), the organisation tier (dev teams, team roles), and the business-application tier (applications, contacts). These are SEPARATE COMMANDS even where two share a source system, because the SME's cadence argument is per subject: business applications are not created daily, the operational estate can be. (b) WIRE THE TWO ORPHANS. pat_team_roles is gate-confirmed (C9, 2026-07-18), has a loader class and cypher, is reachable as `drydocs load pat_team_roles` -- and belongs to NO chain and NO profile, so no operator path has ever run it. area_products is in the same state. Either wire each into its subject command or record a written reason it is excluded; the one thing not allowed is the current silence. area_products has a plausible reason ready to be written down (lob-product-team.yaml records area_products: 0 with the standing area-product-missing open question); pat_team_roles has none that this item could find. (c) Cadence moves OFF the hand-assigned profile tuples and ONTO the source registry entry, so load_profile() DERIVES its steps by filtering on cadence instead of reading a literal maintained by hand. This is what makes "the source dictates how often it refreshes" true in code rather than true in a comment. (d) Acquisition mode joins it on the registry entry (file-drop | db-pull | api-pull | repo | scrape), so the anticipated CSV-to-database move for business-application data is a registry edit plus an adapter swap, with the loader, the command name, the sequence position and the cadence all unchanged. (e) PRESERVE ONE LOAD-ORDER INVARIANT ACROSS THE SPLIT, and state it where the split happens: seal_applications loads BEFORE any loader that can mint a :BusinessApplication. Producer satisfies it today by accident of chain order rather than by declaration, and the split is exactly when an accident gets lost. Producer is additionally safe because pat_product_mapping.cypher MERGEs on the SAME neutral app_id key seal_applications uses -- so no stub, no second node, no ordering dependency. The company is NOT safe: pat_app_links.cypher still MERGEs on the pre-S3 seal_id with is_stub=true, mints a null-app_id node the uniqueness constraint cannot match, and the subsequent SET collides (SME hit it live 2026-08-11; RELAY-8, a T23 residue). Once commands are keyed to sources, the constraint is expressible as a declared dependency rather than a position in a tuple -- state it that way, so the next reorder cannot silently break it. NAMING IS DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE -- this item splits and wires using CURRENT names. Renaming is GN1/GN2 and is frozen-and-ported as one unit; doing both at once makes an already wide port surface unreviewable.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) on SME direction. Depends on G78 because splitting a chain that silently skips its inputs just gives you more places to skip silently. The SME asked whether product and org structure can be separate commands while sharing sources -- yes, and that is the point: the COMMAND is keyed to the subject, the SOURCE is a property of the data, and two subjects may legitimately draw on one source system. What must not happen is the reverse, which is what exists now: one command spanning three sources, so nothing can say whether the command is complete. RIDER NOTE 2026-08-13 (targeted groom, from Idea-119): two of the five loaders named in G78 clause (d) are ones THIS split re-homes -- seal_contacts (a REFRESH_REFERENCE_CHAIN member) and business_segments (refreshed inside the same command, ahead of the chain tuple). If G78's coverage clause has not closed by the time this runs, the tests move WITH the loaders into their new subject command rather than being left pointing at a command that no longer exists. DONE 2026-08-23 (laptop), on branch feat/g79-source-split, merged --no-ff. (a) THE SPLIT: three subject commands replace the seven-loader bundle -- refresh-catalog (LOB -> product line -> product), refresh-applications (SEAL apps + contacts), refresh-teams (dev teams, team roles, team<->app alignment). pat_product_mapping was not named by any tier in the acceptance; it went to TEAMS because its subject is which team is aligned to which application, an org fact that merely cites product ids, and it stays last as it always was. business_segments re-homed to refresh-catalog: it is a read-only COUNT, not a loader, and catalog_lobs reconciles LOBs to those corporate segments, so it is that reconciliation's precondition. ONE runner behind all three -- the G78 contract is identical; only the subject differs. New cli.CHAINS is the single registry every enumeration derives from (COMMAND_LOADERS, the load-map render's declared-input walk, the chain-binding and bundled-fixture guards), so the NEXT split is one edit rather than four. (b) pat_team_roles IS WIRED and, for the first time in its existence, HAS RUN: verified live on the LAPTOP, bolt://localhost:7687 db=drydocs -- `refresh-teams --samples-dir drydocs/data/samples` loaded 6 rows, 0 rejected, and the graph now holds the full G91 shape (DevTeam -[:QUALIFIED_ATTRIBUTION]-> Attribution -[:HAD_ROLE]-> Role, -[:HAS_AGENT]-> Employee) for all six. Wiring it needed a bundled fixture, which did not exist -- added, six synthetic rows using team ids from the dev_teams sample and role ids from the seeded PAT role vocabulary (force-added; drydocs/data/ is gitignored and the other 13 samples are tracked the same way). area_products stays OUT with its reason rewritten to stand on the standing `area_products: 0` open question rather than on "G79 will decide", which is now false. G80's hygiene guard did exactly its job here -- excluded-AND-chained is contradictory -- so wiring the orphan FORCED its stale excuse to be deleted. (c) load_profile() DERIVES. LoadStep.profiles is a declared set OR the DERIVED sentinel; step_profiles() resolves DERIVED by reading the CADENCE of the command's sources through CADENCE_PROFILES. `cadence: weekly|batch|repo-change` is a new dataset-row field on the nine rows a standing sequenced loader reads (derived from the sequence, never hand-listed, so a new chain fails the guard until its source declares a rhythm); values are RECORDED, not invented -- each is the rhythm the chain comments and command help already stated. THE DIVERGENCE RULE: a command whose sources disagree about cadence RAISES rather than picking one, surfacing a ruling the SME owes at the moment it first matters -- something a hand-assigned tuple structurally could not do. Proven by the contract test: flipping a cadence in a FIXTURE registry moves refresh-catalog between operator surfaces with zero edit to the package. SCHEDULED_INGEST_EXCLUSIONS shrank by one: a cadence-derived omission needs no prose entry, because the registry field is the reason and a reader can check it. (d) SATISFIED BY N12, NOT REBUILT -- a correction, not a scope change. This clause was written 2026-08-11 and asked for `file-drop|db-pull|api-pull|repo|scrape` on the registry entry; N12 landed the same mechanism SME-directed on 2026-08-18 as `acquisition.mode: manual|automated (via api|db)`, guarded, with an explicit framing clause. The clause's PURPOSE -- the CSV-to-database move being a registry edit plus an adapter swap with loader, command name, sequence position and cadence all unchanged -- is exactly N12's mode flip, and that is now true. Re-vocabularying a five-day-old SME-directed field would itself be a rename needing a ruling, so it was not done. (e) The invariant is a DECLARATION with a guard: BUSINESS_APPLICATION_MINTERS + APPLICATION_IDENTITY_LOADER, and a test asserting the identity loader's command precedes every minter's in CANONICAL_LOAD_SEQUENCE (plus hygiene so a stale minter cannot let it pass vacuously). refresh-applications is sequenced before refresh-teams for that reason, stated at the step. The port-prompt's RELAY-8 note got an UPDATE rather than a rewrite: what it verified was true and is now ENFORCED, so producer no longer satisfies the rule by luck. refresh-reference survives as a DEPRECATED ALIAS that delegates to the three (the S8 m1-verify -> verify-reference precedent) and is declared AD_HOC, not a fourth sequence step -- the company's scripts and operator muscle memory name it, and a removed verb fails like a broken install. NAMING stayed out of scope as directed (GN1/GN2). Surfaces regenerated; the runbook's Appendix B names the three commands. Suite 2357 passed. ONE THING FOUND AND NOT FIXED, deliberately: the live run's third step, pat_product_mapping, was REFUSED by the pre-cutover guard -- this laptop's drydocs DB holds 4 :BusinessApplication nodes with a null app_id from before the seal_id -> app_id cutover. That is stale LOCAL GRAPH state on one machine, not a repo defect, and the guard refusing is the guard working (it is the same class the RELAY-8 note describes). Repairing it is a graph decision under the wipe-and-rebuild doctrine, not this item's business. Idea-159 captured separately: four tests in test_repo_paths.py pass in the full suite and fail when that file runs alone (a cli_docs circular import), verified PRE-EXISTING at origin/main while checking whether this split had caused it.

G80The unchained-loader guard: a loader registered but in no chain and no profile fails the suite, and the load map renders it as a defect
drydocs-loadP6taskp1sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: G59 built exactly this guard for SUPPLEMENTS -- unchained_supplement_files() fails when a supplement exists on disk but is absent from the chain. There is NO equivalent for LOADERS, which is why pat_team_roles and area_products sit in LOADER_REGISTRY, reachable by name, belonging to no sequence, with nothing turning red. (a) A guard fails when a loader is registered but appears in no chain and no profile, NAMING the loader rather than reporting a count -- the G59 shape. A deliberate exclusion stays expressible and carries a WRITTEN REASON, the SCHEDULED_INGEST_EXCLUSIONS idiom. (b) The same two facts become defect classes in web/src/generated/load-map.json, beside the sourceless_loaders and map_entries_without_registry_source lists it already carries: unchained loaders, and steps whose declared input is absent (G78's other half). O57 already renders that JSON's defect lists rather than dropping them, so this is what makes the console page an honest inventory instead of a tidy one. (c) Portable: the guard must hold in a consumer repo whose chains legitimately differ -- the company chain carries sub_lobs where the producer carries pat_product_mapping, so a guard that hardcodes producer membership fails there for being right.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop). Dependency-free deliberately: the guard is worth having BEFORE G79 moves loaders between chains, because that is exactly when one goes missing. Same family as G59 and as J47 (no guard asserts a PORT-MANIFEST path exists) -- three instances now of "a thing is declared, nothing checks it is reachable". DONE 2026-08-23 (laptop). (a) cli.unchained_loaders() + UNCHAINED_LOADER_EXCLUSIONS (the G59 shape, computed in the module so a consumer repo guards its OWN chains): a LOADER_REGISTRY loader in no COMMAND_LOADERS chain fails tests/unit/test_load_map_declarations.py BY NAME unless excused in writing. area_products and pat_team_roles are the two written exclusions, both parked on G79 (b) per that item's own clause; the hygiene test makes an exclusion that becomes chained CONTRADICTORY, so G79 must delete them when it wires the orphans. (b) load-map.json (+ the N5 HTML and the O57 console defects tab, DEFECT_COUNT included) gains unchained_loaders (reason-or-null) and steps_with_uncommitted_inputs — the G78 other half at the map grain: chain-declared files that are not repo content. The generated SEAL fixtures are declared PRESENCE-INDEPENDENT (cli.GENERATED_SAMPLE_FILES, keys derived from drydocs.seal_samples) so the committed render cannot flap between a machine that has built them and one that has not; paths are repo-relative for the same reason. (c) The firing test uses a synthetic orphan injected into the registry, never a pinned producer membership. The pre-existing console guard (tests/unit/test_load_map_console.py) caught the two new JSON keys exactly as designed and now routes them. Suite 2332 passed; web tsc build green.

G81DATA LOSS: every path the system reads or writes must be DECLARED in configuration with a mode, and no write path may contain a read path
drydocs-coreP6bugp0opus / main
component-topology

Acceptance: INCIDENT, 2026-08-11: the SME's internal folder holding extracted CSV source data was OVERWRITTEN. Recovery is from a backup, so the data is not lost, but the class is live and it fires again the moment the backup is restored to the same place. This is the most severe defect class the repo has produced — every other failure this week was a wrong READ; this one destroyed a source. (a) RECONSTRUCT FIRST, do not guess. Establish what wrote over what, from the code, and record it. The write-capable surface to walk: drydocs_core/data_root.py declares ten-plus path helpers IN PYTHON, several taking create=True so they mkdir, and rua_extracted_dir() names an "extracted" area that a re-run may legitimately rebuild. Reconstruction is part of the deliverable, not a preamble to it — a guard written against a guessed mechanism guards the wrong thing. (b) DECLARE EVERY PATH IN CONFIGURATION, not in code, each carrying a MODE: read (source data the system may NEVER write), write (outputs it owns and may rebuild), scratch (disposable). Three families the SME named, all currently scattered: LOGS (DRYDOCS_LOGDIR, env-only), LOADER INPUT DATA (per source), and REMEDIATION OUTPUT (the greenfield artifact and Jira handoff). Moving the declaration out of Python is the point: today a path is whatever a helper returns, so no reader can enumerate what the system touches, which is why an overlap was invisible until it destroyed something. (c) THE INVARIANT THAT WOULD HAVE PREVENTED IT: no write-mode path may EQUAL OR CONTAIN a read-mode path. Guarded, with the failure naming both paths. This is the whole defect in one sentence and it is mechanically checkable. (d) NO SILENT DEFAULT ROOT. resolve_data_root() falls back to ~/data/DryDocs whenever DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT is unset or empty, so a missing environment variable silently relocates every read and write to a plausible-looking wrong place — the SAME defect family as G78's fixture-directory default, one layer down. An unset root must FAIL, naming the variable. (e) Any path a create=True helper may build is write-mode BY CONSTRUCTION. A read-mode path must be reachable through a helper that cannot create, cannot clean and cannot write. Ties to ADR 0012: a source declaring acquisition file-drop needs a declared location, and that location is read-mode by definition — so (b) supplies what the ADR's acquisition axis assumes exists.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) from an SME incident report. p0 on IRREVERSIBILITY, which is the axis that separates it from G78: a wrong load is re-runnable, a destroyed source directory is recoverable only as far as the last backup, and if that backup had been stale or absent the loss would be permanent. G78 is louder; this one is worse. SME DIRECTION ON SEQUENCING: the layout must be planned with the ARCHITECT PERSONA, and it must be planned WITH the loader restructure rather than after it — G79 moves loaders between chains and ADR 0012 puts acquisition on the source entry, so both touch exactly the paths this item declares. Doing the declaration afterwards means declaring a layout that was just rearranged. The persona review is docs/reviews/persona-python-architect — a layout question, not a graph-modelling one, so the Python architect rather than the Neo4j architect. SCOPE FENCE: this declares paths and guards the overlap. It does not relocate anyone's data — a config change that silently moved a root would be the same class of defect the item exists to close. DONE 2026-08-24 (laptop), branch feat/g81-path-zones, merged --no-ff. (a) RECONSTRUCTION IS THE DELIVERABLE: docs/reviews/g81-data-path-reconstruction.md walks the write-capable surface from the code and MEASURES four live overlaps rather than theorising one -- controlm_xml_dir() resolving EXACTLY to a declared drop zone; rua/extracted/ and rua/incoming/ nested inside the declared `rua/` read zone; and source_dir(), a public arbitrary-parts create-capable helper whose no-argument form is the ROOT, which contains every drop zone. It ranks candidate mechanisms for the incident and deliberately does NOT claim which fired: the machines hold independent data roots and this session cannot see the SME's. The guard forbids the CLASS, so it never depended on identifying the instance. THE ACCEPTANCE'S INVARIANT WAS WIDENED ON THE EVIDENCE, and this is the one place the item's own words were changed: clause (c) says "no write path may EQUAL OR CONTAIN a read path", but TWO of the four findings were read-CONTAINS-write and are invisible in that direction. The guard checks equality and BOTH containment directions. (b) config/data-zones.yaml declares every system-owned zone with a mode (read/write/scratch). Dataset read zones are NOT duplicated -- they are already source-registry acquisition.drop_dir rows (N12), and data_zones.overlaps() JOINS the two files rather than restating one in the other (26 zones checked). data_root.py keeps its helper API so no call site moved, but the helpers are now readers of the declaration. All THREE families the SME named are enumerable: LOGS (zone run-logs), LOADER INPUT DATA (registry drop rows, per source), REMEDIATION OUTPUT (remediation-outgoing + -recommendations). Nuance recorded rather than papered over: the "greenfield artifact / Jira handoff" is a caller-supplied Path in drydocs_remediation/jira.py with NO production caller, read not written -- no path of its own to declare, and inventing a zone would be declaring a layout that does not exist. TWO ZONES NOBODY HAD DECLARED surfaced while walking call sites (cmdline-staging, controlm-api operator config) -- the clearest evidence the file earns its place, since neither was hidden, merely unenumerable. (c) Guarded, names BOTH paths, and PROVEN TO FAIL on each injected shape -- equal, inside, contains, and scratch-counts-as-write (J26). Two DECLARATION CORRECTIONS bring the real tree to zero violations and neither moves a byte (the scope fence): `rua/` narrows to `rua/incoming/`, which is what data_root.py's docstring has said since G19, and the two dpl rows move to `dpl-registry/`. Those had NEVER agreed with the code since N12, so an operator who followed the registry had files nothing read -- a second defect class found by the reconstruction. (d) resolve_data_root() RAISES when DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT is unset or empty; there is no default. DEFAULT_DATA_ROOT survives as the CONVENTIONAL location the error suggests. The unit conftest gives the suite a hermetic tmp root -- sharper than the log fixture's reason: a test resolving the developer's REAL data root could create directories in it. Documented where an operator looks (config/dev-environment.yaml `data:` block, .env.example). Verified live: with the variable unset, `drydocs landing-zones` prints the message and exits 2, and `drydocs --help` still works (nothing resolves the root at import time). (e) Read-zone helpers lost `create` ENTIRELY -- enforced in the signature, not by discipline -- and source_dir(create=True) refuses a target inside any read zone. THE RUNTIME LEG, which the static invariant structurally cannot cover: rua _unpack's `unpack_dir` is caller-supplied, so no comparison of DECLARATIONS can see it -- an operator naming their own extract folder gets it overwritten file by file, since extractall overwrites with no warning and no diff. Refused now on both branches, with a test proving an existing file SURVIVES the refusal. The two archive protections are different guarantees and both are needed: filter="data" polices what is INSIDE the tarball, the refusal polices WHERE it lands. A UX defect found by live-testing my own change and fixed rather than left: the mandatory root presented as a Python TRACEBACK from `drydocs landing-zones` -- the command whose entire purpose is that "my extracts are gone" is a one-command answer, met by an operator already worried about their data. The console script now points at drydocs.cli:run(), which renders both G81 errors as exit 2 (the G78 operator-error code); guarded, because an entry-point revert is silent. SME SEQUENCING HONOURED: planned WITH the loader restructure (G79 landed the same session), not after it. On the ARCHITECT PERSONA direction -- docs/reviews/persona-python-architect-2026-08.md is a CODE-GRAPH review (layering, fan-in, orphans) and rules on no filesystem question, so it neither supported nor contradicted the layout; per the direction the layout plan was therefore WRITTEN DOWN as the record's section 5 rather than left implicit in the diff. SCOPE FENCE HELD: no data was relocated, and DRYDOCS_LOGDIR kept its default -- (d) names the DATA root, and a relocated log is annoying where a relocated data root is destructive. Suite 2381 passed.

G83The C30 ruling never reached the parse contract — the description token registry is two greenfield tokens short and four retired ones long, so a conformant watcher reports seven false findings
drydocs-coreP6bugp1sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: REPRODUCED AT THE GROOM, sample-only -- no database, no machine, so anyone can re-run it (J18). Parse the C30-conformant watcher description "DELIVERY_MECHANISM: MFTS_AGENT | USER: <acct> | FTS_ID: FTS2 | REC_ID: <id>,<id> | SOURCE_CONTACT: <dl>" and validate it as JobType.FILE_WATCHER: SEVEN findings come back on a description that is exactly what the ruled standard requires -- unknown_key on FTS_ID and REC_ID (the two tokens C30 introduced) and missing_required_token on ENV, INBOUND_ROUTE, OUTBOUND_ROUTE, EMAIL_DL_L3 and EMAIL_DL_L2 (the four C30 retired or moved to folder scope). TOKEN_REGISTRY still encodes the C29 capture; C30 ruled the set on 2026-08-11 and only the standards page moved. The module's own docstring promises it is "the single source both the parser and the published register read from, so code and document cannot drift" -- that promise is what broke, and a conformance model that reports conformant jobs as defective is worse than no model, because the findings look authoritative. (a) ADD the greenfield tokens: FTS_ID (watcher; vocabulary FTS1/FTS2/FTS6/FTS7 per the SME ruling carried in C30) and REC_ID (watcher; multi-valued on comma, a SOURCE-SYSTEM REFERENCE feeding dprod:inputPort -- explicitly NOT a route id). (b) DO NOT DELETE THE RETIRED ONES. The deployed estate still carries them and this parser's job is to read what is there: ENV-on-a-watcher, INBOUND_ROUTE, OUTBOUND_ROUTE and PDN_SNOW_QUEUE keep their entries plus a LIFECYCLE MARKER naming the ruling that retired them, so a legacy description parses them as a known-retired token instead of as an unregistered key. Deleting them would silently reclassify real estate data as somebody's private C16 team-local annotation, which is the one reading that governance cannot afford. (c) COMPLETENESS BECOMES ERA-AWARE: required_tokens() must not demand a retired token, so a job authored to C30 validates clean while a legacy job still validates against what it was authored to. The existing route-id exemption for non-MFTS_AGENT mechanisms stays as it is. (d) CONTACTS CHANGED CARRIER, they did not vanish. EMAIL_DL_L2 / EMAIL_DL_L3 are folder-scope documentation under C30, and EMAIL_DL_PDN is a THIRD member the FOLDER_VARIABLES table does not carry at all. Register the three at folder carrier under the C30 spellings and record that the folder-variable twins were spelled L2_EMAIL_DL_NM / L3_EMAIL_DL_NM before the rename, so a live extract authored either way still resolves. (e) RE-POINT THE STANDARD-OF-RECORD line in the docstring at the greenfield standard, with the metadata plan named as the earlier capture rather than deleted, and add a test that asserts the registry and the standard agree on the per-job-type set -- so the next ruling cannot land in prose alone. That test is the deliverable; the registry edit is the easy half. WHAT THIS MUST NOT DECIDE, stated in the acceptance so the evidence is not lost with the entries: marking the route pair retired is NOT an answer to whether the real MFT route id is the numeric form or the MFTS_RT_* string (Idea-104, still the SME's). Keep the note that records the two unreconciled shapes on whichever entry survives. Zero graph writes. Every token stays proposed; no relationship-vocabulary entry is ratified and no property term is bound.

Notes: Raised at the 2026-08-12 groom (desktop) from a cross-check of C30 (done, 2026-08-11) against the code it ruled -- not from an inbox line. WHY IT IS p1 rather than housekeeping: G68 is in next_ready and its folder-set PROFILE reads this contract, so a census run before this lands reports the retired set as missing on every conformant folder and the two new tokens as unknown; and G67's own conformance fixtures ALREADY emit "FTS_ID: FTS2", which the parser today calls unregistered. The drift is therefore live in the test tree, not hypothetical. WHY IT IS A BUG AND NOT A DESIGN QUESTION: C30 is done and SME-ruled, so nothing here decides anything -- the ruling simply never reached the module. The one judgment call is clause (b), retire-in-place versus delete, and it is made here rather than left open because the parser's stated job is reading a 4000-char field as the estate actually filled it. A greenfield standard governs what gets AUTHORED next; it cannot retroactively unwrite ~240K deployed descriptions. PORT CARE: docs/port/port-prompt.md records that description_tokens.py is UNION-MERGED, not wholesale -- producer holds parse_description / required_tokens / validate, the company adapter holds parse_tokens / classify_job_role, and the union survives only because the two name sets do not collide. Do not rename an exported symbol here; add to the registry and the completeness rule instead. SIBLING: G84 edits the same module and the same test file. Both are dependency-free; if both are open, claim them together and land one commit (the G75+G76 batch precedent).

G84Teach the description parser the DD1| sentinel — three disjoint description populations, so legacy prose stops manufacturing tokens and the compliant marker stops being reported as a defect
drydocs-coreP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: REPRODUCED AT THE GROOM, sample-only (J18): parse_description ("DD1|DELIVERY_MECHANISM: MFTS_AGENT | FTS_ID: FTS2") returns an unparseable_segment finding FOR THE MARKER ITSELF -- the parser reports the one thing the standard makes mandatory as a defect. And parse_description("NOTE: rerun after 08:00 | contact: ops team") returns two "tokens" (NOTE, contact) with two unknown_key findings, so legacy waterfall prose is indistinguishable from a legitimate C16 team-local annotation. Guidelines section 7.5 specifies the fix; nothing implements it. (a) ONE CONSTANT, ONE PREDICATE. The marker lives in a single module-level constant and the test is startswith at position 0 -- no strip, no substring search. Section 7.5 gives both reasons and both are load-bearing: a description that QUOTES the convention in prose cannot false-positive, and startswith is the cheapest predicate available to a SQL scan over the whole estate. (b) THE PARSE RESULT CARRIES THE POPULATION -- tagged / generator-literal / untagged -- and the token grammar applies only to the tagged one. The marker itself never becomes a token and never becomes a finding. Untagged is not a defect and must not be reported as one: untagged means unread. (c) THE DIGIT IS A VERSION, NOT A TEMPLATE ID. Parse it as a version and report it, so DD1 and a future DD2 are read side by side through a grammar migration. The module must state that the marker MUST NOT select a job template -- TASKTYPE derived plus the registered JOB_ROLE token do that (section 7.2) -- because spending the version slot on template identity leaves the first grammar change with no way to announce itself. (d) COVERAGE, NOT COMPLIANCE: a helper reports tagged / total over a set of descriptions. The measure of this standard is tagged folders divided by folders, a number that grows, NOT "how much of our metadata is wrong", a number that never closes. Fewer than ten folders carry the standard today; that is a sample, not a shortfall, and the acceptance should not pretend otherwise. (e) FOLDER SCOPE IS DOCUMENTED, NOT ENFORCED. Record in the module why folder scope is preferred -- get_description() is generator-owned, so a tagged block on a GENERATED JOB is overwritten at the next regeneration and the tag does not protect it. The parser reads whatever it is given; the note exists so nobody tags jobs and loses the block. THE FENCE, and it is the reason this item is small: this implements a READ gate over free text and ratifies nothing. Exit (d) is recorded at gate email-dl-contact-point as rider section G6 with a written warrant, and THE GATE STILL RULES IT -- so the marker stays in exactly one constant and a different ruling is a one-line change, not a rewrite. Zero graph writes; every token stays proposed.

Notes: Raised at the 2026-08-12 groom (desktop) from Idea-105, which the 2026-08-11 SME design session resolved on an exit none of its three recorded ones described. THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES: two things claim the same 4000-char DESCRIPTION field -- the DPL generator's literal, which the stub plan's E1 discriminates on an EXACT match, and the company token standard captured at C29. Adding a token block to a generated object breaks E1; requiring the literal leaves the token block nowhere to go. A versioned sentinel PARTITIONS the field instead of choosing between them: the three populations become disjoint, both readers keep working, and NOTHING ALREADY DEPLOYED MIGRATES -- strictly cheaper than losing the metadata where the estate is densest, invalidating E1 on every generated object, or finding a new carrier the generator stamps. IT ALSO RETIRES C29's PROPOSED GENERATED_BY TOKEN, which is why no item mints one: absence of the tag on a literal-match description already IS the provenance signal, so a token asserting it would be a second carrier for one fact. Verified at the groom that TOKEN_REGISTRY never grew one. CONSUMER: G77 clause (a) registers a THEME token INSIDE this block and now depends on this item for that reason. COMPANY RELAY: their copy of the gate prompt is canonical-company and did not take the producer edits, so RELAY-7 carries the rider across. Nothing in this item ports on its own. SIBLING: G83 edits the same module and the same test file -- if both are open, claim them together and land one commit.

G92File-op operands are parsed from RAW shell text, so a variable path and its resolved twin become two different data assets — resolve the job's scope chain before the file-op parse
drydocs-lineageP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology
depends on: G14 G46 G60

Acceptance: REPRODUCED AT THE GROOM, sample-only, no database (J18): the G60 pre/post pass calls parse_command(value) on the RAW variables-CSV var_value, and _file_op keys the asset as asset_id(_FILE_OP_ASSET_KIND, location) from that verbatim operand -- so a job whose POSTCMD moves "%%R_PATH/out.dat" and a job whose CMD_LINE moves "/data/r/out.dat" plan edges to TWO DataAsset nodes for ONE file. The CMD_LINE pass has the same defect; only the pre/post pass makes it visible, because pre/post text is where the variable forms concentrate. (a) RESOLVE, THEN PARSE. The extractor builds the job's folder -> job scope chain and runs the shell text through the ONE resolver (drydocs_core/orchestration/controlm/resolve_layers / resolve_command_line, whose stated guardrail is "no caller may re-implement substitution"), then parses the RESOLVED text. No second substitution engine, no regex twin, no local %%-stripping helper -- a new substitution path in this extractor fails this item outright. (b) RAW STAYS BESIDE RESOLVED, never replaced -- the G46 derived-fact shape. The candidate carries both the verbatim operand and the resolved location, so a wrong binding is auditable rather than baked in. (c) CANONICAL RESIDUE IS NOT A FAILURE. {ODATE}-class tokens survive resolution by design and stay symbolic in the operand; they are counted as EXPECTED residue, distinct from an unresolved user variable, which is counted as a miss. Neither is dropped (the coverage house rule). (d) COUNT THE RESOLUTION QUALITY on the ResolveCoverage precedent (drydocs/cmdline_staging.py): per-run counters for resolved / residue / nothing-to-substitute / no-scope-chain, reported through the existing ExtractCoverage summary line so the yield is measurable in the same place the prepost_* counters already land. (e) SCOPE CHAIN COMES FROM THE SAME CSV the shell text does. The aliased projection carries var_scope (FOLDER | JOB); the raw export does not, and there the folder rows are the header row where JOB_NAME equals the folder name (the drydocs/staging.py is_folder_header rule). Both shapes must feed the chain, and a row with NO resolvable scope chain is counted, never silently parsed raw. ENDPOINTS AND MEANING ARE UNCHANGED: same READS_FROM / WRITES_TO, same ControlMJob -> DataAsset shape from the 2026-07-15/16 gate EDIT, no new relationship type, m3_reads_from / m3_writes_to stay planned. Zero graph writes; a unit test on a sample job proves the resolved and raw spellings of one path converge on ONE asset id.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-12 (targeted groom) from Idea-112, raised working through the G60 result with the user. Verified at the groom rather than taken from the entry: _prepost_pass parses var_value directly (controlm_inventory.py), resolve_layers / resolve_command_line already return each definition's resolved_value plus substitution provenance (G46, done), and PRECMD/POSTCMD are themselves SETVAR definitions -- so the scope chain that resolves the rest of the job resolves them in place. This is a FEED change, not a new parser and not a new resolver, which is why it is sonnet: every semantic decision it depends on was made at G14, G46 and G60. MODULE: drydocs-lineage, chosen because the change point is the extractor's pass; core's resolver is CALLED, not modified. If core turns out to need a public helper for the scope-chain assembly, that is a drydocs-core follow-up item, not a widening of this one. DONE 2026-08-25 (desktop, same session as G97). Built as a FEED change exactly as the notes framed it: no new parser, no new resolver, and no second substitution path. (a) RESOLVE THEN PARSE, through `resolve_command_line` — the one core resolver whose stated guardrail is that no caller may re-implement substitution. The scope chain is built ONCE per run before the jobs pass (`_build_scope_chains`), because the CMD_LINE file-op parse has the same defect the pre/post pass does and needed the same chain; that reordering is the only structural change to `extract()`. (b) RAW BESIDE RESOLVED: the asset is keyed on the RESOLVED location — that is what makes one file one node — and every DISTINCT raw spelling that reached it accumulates in a `raw_operands` property. ACCUMULATED rather than first-seen deliberately: two jobs spelling one path two ways IS the evidence that makes a wrong binding findable, and keeping only the first would hide the second. Raw and resolved ops are paired by parsing both spellings and zipping — sound because substitution replaces values IN PLACE and never adds, removes or reorders statements; where the two parses disagree anyway (a variable holding a whole `;`-separated command would do it) the disagreement is COUNTED and the resolved op travels with no raw twin rather than being paired with the wrong one. (c) RESIDUE IS NOT A MISS: `{ODATE}`-class canonical tokens survive by design and count as expected residue; a user `%%ref` with no binding counts as a miss AND still stages on its raw spelling, because a dropped operand is invisible and a raw one is not. (d) Five counters on the ResolveCoverage precedent ride the existing ExtractCoverage summary line. ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ITEM'S OWN ACCEPTANCE, clause (e). It says the raw export's folder rows are "the header row where JOB_NAME equals the folder name (the drydocs/staging.py is_folder_header rule)". That conflates two real rules in two files: the JOB_NAME = SCHED_TABLE comparison is how drydocs/loaders/sql/controlm_variables.sql DERIVES `var_scope`, while staging.py's `is_folder_header` falls back to the JOB_ID = 1 smart-folder heuristic when `var_scope` is absent. Both were implemented: declared `var_scope` wins when present, else either spelling identifies a folder row. Accepting both is strictly safer than accepting one, the raw shape carries the columns for both, and a row matching neither is JOB scope, which is the correct default. No behaviour rests on the acceptance's wording being right — it rests on the two files. TESTS: 8 new in tests/unit/test_lineage_inventory.py, synthetic and no database (J18) — the acceptance's named convergence test (a %%R_PATH POSTCMD job and a literal CMD_LINE job land on ONE asset id, with the %%-spelling never becoming a node), expected residue, an unresolved user variable as a counted miss, no-scope-chain counted with behaviour unchanged, BOTH clause-(e) scope-chain shapes, job-scope-overrides-folder (pinned because the wrong chain order still resolves — just to the wrong file, silently), and a clause-(a) guard that the module calls the one resolver and imports no regex module. Three mutations checked and all caught: parsing raw (6 failures), reversing the chain order, and collapsing the residue/miss distinction. ENDPOINTS AND MEANING UNCHANGED as required: same READS_FROM / WRITES_TO, same ControlMJob -> DataAsset, no new relationship type, zero graph writes. INVOCATION TARGETS DELIBERATELY STILL PARSE THE VERBATIM COMMAND: invocation identity is already env-stabilised by `_stable_invocation_key` (DPL GUID, Ab Initio basename) and re-keying it on resolved text would move a signed ruling (cmdline-lineage-review 2026-07-16) — that is a gate question, not a build. Idea-176 captures both that boundary and the G97 artifact pass, which still skips %%-bearing artifact values it could now resolve; left out because this item's acceptance and counters are file-op ones and widening would have silently changed G97's numbers in the commit that established them. Suite 2459 passed / 10 skipped, ruff clean, CLI gates green.

G95Draft the gate prompt for standard IDENTITY and its carrier: can a validation profile be stored per team, and what may legitimately select a standard?
configP6taskp3fable / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A gate prompt is DRAFTED -- drafting decides nothing (the G27 / W1 / N10 / G61 precedent), nothing is written to the graph, and no entry leaves `planned` until the SME signs. The prompt must put four questions, each with the evidence already in the repo: (a) IDENTITY: does a standard get a stable id, and what is its shape? Today the per-job-type sets are CODE-AS-DATA in TOKEN_REGISTRY, whose own docstring calls itself "the single source both the parser and the published register read from, so code and document cannot drift" -- guarded by the registry-vs-standard agreement test. Giving a standard an id outside that module is a CONTRACT CHANGE and the prompt must say so plainly, with what the agreement test would then be guarding. (b) CARRIER: user direction 2026-08-12 proposes a config table (SQLite was floated) keyed by standard id, holding a validation profile BY TEAM, with a platform / product hierarchy later. The prompt lays the candidate carriers side by side -- versioned YAML under config/ (the launcher-registry precedent: schema-pinned, test-guarded, teams add rows without a code change) versus a database table -- against what each costs at review time and at port time, and asks the SME to rule. It does not pre-pick one. (c) WHAT MAY SELECT A STANDARD, restated as a fence rather than assumed: section 7.5 and G84 rule the DD digit a grammar VERSION and forbid it selecting a template or a standard, so a standard id needs its OWN carrier. The prompt asks the SME to ratify that fence explicitly, because a per-team registry is exactly the pressure that would break it. (d) DIVERGENCE POLICY: if a team may hold its own profile, what may it change? Adding a team-local token is the C16 annotation case the parser already knows; RELAXING a required token of the company standard is a governance decision, and the prompt must ask whether that is permitted at all, and if so who ratifies it. Every term or entry the prompt proposes is registered `planned` and stays planned until the gate signs. The deliverable is the prompt file plus its gate-log stub -- no code, no registry, no schema.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-12 (targeted groom) from Idea-114, clause 2 (identity + storage). Split from G94 deliberately: the selection tree is derivable from data the repo already has, while identity and carrier change the parse contract and are gate-relevant, which the inbox entry itself says. Promoting the DRAFT rather than the build is the standing pattern -- a prompt decides nothing, and it puts the question in front of the SME with the evidence attached instead of leaving it as an inbox line nobody can act on. MODULE: config, chosen because the artifact under discussion is a registry / profile store and config/ is the declared home for precedence, registries and crosswalks (the launcher-registry.yaml precedent is the closest existing shape). The prompt DESCRIBES a change to a drydocs-core module; it does not make one, so it is not filed there. RELATED: G94 (the selector this would eventually feed), G77 (a THEME token inside the same DD1 block), the etlprocess-kind-enum rider (engine vocabulary, which is where the engine names would have to agree if per-engine standards get ids). DONE 2026-08-25 (desktop). Drafted config/gate-prompts/standard-identity-and-carrier.yaml (5 sections, 17 confirmations, format guard green) + the gate-log RECORD stub the acceptance names as part of the deliverable. Drafts only; nothing decided, TOKEN_REGISTRY untouched, its every entry proposed exactly as its own header says. ALL FOUR ACCEPTANCE QUESTIONS ARE ON THE PAGE, and two gained teeth from rulings that landed AFTER the groom: (a) IDENTITY -- §A proposes <domain>.<subject>.v<N>, opaque to selection, versioned by CONTENT (grammar versions are the DD digit's job). The contract change is said plainly per the acceptance: an id outside TOKEN_REGISTRY turns the registry-vs-standard agreement test from two-way (code == document) into THREE-way (code == document == carrier), both directions -- the D3 endpoint-guard lesson -- and §A3 makes the test's new obligation part of the ruling so the build inherits it. (b) CARRIER -- three candidates priced, none pre-picked. The groom could not have known the two constraints that now frame this: ADR 0014 (accepted 2026-08-25) draws the per-machine-vs-domain line and a validation profile is a DOMAIN fact, so SQLite-as-primary collides with 0009 rule 1 AND 0014's line -- priced as re-opening a rule 0009 calls permanent, never forbidden outright. Candidate 3 (0009's own hybrid: YAML truth + mapping.db derived + rule-5 draft flow) is named as the shape the floated config table can have WITHOUT breaching anything. And §B4 makes the PORT DISPOSITION of by-team rows part of the carrier ruling itself -- the same-day alias lesson: company values in a canonical-producer file are overwritten wholesale at port, and a by-team profile is company data by definition. (c) THE FENCE -- §C ratifies §7.5/G84 explicitly, with the reason the acceptance gives (a per-team registry is exactly the pressure that would break it) sharpened into a schema rule: a carrier that even PERMITS a grammar-version column fails review. G94's same-job-under-DD1-and-DD2 test then enforces something SIGNED. (d) DIVERGENCE -- ADD is the C16 case and stays free (parse rule 5 already preserves team-local keys verbatim, never load-bearing). RELAX is put as forbidden vs permitted-with-ratification (gate-log id carried IN the profile row -- O24/A3 applied to governance), with recorded-only recommended AGAINST in the page's own text, and §D3 makes profile history append-only regardless of the outcome. REGISTERED: NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE RECORDED DECISION, not an omission. The acceptance's "every term the prompt proposes is registered planned" is conditional and this prompt proposes NO vocabulary term, node class, property term or map row -- identity and carrier are config-layer. Minting a map row anyway would be the stretching-a-wrong-label failure CLAUDE.md §1 names; §E1 puts the absence on the page and the gate-log stub carries it, with a future :Standard graph presence named as its own ontology gate. Suite 2461 passed / 8 skipped; ruff clean.

G96Control-M API-call framework the deploy/pull shell scripts can call — generic .sh, config-resolved in/out directories, calls discovered from the reference corpus (folder, job, calendar)
drydocs-coreP6taskp2opus / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A producer-side API-call framework the Control-M shell scripts can call, built MECHANISM-ONLY (the scripts themselves — controlm_common.sh, controlm_deploy_lite.sh, controlm_folder_pull.sh with a filled controlm_deploy.cfg — are company-side; verified 2026-08-12 that this tree carries no .sh at the root and no adapters/scripts/ directory, so what lands here is the framework and the generic sample, never the instance). (a) FIRST, THE NOTE, before any code: record the convention that keeps the .sh GENERIC — an internal shell-script home and a directory that stores the API artifacts, with the INPUT and OUTPUT directories resolved from CONFIG, never hardcoded. The producer mechanism for that convention already exists and is named in the note: drydocs_core/data_root.py (remediation_incoming_dir / remediation_outgoing_dir / controlm_xml_dir under DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT, logs under DRYDOCS_LOGDIR), with the company-side script home recorded as the vendor-namespaced scripts directory beside the adapters and the filled config staying untracked (sample committed, real values never). The note lives where the next builder looks: the framework module docstring plus a README beside the sample config. (b) THE FRAMEWORK: a Python call surface under drydocs_core/adapters/ that a generic wrapper .sh can invoke per operation, taking its endpoint/profile from config and its in/out directories from the data-root conventions, returning machine-readable results the scripts can test. Connection-profile handling is mechanism-only: shape from the corpus doc, no real endpoints, hostnames or credentials anywhere in the tree (classification boundary; secrets discipline). (c) THE DISCOVERY, in the item because the user put it there: search the knowledge graph — and where the graph does not yet hold the vendor corpus, the corpus files directly — for EXAMPLE API CALLS usable for FOLDER, JOB and CALENDAR operations, and write the candidates up as a short mechanism reference (operation, call shape, corpus source) that the framework's per-object surface is then built against. The corpus already carries controlm-api-folder-reference.md, controlm-api-job-properties.md and controlm-calendars.md plus the connection-profile and installation pages, so the search has ground truth to cite. (d) VERSION GUARDRAIL, so the framework does not assume an API the company does not run: the company orchestrator is 9.0.21.300 XML-first (the JSON/SaaS API files were demoted to conceptual reference once that was established), so the discovery step must state per candidate call whether it is available at that version, and the framework's contract must degrade honestly — an unavailable call is a reported capability gap, not a silent fallback.
