Acceptance: NO GATE IS OPENED OR REOPENED -- this builds what two signed gates already ruled. cmdline-nfr-vetting (2026-07-21, SME-2 / SME-3) ruled the DISTINCT label rather than a single label with a role, and adopted the :Script refinements with it; rua-load-shapes (2026-08-07, 28/28, applied at G55) ACTIVATED m3_invokes and m7_uses_artifact in the same breath, on the stated reasoning that activating INVOKES alone would land payloads in the 1..n fold first and force an in-graph migration. G16's own notes name this item: "the m7 build (payload migration to USES_ARTIFACT, script_role stamping) is its own follow-up item once the writer endpoint work lands." (a) THE SPLIT: the writer emits USES_ARTIFACT from the job to the PAYLOAD artifact the launcher dispatches, while INVOKES keeps the LAUNCHER only. The discrimination comes from the G16 FACT_REGISTRY canonicals (ETL_ARTIFACT_URI / ETL_ARTIFACT_KIND / ETL_ARTIFACT_SHA and the ETL_PLATFORM pair) under the aliases-suggest-values-decide contract, plus the G15 launcher properties -- NEVER from a variable NAME alone, which is the 2,384-variable gap analysis' one durable finding: names lie. (b) :Script GAINS script_role {launcher, payload} and the gate-adopted artifact properties (platform / artifact_uri / artifact_kind / platform_flags / script_path). The property already exists -- the writer stamps script_role='profile' for the rua profile case (G23, section C2) -- so this EXTENDS a value set rather than inventing a property. Script identity stays PATH-keyed; that ruling is not touched. (c) ENDPOINT CLASS PER EDGE: to_node is Script | ETLProcess per rua-load-shapes section B2 -- one edge meaning, two endpoint classes, the endpoint RECORDED on the edge -- with the raw evidence string (the command line or variable form that produced it) kept VERBATIM per section B3, which is what keeps the endpoint choice re-checkable later. (d) EXISTING GRAPHS: state the position rather than assume a clean load. Where a live graph already folded payloads into a 1..n INVOKES set, either an idempotent re-load (MERGE-keyed) or a named migration step covers it -- whichever, it is written down and the counts are reported. A silent double-representation (payload on both labels) is the one outcome that must be impossible. (e) COUNTS AND A WARN STREAM: invocations classified launcher, classified payload, and UNCLASSIFIED. An unclassified invocation stays exactly where it is today and is reported; it is never promoted to a payload on a guess. TESTS: a fixture command line carrying both a launcher and a payload yields exactly one INVOKES and one USES_ARTIFACT edge with script_role stamped on both endpoints; a payload-less command line yields no USES_ARTIFACT edge at all; the vocabulary guard (write_curated raises GateBoundVocabularyError on a non-active entry) still holds. Full suite green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-13 (targeted groom -- node labels and Cypher loaders) from Idea-23, whose parked trigger -- "once the writer's ETLProcess endpoint work makes the edge landable" -- has FIRED, verified two ways at the groom rather than assumed. (2) drydocs_lineage/writer.py MERGEs :ETLProcess on its token and carries the union-endpoint machinery, so the endpoint class the edge needs exists. ALSO VERIFIED ABSENT, so this is a real build and not a re-close: the writer emits NO USES_ARTIFACT edge today and stamps script_role only for the rua profile case -- a grep of writer.py on 2026-08-13 returns the profile stamp and nothing else. DONE 2026-08-25 (desktop). NO GATE OPENED OR REOPENED, and the two ruling texts were READ rather than worked from their one-line restatements -- which mattered, because the acceptance's clause (c) reads as if USES_ARTIFACT gets the Script|ETLProcess union and IT DOES NOT. rua-load-shapes B2 widened `scheduler_invokes` only ("FOLLOW-UP BUILD per I1: the m3_invokes entry's to_node widens at its build"), while cmdline-nfr-vetting SME-2 ruled m7 as ControlMJob->Script{payload} and the live vocabulary entry still says `to_node: Script`. THAT RESOLVES THE ONE REAL COLLISION IN THE ITEM: an Ab Initio pset or DPL pipeline reached through a launcher is an :ETLProcess, so it STAYS on INVOKES -- which is exactly what B2 bought when it declined B1 rather than re-model G12's working wrapper-payload expansion. It is counted as its own bucket, never as clause (e)'s "unclassified", because the reason is a ruling and not an absence of evidence. No vocabulary entry was edited. WHERE THE SPLIT LANDED, and why not purely in the writer as the groom note suggested: three things in the code forbid it. `LineageGraph.add_rel` refuses any label outside REL_TYPES, so USES_ARTIFACT joins the model wherever it is emitted; `plan_curated` enforces confirmed <= graph.rels, so a writer-invented edge could never be confirmed by the SME and the writer would be writing meaning the curation surface never saw; and the acceptance's own test wants script_role on BOTH endpoints, which needs a launcher NODE that today's extractor never mints (it keys the single node on `target`, which IS the payload whenever one exists). THE FEED IS THE VARIABLES, per the acceptance: a new `_artifact_pass` over the same variables CSV `_prepost_pass` already joins, routed through `classify_variable` so the G16 "aliases suggest, VALUES decide" contract applies and no code path ever reads a variable NAME (the 2,384-var finding). ALSO MOVED: `_ETL_PROCESS_KINDS` writer -> model (re-exported under the old name), because two consumers now need it and two copies of a classification set is how they drift. TESTS: 10 new in tests/unit/test_lineage_inventory.py -- both cases the acceptance names (one command line yielding exactly one INVOKES + one USES_ARTIFACT with script_role on both endpoints; a payload-less line yielding no USES_ARTIFACT at all), plus the clause-(e) unclassified case, the clause-(d) migrate-never-duplicate case, the B2 ETLProcess case, unresolved %%value, values-decide (%%JAR_PATH holding dt-launcher.sh is a LAUNCHER), unmatched job, the writer plan (USES_ARTIFACT batch + scheduler_uses_artifact vocab id + the SME-3 rows + the counts), and the migration script's own shape. G103The rua bundle's script-copy path is a convention the extractor re-derives, not a column the collector declares — a layout change reports an empty bundle, not a broken contract
drydocs-lineageP6chorep2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: EXACTLY ONE of three resolutions lands, and WHICH is recorded in the close note (the A4 idiom). All three are legitimate; what is not legitimate is the current state, where the contract exists only as a comment on one line. (a) DECLARE IT -- add a copy-path column to scripts.tsv so the location is stated rather than guessed. That is a bundle SCHEMA change: COLLECTOR_VERSION goes to rua-inventory/v3 and the script's own optional-column discipline (v1 bundles stay ingestible; scripts.tsv and the sha256 columns are treated as OPTIONAL) applies to the new column too. (b) PIN THE CONVENTION -- leave the wire format alone and add one test that builds or fixtures a small bundle and asserts a captured file is readable at the derived path from the EXTRACTOR's side, so a collector-side layout change reds a test instead of silently zeroing the counters. The cheaper candidate, and the S10 / derived-coverage idiom the repo already uses elsewhere. (c) ACCEPT AS IS -- with the reason written where the coupling lives, not only in a close note. WHAT THE RESOLUTION MUST CARRY EITHER WAY, because it is the reason this is worth an item: the failure is SILENT and reads as something else. Both consumers already handle a missing copy correctly -- scripts_unreadable / scripts_no_copy in G21's rua_code_ops.py, server_uncomputable in G24's code_repo.py -- because an over-cap file is LISTED but not COPIED by design (SCRIPT_COPY_MAX_BYTES, 1 MiB default). So a mirror-layout change lands every counter in the "too big to copy" bucket, the run SUCCEEDS, and "the collector's layout changed" is indistinguishable from "this estate has large scripts". NOTHING IS WRONG TODAY: the chain is correctly wired and this is a latent coupling, not a live defect -- the item exists so it stays that way.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-19 from Idea-115 (found 2026-08-12 tracing G24 end to end at the user's ask). VERIFIED AT THE GROOM, not recalled: rua_inventory.py:380-390 already carries a comment naming this as "DERIVED, not declared (Idea-115)", and drydocs_lineage/collect/rua_inventory.sh still writes the header path/owner/group/perms/size/mtime/sha256 with the mirror built separately. Module drydocs-lineage / phase 6 / epic component-topology follows G21, G24 and G97 -- the items on either side of this chain. N12's notes already cite this entry as the precedent for the class (a contract that existed only as a derived expression, fixed by making both ends name each other); this item is that class's own instance. DONE 2026-08-21 (desktop). RESOLUTION (b) PIN THE CONVENTION -- the wire format is unchanged (COLLECTOR_VERSION stays rua-inventory/v2, no new column), and the contract that lived as one comment is now held by a test that reads BOTH halves: tests/unit/test_lineage_rua.py:: test_collector_mirror_layout_and_extractor_derivation_are_the_same_convention parses the collector's literal `dest="$BUNDLE/scripts$path"` (drydocs_lineage/collect/rua_inventory.sh) and the extractor's `copy_rel = f"scripts{row['path']}"` (rua_inventory.py) and fails when either moves, naming the other side; test_derived_copy_path_is_readable_from_the_extractor_side proves the derived pointer resolves to a real readable file on a collector-shaped fixture bundle. So a layout change on either side now reds a test instead of landing every counter in the "too big to copy" bucket (scripts_no_copy / scripts_unreadable / server_uncomputable), which read as "this estate has large scripts". Why (b) over (a): a v3 schema bump for a column whose only reader is the repo that writes the collector is cost without a second consumer; over (c): a comment is what failed. The coupling site carries a comment pointing at the test. Nothing was wrong today; it stays that way by guard.

Acceptance: A new `docs/decisions/0014-runtime-substrate.md` exists with status **Proposed** — never Accepted, because acceptance is the user's and is recorded in `docs/decisions/README.md` only after they rule. 0014 is the next free number as of this groom. The ADR decides, or explicitly defers with a named trigger, each of the seven clauses Idea-152 raised: (1) one `RuntimeSettings` group on the `DRYDOCS_` prefix (pydantic-settings, the shape `drydocs_core/config.py` already uses) carrying `log_dir`, `log_level`, `log_retention_days`, `data_root` — `.env`-readable, env-overridable, defaults unchanged, with `SPIDERP_*` kept one cycle as deprecated aliases and then dropped from BOTH log families; (2) stdlib `logging.config.dictConfig` driven from that group with NO new runtime dependency — console plus a JSON-lines file sink in `log_dir`, level from settings, `--verbose` still winning, and `run_log.py`'s existing header/summary contract untouched; (3) ONE naming rule for the shared directory, `<kind>.<name>.<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.{log|jsonl}`, with the per-DAY `qa.graph_qa.<YYYYmmdd>.jsonl` ledger either moved onto it or its exception written down; (4) retention as a `drydocs prune-logs` verb mirroring `prune-snapshots` (age + size, dry-run default) rather than a background sweeper thread; (5) every component opening a `LoaderRunLog` per batch; (6) an API request/audit line for every Cypher-executing route, actor hashed the way `:AgentRun` already hashes it; (7) a single declaration of the data-zone map. THE HARD REQUIREMENT: the ADR states in its own text how it reconciles with **ADR 0009 (configuration substrate)**, which already makes git-tracked YAML the settings source of truth — an env-var-and-`.env` settings group is either an exception ADR 0009 permits (say where) or an amendment to it (say so, and say what in 0009 changes). It also records the sister project's own gotcha list as REJECTED alternatives, since Idea-152 captured it as an anti-checklist: level hardcoded with no env override; a Linux-absolute default that breaks on Windows; silent fallback to the local profile on a misconfigured box; one process-start timestamp shared by every file; and an unbounded sweeper registry when the logger factory is called with per-incident names. Named as OUT of scope: persisting executed Cypher server-side for ask-search — a separate idea whose owning surface is undecided. `docs/decisions/README.md` gains the 0014 row reading Proposed. No code changes in this item.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-21 (laptop) from Idea-152 (prio High, user-confirmed), which carries the 2026-08-20 survey and asked in writing to be groomed into "the ADR; a core item (1-3); a load item (4); per-component items (5); an api item (6); a config item (7)". G104 is the ADR; G105-G109 are those five, each `depends_on` this item so nothing implements an unratified decision. EPIC AND PHASE CHOICE, recorded because it was a judgement call rather than an obvious fit: no runtime-substrate epic exists and a groom cannot mint one, so the chain is filed under component-topology / phase 6 — the epic that already owns cross-component structural rulings (ADR 0002's core-vs-component split) and that already holds an ADR-drafting item as precedent (G53, the ADR 0011 shelf plan). A dedicated epic is PROPOSED TO THE USER in the groom report; if they take it these six items change `epic:`, not their ids. Module `docs` follows Y1 and R1 — a decision document is docs work even when its subject is core. Model fable because the ADR decides a boundary (where settings may live at all) against a standing ADR. Status stays Proposed on purpose: this item drafts the decision, it does not make it. DONE 2026-08-24 (desktop). docs/decisions/0014-runtime-substrate.md written, status PROPOSED, and the README row reads Proposed -- the ruling is the user's and this item does not make it. All seven clauses decided or deferred with a named trigger; two are deferrals (clause 5's API scope, trigger = clause 6's audit-line design; clause 6's Cypher text, trigger = the ask-search owner), and clause 3 ships a deliberate exception rather than a clean rule. THE 0009 RECONCILIATION, which was the hard requirement, lands as an EXCEPTION 0009 ALREADY PERMITS rather than an amendment: rule 1 scopes git-text source-of-truth to "anything an SME gates, a port carries, or a classification test guards", and the runtime substrate fails all three named tests -- with PORT-MANIFEST marking the sibling dev-environment.yaml canonical-company precisely so local paths never cross, which is the same argument one file over. The ADR draws an explicit anti-drift line (per-machine operational facts only) and names the one place the ruling could go the other way, so a broader reading of rule 1 turns this into an amendment instead of being quietly assumed. THE SURVEY WAS RE-VERIFIED, NOT TRUSTED, and that earned its keep: Idea-152 is four days old and G81 landed inside the gap. TWO of its findings are stale and the ADR records both rather than arguing from them -- sql_run_log.py does NOT honor only the legacy var (it imports claim_log_path from run_log, so both families already share the resolver and differ only in file naming), and .env.example now documents DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT (G81, 2026-08-23), leaving only DRYDOCS_LOGDIR undocumented. The other findings hold and are cited to line. Clause 7 is likewise mostly executed already: G81 built config/data-zones.yaml and the guards, so G109 is the remainder -- and the ADR fences it against creating a THIRD declaration by ruling that the zone map keeps mode and the registry gains rows. It is not -- it is deliberate and documented ("telemetry never turns a good answer into an error"). Rewritten to the accurate and more useful point: the swallow is right, and with no logging backbone behind it a permanently broken ledger still reports nothing, which is what clause 2 fixes without touching the swallow. RIDER ADDED AT THE 2026-08-25 RULING, because this item's clause-by-clause text restates the PRE-AMENDMENT ADR and two of its premises are now wrong. (i) Clause 1 was ruled PER-KIND: the group reads `config/log-kinds.yaml` (root + defaults + one entry per kind naming its writer), so `log_dir` / `log_level` / `log_retention_days` below are the per-kind DEFAULTS, not one global set. (ii) The sentence below claiming `sql_run_log.py` "honors ONLY the legacy variable" is FALSE and was already false when this item was groomed -- it imports `claim_log_path` from `run_log`, so both families have always shared the resolver; they differ only in file naming. (iv) `kind` does not exist in code today -- three sites hardcode it and none agree (`run_log.py:147`, `llm_ledger.py`, and `sql_run_log`'s unvalidated `base_name`); making it real is part of this item, not a precondition of it. Idea-171 carries the measurement behind all four. (1) A `RuntimeSettings` group in `drydocs_core/config.py` (pydantic-settings, `DRYDOCS_` prefix, beside `Neo4jSettings`) carries `log_dir`, `log_level`, `log_retention_days`, `data_root`. Today's resolution order is PRESERVED as the default rather than replaced: `DRYDOCS_LOGDIR` wins, `SPIDERP_LOGDIR` still resolves for one deprecation cycle with a warning, `~/logs/DryDocs` stays the fallback. `drydocs_core/adapters/sql_run_log.py`, which honors ONLY the legacy variable today, resolves through the same group, so the two run-log families can no longer disagree about where the directory is. (2) `drydocs/cli.py`'s single `basicConfig` — the only one in the tree, currently stderr-only with its level from `--verbose` alone — is replaced by `logging.config.dictConfig` built from the group: console plus a JSON-lines file sink under `log_dir`, level from `RuntimeSettings.log_level`, `--verbose` still overriding it. "Defaults unchanged" is proven, not asserted: a test clears the environment and shows every path this touches resolves exactly where it resolved before. `poetry run pytest -q`, `python -c "import drydocs.cli"`, `drydocs --help`, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` all green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-21 (laptop) from Idea-152 clause (5). MODULE CHOICE, recorded because the entry asked for "per-component items" (plural) and this groom filed ONE: the change is a single mechanical pattern applied four times against one core contract, so four items would fragment one review across four pulls while multiplying the chance the four drift into four slightly different run-log shapes — which is the exact defect the item exists to remove. `module: drydocs-lineage` names the first component in the list; the acceptance enumerates all four so nothing is lost by the single filing. THE ACCEPTANCE'S CITED PRECEDENT DOES NOT EXIST. It says to do this "exactly as drydocs_remediation does after G93" -- G93 is still todo, so remediation opens no run log and logs nothing at all. Built against the LIVE precedent instead: drydocs/loaders/base.py, which has always done it correctly (open -> capture the exception -> re-raise -> close in finally) across eight call sites. G93 gains a rider so remediation joins this shape rather than minting a fifth. Wrapping a function that cannot run produces a log that opens and immediately closes with a failure summary, every time, forever; a test asserting that would be asserting the scaffold. It rides MM10, and the test module says so in its docstring rather than leaving a reader to wonder which component is missing and why. ONE SHARED HELPER, NOT FOUR COPIES -- drydocs_core.run_log.batch_run_log, a context manager yielding a mutable summary dict. base.py had the right block but inline, so a component wanting the same behaviour had to copy it. Copying it four times IS the drift this item's own groom note warned about: four components, four almost-identical shapes, no single place to fix the one that is subtly wrong. It also carries base.py's OSError rule -- an unwritable log directory is swallowed and the batch runs WITHOUT a log, because a run log is an audit trail and must never be the reason a batch fails. WIRED, each by rename-plus-wrapper so the diff is the wrapper rather than a re-indented body: lineage write_curated + write_rua, docmeta's two connectors (fetch kept as the PUBLIC name, so the Connector protocol still holds -- guarded), and the vendor scrape's capture, which printed to stdout only and left nothing behind once the terminal closed. A JUDGEMENT CALL: write_curated's empty-confirmed guard runs BEFORE the log opens. Nothing was asked for, so there is no batch to record, and a log per no-op call would bury real runs among empties. Guarded, so the choice is visible rather than incidental. A BUG MY OWN TEST HID, worth recording because the lesson is general. Both connectors were written against source.source_id -- a field FetchSource does not have; it is source.id. My new test used a FAKE carrying source_id, so it passed against the same invention, and SEVENTEEN EXISTING docmeta tests are what caught it. The fix was not just the attribute: the test now constructs the REAL FetchSource. A fake allowed to differ from the type it stands in for validates the author's belief instead of the code. 12 new guards, every component tested on BOTH paths -- the failure path is the half that matters, since a run log that only exists when nothing went wrong records the runs nobody needs. G108drydocs_api logs nothing at all — an audit line for every Cypher-executing route, including /raw-cypher and /specs/{id}/run, with the actor hashed the way :AgentRun already hashes it
drydocs-apiP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology
depends on: G104

Acceptance: SME RULINGS FOLDED IN 2026-08-25 — the clause-6 deferral is CLOSED and this item now builds TWO kinds, not one. Read these before the original acceptance below, which predates them. (A) TWO KINDS, not one surface at two levels. `api` is the AUDIT record: lean, 90-day retention, and it does NOT carry Cypher text. `api-debug` is a separate declared kind in config/log-kinds.yaml: verbose, short retention, per-run rotation, and it DOES carry Cypher text and request detail. Ruled as a split rather than one kind at DEBUG level so a 90-day metrics record is never buried in debug noise and debug can be deleted aggressively without touching the audit. This closes ADR 0014 clause 6's deferred question ("does the line carry the Cypher text") by answering it per kind instead of once. (B) 90-DAY RETENTION ON THE AUDIT KIND, and the reason is a metrics window, not an audit relic: the SME's purpose is meaningful figures on WHAT IS SEARCHED. Declared in config/log-kinds.yaml per G105, never as a literal here. (C) VERBOSE IS SETTINGS-LEVEL, NOT PER REQUEST. There is no `--verbose` on an HTTP request, and a per-request header would let an untrusted caller turn on verbose capture of their own traffic. The `api-debug` kind's level comes from its declaration, so it is configured rather than asked for -- the everything-configurable principle applied to a surface that has no CLI flag. (D) A CORRELATION ID IS REQUIRED, and it is the field this item would otherwise have shipped without. The QA ledger holds the QUESTION TEXT and the API audit holds the ROUTE AND OUTCOME, and today nothing joins them: the ledger carries `run_id` and the drafted audit fields carry no equivalent. Without it "what is searched" cannot be answered -- half the metric is in each file. This is not hypothetical wiring: agents/graph_qa/agent.py:60 calls ephemeral_client, which POSTs to {api_url}/specs/ephemeral, so one console question really does produce ledger lines AND an API call. Carry the agent `run_id` where the control part supplies one, else the hashed session token that control.py already passes. Adding it later is a migration; adding it now is a field. (E) THE ONE THING HELD FOR SME REVIEW: whether debug-tier Cypher text is ever DISPLAYED IN THE UI. Capturing it is ruled; surfacing it is not, and the SME asked for that specific question to go to the TOP of the review list. So this item may write it and must not surface it, and any UI work that would display it is blocked on that review rather than on this item. Every `drydocs_api` route that executes Cypher writes one audit record per request — `/raw-cypher` and `/specs/{id}/run` at minimum, plus any sibling found by enumerating the routes rather than by memory (the enumeration is part of the deliverable: the item lists what it found). The component logs NOTHING today, so this is the first record of who asked the graph for what through the API. Each record carries: timestamp, route, spec id where one applies, the outcome (rows returned or the error class), elapsed time, and an ACTOR identifier hashed by the same function `:AgentRun` already uses — never a raw actor value, so the record is publishable under the §3 sensitivity rules and cannot become the place a real identity leaks. The record does NOT contain result values; it is an access record, not a data copy. Where the Cypher text itself is recorded, that choice and its size bound are stated in the acceptance of whoever builds it — this item does not silently decide to persist query text. The sink is the `RuntimeSettings` log directory via G105's dictConfig, on G105's naming rule; no second logging mechanism is introduced. Tests: one request per Cypher-executing route asserts exactly one audit record, that the actor field never equals the raw input, and that a route raising mid-query still emits a record with the error class. `poetry run pytest -q`, ruff clean.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-21 (laptop) from Idea-152 clause (6). Module drydocs-api; depends on G104 for the ratified shape and, in practice, on G105 for the sink — sequenced through G104 only, so it does not block on core landing first if the ADR ends up specifying the sink completely. Deliberately scoped as an ACCESS record, not query persistence. Idea-152's closing line — that server-side persistence of executed Cypher for ask-search is a separate idea whose owning surface is unknown — is respected here: this item makes the request auditable without deciding where executed Cypher lives. DONE 2026-08-26 (desktop). `drydocs_api/audit.py` — ApiAuditLog, and both declared kinds flipped ACTIVE in config/log-kinds.yaml with `writer: drydocs_api.audit.ApiAuditLog` (the planned->active mechanism working as G105 designed it; test_log_kinds now pins the flip instead of the planned state). THE ENUMERATION, the deliverable's list, lives in audit.py's docstring and is TWELVE routes under the ruled Cypher-OR-writes scope: five Cypher-executing (/query/{id}, /raw-cypher, /specs/{id}/run, /specs/{id}/export, /specs/ephemeral — the last audited because the Cypher ENTERS the system there and it is where the agent run_id arrives) and seven writes (the four intake POSTs, overrides/draft, drafts/{id}/promote, app-code/draft). Exclusions are STATED with reasons, not implied: /login and /logout touch only the in-memory session store; POST /mappings/changeset persists nothing server-side (the O13 returned-artifact contract); every GET is a read. A 401 with NO bearer header is unaudited — there is no actor to record — while invalid-token and forbidden outcomes audit with the ORIGINAL error class (Forbidden, InvalidTokenError), never the mapped HTTPException; a test pins that distinction. ONE INTERPRETATION RECORDED so the acceptance's literal wording reads right: "via G105's dictConfig" predates the 2026-08-25 two-kind ruling that made `api` per-day jsonl — jsonl kinds append directly via log_kinds.log_filename in run_log.resolve_log_dir's directory (the `qa` ledger precedent; dictConfig serves the format:log `cli` kind). No second mechanism: the declaration IS the mechanism and this writer is the one it names. ACTOR: sha256 hexdigest of the bearer token — the :AgentRun caller-identity function, REIMPLEMENTED because agents/ is a separate venv, and pinned by a known-value test rather than asserted. RULING D WIRED END TO END, not just fielded: X-DryDocs-Run-Id accepted on the five Cypher routes (bounded — 128 printable chars, failing values drop to the session-hash fallback, because it is untrusted caller input headed for a 90-day record), ephemeral_client sends it, and agent.py threads run_id into make_register as a CLOSURE so register_cypher's call signature — and every fake of it — is unchanged. correlation_id = run_id else actor hash, correlation_source says which. DEBUG TIER: settings-level per ruling C — on only when the api-debug DECLARATION says level: DEBUG (the repo default is INFO = off, tested); per-run stamp frozen at construction; Cypher bounded at 20,000 chars with a cypher_truncated flag, the bound stated in the kind's note as the acceptance requires. The api line is built from an ALLOWLIST so cypher/params structurally cannot leak into the 90-day record (tested by setting them and asserting absence). Export streams record at job creation with rows NULL — the row count is the export manifest's fact (registers on completion) — carrying export_id instead. Ruling E honoured by omission: the debug text is written and NOTHING surfaces it; any UI display is blocked on the SME review, not on this item. TESTS: 14 in tests/unit/test_api_audit.py, two tiers — pure ApiAuditLog (the acceptance's core claims hold with no framework installed) and TestClient wiring (one request per audited route = exactly one line; reads add none). THREE MUTATIONS, all caught: write-only-on-success (the error tests bite), cypher appended to the api line (the allowlist test bites), one route's audit deleted (the per-route count bites). The enforcement matrix regenerated — the new guard tests changed that derived surface. Suite 2495 passed / 10 skipped, ruff clean, CLI gates green.

Acceptance: The data zones under `DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT` are declared in ONE place and the resolvers derive from that declaration instead of restating it. (a) The six zones the 2026-08-20 survey found in code with no `source-registry` row — `email-extracts`, `context-intake`, `vendor-docs`, `remediation/*`, `cmdline-staging`, `catalog` — each get a row, or a recorded reason a zone legitimately has none. Today `drydocs landing-zones --check` is BLIND to all six, which is the defect: a check that silently covers half the zones reads as coverage. (b) The `dpl/` (registry) vs `dpl-registry/` (code) drift is reconciled to one name, with the losing name kept as an alias for one cycle if anything on disk already uses it, and the choice recorded. (c) `drydocs_core/data_root.py`'s resolvers are derived FROM the rows rather than hardcoded beside them, so a new zone cannot exist in code without existing in the registry. A test asserts the two agree: every zone the code can resolve has a row, every row resolves. (d) `.env.example` documents `DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT` and `DRYDOCS_LOGDIR`; it documents neither today. (e) The Confluence capture that lands IN-TREE against `landing_zones.py`'s tracked-only rule is ruled one way and the ruling is written down: either it moves under the data root, or the rule gains a stated exception naming it. Notes: Groomed 2026-08-21 (laptop) from Idea-152 clause (7) / finding (e). Module `config` because the deliverable is registry rows plus a derivation rule, not new component behavior; the `data_root.py` edit is the consequence of the declaration, not the point of the item. Watch item for whoever pulls it: each new source-registry row must carry a `classification` per CLAUDE.md §3 — the six zones are operational metadata, so Internal is the likely answer, but it is a per-zone call and no default exists. DONE 2026-08-24 (desktop). TWO OF THE FIVE CLAUSES WERE ALREADY SATISFIED BY G81, which landed four days after this item was groomed -- recorded as overtaken per the Q9/Q14 idiom, acceptance text untouched, NOT re-done. (b) OVERTAKEN: the dpl/ vs dpl-registry/ drift is already reconciled. Both dpl rows read dpl-registry/ and data_root.py records that the registry said dpl/ from N12 until G81 corrected it. No alias was needed; the company relay about exports stranded in dpl/ already rode out in fcf973b5. (c) OVERTAKEN: resolvers already derive from the declaration and two guards already assert the agreement -- test_every_data_root_helper_maps_to_a_declared_zone (code to declaration) and test_each_zone_path_equals_what_its_helper_actually_resolves (declaration to code, added at G81's follow-through and proven to fire on injected drift). The acceptance said "derived FROM the rows" meaning source-registry rows; G81 derived them from config/data-zones.yaml instead. Same intent, different file, and ADR 0014's fence against a THIRD declaration is why it stays that way. (a) THE PREMISE MOVED AND THE REAL DEFECT IS SHARPER. The acceptance says the six zones have no source-registry row so landing-zones --check is blind to them. Post-G81 all six DO have a declaration -- in config/data-zones.yaml -- and the command was still blind, because it read only the registry. Duplicating them into the registry was the wrong fix twice over: data-zones.yaml's own header rules that a zone duplicating a registry row FAILS the guard, and a write zone has no provenance, trust axis or acquisition mode, so its registry row would be a field set of nulls asserting a source that does not exist. That is the acceptance's own "recorded reason a zone legitimately has none" branch, now written into the header naming all seven write zones. What was fixed instead is the READ SURFACE: drydocs landing-zones reports BOTH declarations (15 registry + 11 declared = 26 zones, was 15), and --check is MODE-AWARE -- an empty read zone fails, an empty write zone does not, because failing on an output directory the system rebuilds trains the operator to ignore the exit code. ONE BUG CAUGHT IN MY OWN CHANGE before it shipped: the first cut printed a second JSON array, so --json emitted two documents and stopped parsing. Restructured to one object, manual_zones plus declared_zones, and a guard asserts that shape -- a machine surface that does not parse is worse than one omitting half the data, because the omission is readable. (d) .env.example documents DRYDOCS_LOGDIR. Only that one: G81 added the data root on 2026-08-23, so "documents neither" was half-stale at drafting. The block records that the log dir is OPTIONAL where the data root is mandatory -- the G81 (d) scope fence. (e) RULED: THE CAPTURE MOVES, it does not get an exception. The cdo-frameworks Confluence capture had been landing in-tree under internal/knowledge/data/<space>/ -- untracked AND not gitignored, the one category git clean -fd removes without needing -x. An exception could never expire: landing_zones.py permits an in-tree zone only when its contents are TRACKED, and PUBLISH-BOUNDARY forbids ever tracking a verbatim capture carrying real employee names and internal URLs, so it would be permanent by construction. Declared as read zone confluence-capture; vendor-docs is the exact precedent, existing as the ServiceNow .gitignore precedent generalized to a real out-of-repo home. The doc-source row gains landing_zone: confluence-capture, and its historical source: path is LEFT AS WRITTEN -- falsifying a provenance record to match a later ruling is the one thing a VERBATIM row may not do, so the ruling governs the next capture, not the record of the last one. Producer has no internal/knowledge/ at all, so this costs nothing here and is a real relocation only on the checkout holding the capture. NO NEW REGISTRY ROW WAS MINTED, so the groom's classification watch item never triggered -- worth saying plainly, because "the guard did not fire" and "the guard was not reached" look identical from a green suite. Two new guards, both behavioural rather than structural: the read surface covers every declared zone and stays one JSON document, and --check distinguishes an empty read zone from an empty write zone. MODULE_MAP's data_zones row records the new read surface. Suite 2384 passed / 10 skipped, ruff + format clean, CLI import + --help pass.

Only `google-adk>=2,<3` is bounded today; `neo4j`, `python-dotenv`, `litellm` and `pyyaml` are BARE, so the agent runtime resolves whatever is current on the day someone builds the venv and no two machines are reproducible. Notes: Groomed 2026-08-21 (laptop) from Idea-141's "worth doing regardless of the verdict" clause. G111A declared zone whose env variable is set resolves to the untouched default: data_zones._resolve() ignores the env field, and the G81 declared-equals-resolved guard only walks zones that carry a helper
drydocs-coreP6bugp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: (a) THE RESOLUTION. `data_zones._resolve()` handles `base: home` and `base: data_root` and nothing else, so the `env:` field a zone declares is read by no code at all. `config/data-zones.yaml`'s `run-logs` zone declares `env: DRYDOCS_LOGDIR`; with that variable set (this desktop sets it, per the local data/log roots), the zone resolves to the default under the home directory while every real log lands elsewhere. After this item, a zone declaring `env:` resolves through that variable when it is set and non-empty, and falls back to `base` + `path` when it is not — the same order `drydocs_core.log_kinds.resolve_root()` already implements for the log root, reused rather than re-derived so the two cannot drift. (b) THE GUARD. `tests/unit/test_data_zones.py`'s declared-equals-resolved check walks only zones carrying a `helper`, and `run-logs` has `helper: ~`. A helper-less zone is therefore unguarded, which is why (a) survived G81 and G109. The guard is widened to assert every zone resolves to what the declaration says, helper or not, and the widening is written RED FIRST against the current code with `DRYDOCS_LOGDIR` set — a guard that is green the moment it is written has proven nothing. (c) THE READ SURFACE. `drydocs landing-zones` (widened by G109 to report declared zones) shows the `run-logs` row resolving to the same directory `drydocs_core.run_log` actually writes to, verified on a machine where `DRYDOCS_LOGDIR` is set and named in the close note per J18. This is the point of the item: the command exists so "where did my logs go" is a one-command answer, and today it answers confidently and wrongly. (d) THE DOCSTRING THAT PREDICTED THIS. `log_kinds.resolve_root()` carries a paragraph naming this exact defect as live next door; it is rewritten to describe the fixed state rather than left asserting something untrue.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-26 from Idea-171's residue. Clauses 1, 3 and 4 of that entry were RULED into ADR 0014 on 2026-08-25 and built by G105 (one log root, per-kind declaration, derived grammar, retention read from the declaration); this is the part the ADR does not close. ADR 0014 clause 1 gives the LOG root one resolution site, which is a forward fix for one zone — the bug here is general to any zone declaring `env:`, and the guard gap is general to any helper-less zone. Module `drydocs-core` and epic component-topology recorded as a choice: `config/data-zones.yaml` is the declaration but the defect is entirely in the resolver and its guard, which are core. Filing it under `config` would put the item on the shelf where nothing needs to change. Mechanism only. No edge semantics, no gate. p2 rather than p1 because nothing loses data — a log lands in the right place today; only the description of where it landed is wrong. CLOSED 2026-08-28 (desktop, advisor-dispatch build; merged --no-ff from a worktree branch). data_zones._resolve() now honors a zone's declared env: field, reusing drydocs_core.log_kinds.resolve_env_override() (extracted from resolve_root()'s existing check) rather than re-deriving the order -- the log root and the run-logs zone read the same environment variable through one implementation. The declared-equals-resolved guard in tests/unit/test_data_zones.py now walks every zone, not just helper-carrying ones, closing the gap that let this survive G81 and G109; it was written and run RED-first against the unfixed code before the fix landed (TypeError + 2 failing tests recorded). Verified live per J18: desktop, DRYDOCS_LOGDIR set -- drydocs landing-zones reports the run-logs zone at the DRYDOCS_LOGDIR directory, matching drydocs_core.run_log.resolve_log_dir() exactly. resolve_root()'s docstring paragraph that named the defect as live next door now describes the fixed state.

No graph writes, no edges: attribution is a census and Epic K still owns what it means. THE SHAPE EVERY REPORT SHARES, and the part worth reading: a row that cannot participate in the join is held OUT of the set arithmetic rather than folded into either side. A DPL-origin dataset with no registration_source_ref, a distribution with no URN, an unparseable URN — each gets its OWN counted list. Folding them into catalog_only would report gaps that do not exist; dropping them would hide real defects. That is the G25 counted-AND-listed rule extended one step. The DPL join key comes from CatalogExtract.dpl_refs(), which G42 published for exactly this consumer, rather than being re-derived here -- the rule (the catalog guid is a CATALOG id; the DPL guid lives in registration_source_ref) is not obvious and must have one home, and joining on the wrong one returns a clean-looking zero overlap. ONE DEFECT FOUND IN THIS ITEM'S OWN WORK BY THE J26 DISCIPLINE, worth carrying: the URN parser split from the RIGHT, and the module comment justified it as protecting a dotted db.schema namespace. That reasoning was WRONG -- a dot is not the separator, so left- and right-indexing agree on any well-formed URN, and the injected left-indexed split left the suite green. The real case is a COLON inside platform/namespace, where BOTH readings are wrong (last-two drops db, fields-4-5 drops the table) and neither is detectably so. Now refused as ambiguous and bucketed as unparsed. The test that was supposed to cover it could not tell the two implementations apart -- a guard for a property nobody had tested. 23 tests on synthetic fixtures (no Neo4j, no network, re-runs anywhere per J18); six injected defects each proven to red the suite. J42Nothing checks the backlog union rule a port promises: diff the two repos' item-id sets at the port base and fail the report on a gap

Acceptance: A PORT-TIME check -- not a unit test, because the producer tree cannot see the consumer's -- that reads both repos' SHARDED backlog at the RECORDED PORT BASE, diffs the item-id sets, and FAILS the port report when producer-minus-consumer is non-empty, naming every missing id. THE ID SET IS THE DIRECTORY LISTING: since Y2/ADR 0013 Clause 6 the entry IS the file, so the set is the stem of every docs/restructure/backlog/items/<id>.yaml on each side -- take it from the listing, or from drydocs_core.backlog_store.load_backlog_document(), and NOT by parsing a monolith. THE VACUOUS-GREEN TRAP, which is the whole reason this clause is written out: docs/restructure/backlog.yaml is a TOMBSTONE (sharded 2026-08-20) and has no items[] key at all, so a check aimed at it reads two empty sets, reports "no difference" and passes for being wrong -- exactly the J26 class this item exists to close. The check must therefore FAIL LOUD, not pass, when either side's items directory is absent or empty, and when the id it reads from a filename disagrees with the id inside that file. An explicit allow-list carries ids deliberately not carried across, each with its reason, so that "no difference" and "a difference somebody accepted" are distinguishable in the output rather than both rendering as silence. SCOPE FENCE: this item owns the UNION half only -- never-drop-an-entry. The never-regress-a-status half of the same manifest row is the J16 guard's, which reads the assembled tree through backlog_store.dump_document(); do not re-implement it here. It runs from the reconcile side, where both trees are reachable, and is named in .claude/skills/reconcile-port/SKILL.md and docs/port/port-prompt.md so a session that never opens the manifest still runs it. Proven to FAIL on an injected defect -- one item FILE deleted from the consumer copy -- before it is trusted (J26).

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-11 from Idea-96. PORT-MANIFEST.yaml states the union rule unconditionally for docs/restructure/backlog.yaml ("Union the items; NEVER regress a status ... or drop an entry"), and tests/unit/test_backlog.py enforces plenty about the file -- schema, roll-up arithmetic, next_ready, unknown depends_on -- but every one of those checks looks at ONE copy in isolation. The union is a claim about TWO copies and nothing compares them, so a port that quietly under-delivers items leaves both sides internally consistent and green. Textbook J26: a rule written in prose and enforced by nobody. The near miss that makes it worse -- the dependency guard would have caught it only if a surviving item happened to depend on a missing one, so whether the gap is visible at all is luck rather than design. J52Verification evidence about a local dev server counts only when the session launched the browser itself — record the rule and the recipe in the verify skill

A browser the session merely ATTACHED to is not a known venue, and "verified" without a known venue is the J18 defect in browser form. (b) THE RECIPE IS THERE, NOT JUST THE PROHIBITION: the skill already documents headless Edge for rendered HTML files; it gains the dev-server case — a session-launched headless browser driven from the session scratchpad (the 2026-08-21 close used puppeteer-core against a Vite dev server on an alternate port and behaved correctly throughout), carrying the same "launch from PowerShell/`subprocess`, NOT Git Bash" caveat the skill already states. (c) THE OBSERVATION IS CITED AS AN OBSERVATION: on 2026-08-21 an extension-connected tab at `localhost:5173` served a DryDocs checkout that did not match the working tree while reporting `isLocal: true`, and cache-bypassed fetches from inside that tab disagreed with `curl` against the same address. The reading that the session was attached to another machine's Chrome is UNPROVEN by the entry's own admission and MUST NOT be written into a tracked, ported file as a mechanism — the rule stands on the venue argument, which holds either way. (d) NO MECHANISM CHANGE AND NO CODE: one rule and one recipe in an existing skill. Nothing in `web/` changes; `web/README.md` is an input only because it is where the `?as=<persona>` headless sign-in is already documented, and a one-line cross-reference belongs there if the recipe needs it.

J53The snapshot script's board refresh half-failed and reported a traceback banner with no traceback in it — name the cause, and make a partial render distinguishable from a skipped one
docsP8bugp2sonnet / main
release-infrastructure

Acceptance: (a) THE MESSAGE NAMES A CAUSE. The catch block around the board refresh prints the exception message, which for a failing native command is the FIRST line of stderr — and the first line of a Python failure is always the literal traceback banner. So the warning can never name a cause by construction: it reports the banner and discards the exception. Capture the command's full stderr and print the LAST line (the exception type and message) or the whole block. Proven by making the render fail deliberately and reading the warning. (b) A PARTIAL RUN IS VISIBLE. The refresh is wrapped so it never blocks the snapshot, which is right and stays. But a half-written render set is worse than none: on 2026-08-23 three of the renderer's nine outputs were written and six were left stale, and nothing said which. After this item the warning states which outputs landed and which did not, so the stale-render diff check in the session ritual is run against a known state rather than an unknown one. (c) THE SAME TREATMENT WHERE IT APPLIES. The design-doc refresh immediately below uses the identical catch idiom. Fix both or state why one is different — leaving the sibling with the message that cannot name a cause reproduces the defect the next time it fires. (d) THE REPRODUCTION IS RECORDED, NOT THE MACHINE-SPECIFIC CAUSE ALONE. On this desktop the trigger is the pre-set virtual-environment variable that the script's poetry invocation inherits, so the import resolves against the wrong environment partway through; a user's own terminal is unaffected, which is why it was never seen interactively. That belongs in a comment as the worked example. It is not the fix — the fix is that the message would have named it.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-26 from Idea-158. This is the Idea-111 shape again — an instrument whose failure mode is silence — inside the ritual step that was added to stop exactly that, which is the argument for fixing it rather than remembering it. Module `docs` and epic release-infrastructure follow J52: the snapshot script is cross-cutting session-ritual tooling rather than any component's code. Mechanism only, no gate. p2: it does not corrupt anything, it hides things. CLOSED 2026-08-28 (desktop, advisor-dispatch build; merged --no-ff from a worktree branch). Both refresh blocks (board and design-doc) now share Invoke-RefreshStep/Write-RefreshFailure: the render command's merged stdout+stderr is captured explicitly, LASTEXITCODE is checked directly (the old catch never fired reliably -- in this shell the native stderr never became a terminating error, so the old idiom printed NO warning at all, strictly worse than the groomed description), and on failure the warning names the LAST non-empty output line (the exception type and message) plus a landed/stale list per expected output, compared by mtime before and after the run. Verified against a live reproduction of the desktop VIRTUAL_ENV leak (the clause (d) worked example, now recorded in a comment): the warning read "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'typer'" and listed 3 landed / 6 stale outputs -- the exact 2026-08-23 incident shape. Success path confirmed unchanged (exit 0, all nine wrote lines, no warning); only snapshot.ps1 changed, render byproducts reverted before commit; script parse-checked and test_depgraph_snapshots.py green.

OPTIONAL = the three Operate Manager classes, chief_business_technologist, deployment_owner, deployment_information_owner, application_module_owner, and site_reliability_engineer. G73Inheritance: assertion mode + a modelled ancestor edge, authored rows only — and the ancestor-CI widening that K21 §7.4 needs
ontologyP9taskp2fable / main
seal-attribution
depends on: G70

Acceptance: Per the signed §E. THE LOAD STORES AUTHORED ROWS ONLY: of the three Inheritance states, Direct (blank) and Overridden are AUTHORED; Inherited rows are DERIVED COPIES carrying two lineage pointers. Inheritance is computed, not materialised — storing a derived fact as though asserted is how a graph starts disagreeing with its source. THE ANCESTOR IS A MODELLED EDGE, not a property (§E4 ruled), so "why does this application show a different owner than its parent" is TRAVERSABLE — which is what §D2 says an operator cannot do today. Both lineage references are load-bearing: the ancestor CI and the ancestor ROW. IT IS ONE MECHANISM UP AN N-LEVEL CHAIN, not a two-level relation (§E1e): "copy from the nearest ancestor holding the role", applied repeatedly. A model built for a fixed application→deployment relation cannot represent the observed pass-through case, where a role originates two rungs up and passes straight through the application untouched. OVERRIDES PROPAGATE: a child inherits the ancestor's CURRENT value even when that value is itself an Override, so the effective holder can differ from the top of the chain. AND IT AMENDS THE PULL SCOPE — this is the item that carries it. Reconstructing an inherited holder requires ANCESTOR CIs, which sit ABOVE the ~200 applications DryDocs supports, including CIs owned by teams it does not. K21 §7.4 is amended to take ancestor CIs FOR THEIR TOM ROWS ONLY, and the amendment is written there rather than left implicit.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 at the G35 sign-off. This is the first place the ~200-application boundary and the inheritance model actually conflict, and the gate crossed it deliberately rather than quietly. The alternative — materialise inherited rows and flag them derived — stays inside the boundary and was considered and rejected: it duplicates, and it drifts when an ancestor changes. DONE 2026-08-27 (laptop, Lane B). TWO EDGES REGISTERED, BOTH status planned (nothing loads on either side today; the G72 servicenow-tom surface is what the future loader stamps): (1) business_application_contained_by_ci (CONTAINED_BY, BusinessApplication -> AreaProduct | BusinessApplication, in 41) — the SS-E4 modelled ancestor, NAMED FOR WHAT THE SOURCE ASSERTS (cmdb_rel_ci "Contained by", endpoints-in-seed per K21 7.4), never for the computation over it; the note answers K22's declined-containment decision on K22's own terms (catalog rollup vs the cmdb chain whose ancestors the catalog will never hold), cites the C8 reuse of INSTANTIATES for the DeploymentModule rung, records SS-E1e's one-mechanism- N-level walk + override propagation, and records assertion_mode semantics (direct | overridden; the source's blank IS Direct; inherited NEVER stored). (2) human_attribution_derived_from (WAS_DERIVED_FROM, Attribution -> Attribution, prov:wasDerivedFrom, in 52 — the per-domain rule split the pair across two fragments though the item listed only 41) — the ancestor-ROW pointer, registered so a materialised projection (O44) has a shape instead of inventing one; the note states registration is not a licence to materialise (the rejected alternative stays rejected). assertion_mode is NOT a property_terms row — that section is standard-CURIE bindings and PROV has no term shaped like it; semantics live in the edge notes. K21 7.4 AMENDED IN PLACE, dated blockquote + take-table row: ancestor CIs of seeded applications, N levels UP, FOR THEIR TOM ROWS ONLY — and the amendment reconciles the standing depth caution (that sentence is the OUTWARD/DOWNWARD hop and stands untouched; upward is bounded by the chain's height). schema_graph.cypher regenerated (C8 render). G74The :Employee backbone — hierarchy placement (§B7's deferral has no owner) AND the creation policy, where the runbook forbids exactly what seal_applications.cypher does
ontologyP9taskp3fable / main
seal-attribution

Acceptance: TWO CLAUSES, one backbone. Per the signed §B7. The TOM load links an Attribution to a PERSON and stops; placing that person in the reporting structure is separate work on a separate cadence. THE DEFERRAL CURRENTLY POINTS AT NOTHING, which is what this item fixes: :Employee is a node class with NO Employee-to-Employee edge anywhere in the relationship vocabulary — no REPORTS_TO, no manager edge — and until this item there was no backlog entry that would create one. Scope: propose the edge and its provenance, route it through docs/RELATIONSHIP_GUIDE.md and the relationship-vocabulary registry as status: planned, and identify the SOURCE that could populate it. DO NOT BUILD A LOADER — the source question is the real one, and the producer-side HR hierarchy direction (two-scope HR supplement, two-pass loader, REPORTS_TO current-state sweep) is company-gated work that this item must not pre-empt. A CLOSER SOURCE MAY EXIST: group-scoped TOM roles resolve to sys_user_group MEMBERS today, which is a people-graph of a different shape — adjacency rather than hierarchy. Say whether that is a route or a distraction. SECOND CLAUSE, ADDED 2026-08-11 (SME, from a desktop session) — RULE THE :Employee CREATION POLICY, BECAUSE THE DOC AND THE CODE CONTRADICT EACH OTHER AND BOTH ARE DEFENSIBLE. The runbook's "backbone-and-enrich" rule, in BOTH v2 and the published v3, states that :Employee is created ONLY by load-employee-roster and that SEAL attaches enrich-only via OPTIONAL MATCH — "a SID not in the roster gets no edge, never a stub". seal_applications.cypher does the OPPOSITE: it MERGEs (e:Employee {employee_id: <owner/CTO/info-owner SID>}) ON CREATE SET e.source = 'SEAL', minting placeholders. DIRECTION LANDED 2026-08-18 (SME in-chat, gate-log RECORD same date): STUB-AND-ENRICH WINS. "The HR database has ~300k; my expectation is that it will be the stub and supplemented with HR data later." The loader behavior is the policy; the runbook text is what must change. What this item still owes: harmonize the runbook (v2 + published v3), rule the stub property idiom (what marks awaiting-enrichment beyond `source`), and clause 1 (REPORTS_TO + its source) in full. pat_team_roles.cypher was flipped to the MERGE-stub idiom in the RECORD's commit. MEASURED STATE (desktop graph, 2026-08-11): 11,464 :Employee nodes, ALL source='SEAL', every one minted by the seal_applications load. They carry employee_id + full_name and NO REPORTS_TO — there is no HR backbone yet. 11,445 are HAS_AGENT targets of ownership attributions; 19 are unattached (likely CTO/info-owner SIDs whose attribution did not land, or delete leftovers). THE MECHANISM IS SOUND AND SELF-RECONCILING, which is why this is a ruling and not a bug: load-employee-roster MERGEs on the SAME key and unconditionally flips source SEAL -> HR (authoritative), so a SID in both is upgraded and gains the REPORTS_TO backbone, a roster-only SID is created fresh as HR, and a SID in SEAL but in no loaded HR subtree STAYS source='SEAL'. That residual is a COVERAGE REPORT, not debris — count the source='SEAL' survivors after a roster load and you have the owners HR did not cover. The placeholders are intentional and keyed to reconcile. RULE ONE OF TWO, and record which: (a) FIX THE DOC to describe the placeholder pattern, keeping the code's behaviour — it preserves the ownership SID and name that would otherwise be LOST whenever the roster is not loaded, and the source flag keeps them cleanly reconcilable; or (b) FIX THE LOADER to OPTIONAL MATCH, if roster-only really is the intent — at the cost of dropping ownership identity when the roster is absent. NOT A MID-LOAD DECISION and not urgent: the graph is safe to run load-employee-roster against as it stands. What is NOT acceptable is leaving a design doc that forbids what the loader does, since the next reader trusts whichever they happen to open. THE RULING HAS A COMPANY-SIDE HALF, VERIFIED PRODUCER-SIDE 2026-08-11 — DO NOT RULE IT HERE ALONE. Only ONE of the three surfaces is producer-side: drydocs/loaders/cypher/seal_applications.cypher DOES mint the placeholders, at lines 145 / 169 / 192, for app_owner_sid, chief_tech_officer_sid and info_owner_sid respectively — checkable from here. The OTHER TWO ARE NOT. There is no employee-roster loader producer-side (no load-employee-roster verb, no roster cypher; the port-prompt already records tests/unit/test_employee_roster.py as company-only, T21), and the "backbone-and-enrich" runbook prose that FORBIDS the stub appears in no producer runbook under docs/design/. So the producer holds the code that mints, and the company holds both the doc that forbids it AND the loader that reconciles it. CONSEQUENCE: the producer can rule what ITS loader should do, but it cannot fix a doc it does not have, and it cannot verify the reconciliation half. Route this ruling through the port rather than landing it one-sided — the same asymmetry class as RELAY-6, and it is the second time this session that a producer-side item turned out to overlap company-only material.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 at the G35 sign-off, on the SME's instruction that the deferral needed an owner. Deliberately p3 and dependency-free: it blocks nothing and nothing blocks it, and it exists so a correct deferral stops being an omission with better wording. THE SECOND CLAUSE ARRIVED THE SAME DAY and belongs here rather than in its own item because it is the SAME BACKBONE: clause one asks what creates the Employee-to-Employee edge, clause two asks what is allowed to create the :Employee NODE. Ruling the second without the first would settle the node policy while leaving the hierarchy homeless, and ruling the first without the second would build a backbone on top of an unruled creation policy. The doc-vs-code contradiction was found by a desktop session reading the loader against the runbook, and it is the kind that survives because each surface is internally consistent — only reading both together exposes it. MERGED IN 2026-08-12 (groom, desktop) — Idea-73, "where does the employee hierarchy come from, and does it live producer-side at all", filed 2026-08-05 and open since. It is this item's clause one asked from the other end, so it rides here rather than opening a second owner. Three things it adds that the acceptance should carry through the ruling: (1) THERE IS A SECOND WAITING CONSUMER besides §B7 — O44's first column is an ownership-reconciliation view whose MANAGER FILTER is its whole point, so two committed directions currently defer to a structure that does not exist; (2) pat:people-report is NOT the source — it carries TEAMS, not reporting lines, so the closest producer-side people data cannot populate a hierarchy (G82's projection does not change that); (3) the 2026-07-23 producer-session HR-hierarchy direction — single :Employee backbone, two-scope HR supplement, two-pass loader, REPORTS_TO current-state sweep — was written FOR THE COMPANY hr-emp-hierarchy gate, which is the likeliest reason nothing landed here. So the honest outcomes include "the producer records explicitly that both halves are company-side": a deferral pointing at nothing is an omission with better wording, and saying so counts as ruling it. DONE 2026-08-27 (laptop, Lane B). CLAUSE 1 IN FULL: human_employee_reports_to registered (REPORTS_TO, Employee -> Employee, 52-local-human.yaml, status planned) — maps to org:reportsTo with the Agent->Agent PROV row deliberately not reached for (a reporting line is org structure, not activity delegation; recorded in the entry). SOURCE IDENTIFIED, NOT LOADED: the company HR hierarchy database via the company hr-emp-hierarchy gate (the 2026-07-23 direction — single spine, two-scope supplement, two-pass loader, current-state sweep); no producer loader built, per the acceptance. sys_user_group RULED A DISTRACTION for this edge (adjacency, not hierarchy; the real people-graph it is belongs to snow-hpsm-queue-to-group) — in the entry so it is not re-proposed. Both waiting consumers (SS-B7's later pass, O44's manager filter) named in the entry. CLAUSE 2, the producer half: the stub property idiom is RULED — `source` IS the awaiting-enrichment marker and nothing else is minted (a non-HR value = stub; the survivor count after a roster load IS the HR-coverage report); recorded on the Employee class row in 10-node-classifications.yaml beside the stub-and-enrich policy (SME 2026-08-18 RECORD), which the loaders already implement — no loader change. THE COMPANY HALF IS ROUTED, NOT RULED HERE (the acceptance's own instruction): runbook v2+v3 harmonization and reconciliation verification ride the next port — handed to the desktop Lane A session for the port-prompt relay (this session does not edit Lane A port surfaces). schema_graph.cypher regenerated. Notes: Groomed 2026-08-05 (desktop) from Idea-66 + Idea-69, with Idea-63b and Idea-68 riding as clauses. WHY (a) IS THE BIGGER HALF and was the surprise: this looked like a steward capture exercise until the SME supplied the DAT SRE Framework -> APPCODE table. The platform list is CLOSED AT SIX CODES and positions 3-5 of the folder prefix decide the tier, so tier assignment is MECHANICALLY DERIVABLE — a six-row list plus a name parse, not a data-entry backlog. It also means this item does NOT depend on the SME's owed tier-1/tier-2 enumeration (Idea-28): that enumeration is needed to RESOLVE a tier-2 code's consumers, not to recognize one. THE FAILURE IT PREVENTS IS SILENT AND LOOKS CORRECT. `AOC -> <platform SEAL>` is a TRUE statement about the platform and a false one about the consumer folders it would be stamped on. Both AOC (the datalake / Ab Initio platform) and DCL (the DPL launcher spine) are shared codes whose folders serve many consuming applications, and the only in-file hint of platform-ness is the word "Platform" in `descr` — the untrustworthy column. Nothing is mis-written TODAY only because no producer-side platform code has been authored yet. RIDER (Idea-63b): `descr` is a CORROBORATION signal with a known-imperfect base rate, never a validity test and never a derivation source. If this item compares column 2 to the head of column 3 at all, the output is a REVIEW QUEUE of disagreeing rows for a human — candidate stale renames, decommissioned SEALs, copy-paste — not a pass/fail gate. RIDER (Idea-68), cosmetic and do it here or not at all: "tier" names two things — the K7 row-kind (a STRING enum seal-born|platform|dual-coded) and the K2 match precedence (an INT, 1 SEAL .. 5 manual). The value spaces do not collide, so a `tier` edge property is not ambiguous in practice and this is naming hygiene rather than a correctness risk — but `row_kind` vs `match_tier` is worth renaming BEFORE either surfaces in a QuerySpec, and this item is already in both files. DISAGREEMENT RULE (added at claim, 2026-08-05): clause (a) gives the loader TWO tier signals for an authored code — the name-derived tier and the row's declared kind — and the acceptance did not say which wins when they disagree (e.g. a steward authors a tier-1 row for a code the name parse says is platform). Ruling, on the Idea-63b pattern and the S10 refusal precedent: a disagreement NEVER resolves silently. The name derivation wins for BLOCKING fan-out — a platform-prefixed code never fans out code-level even if its row claims tier-1 — and the disagreeing row lands in the review queue with both signals shown; a human re-authors or the list is corrected. The inverse disagreement (row declares platform, name parse says application) blocks nothing but queues the same way. DONE 2026-08-05 (desktop, 1386faf): (a) built — load_platform_codes (values twin internal/standards/technology/platform-codes.yaml, six codes; missing file = guard inert) + platform_prefix pos3-5 + the resolver guard (blocked fan-out queues a RowKindDisagreement, folders surface platform-unresolved; inverse queues without blocking); row-level tests cover a platform prefix AND an application prefix. (b) built — validate_app_code_row: platform code-level row now REQUIRES the platform's own app_id + rationale (declare-by-absence retired; legacy empty-app_id shape still reads as a declaration in the resolver, defensively); store schema v3. (c) built — declared-code folders already surfaced platform-unresolved; the guard now routes derived-platform codes there too. Idea-68 rider APPLIED: tier -> row_kind end to end (column, CSV header, wire, model, edge property, steward screen); K2 match tiers keep their name (no property surfaces, nothing to rename). Idea-63b rider NOT EXERCISED: no descr comparison was built (the rider is conditional; the review-queue rule stands recorded for whoever builds one). COMPANY-SIDE: header+edge-property renames ride the T23 migration family — their tier-authored rows re-author as row_kind; live r.tier edges migrate with the K8 reload. Suite 1597 green. K19 unblocks.

Only mechanism is recorded here; anything value-bearing stays company-side. Three deliverables. (1) THE WORKING QUERY, transcribed as MECHANISM into the ServiceNow/TOM material: the join spine is `x_<scope>_cmdb_tom_main` -> `x_<scope>_cmdb_tom_roles` (role -> sys_id, active) -> `cmdb_ci` (parent_id) -> `core_company` -> `cmdb_ci_service_discovered` -> `sys_user_group` (group, and again on assignment_group) -> `cmdb_ci_business_app`, with the CI self-join on `inherited_from_ci`. The columns that matter to DryDocs are named and mapped to our vocabulary: `u_seal_application_id` / `u_seal_deployment_id` (the SEAL join), `correlation_id`, `sys_class_name`, `inheritance` / `inherited_from_ci`, `u_status`, `u_application_state`, `u_external_service`, and the role/group/team names. State which of those the TOM-role gates (G35, seal-tom-attribution-reshape) already assume and which are NEW evidence. (2) THE VIEW INVENTORY as taxonomy: the replica exposes one `V_`-prefixed view per ServiceNow table across several `DW_*_DATA_VIEW` schemas (a common/CMDB one, an ITSM one, and at least two others). Capture the view -> ServiceNow-table naming rule and the schema split; that rule is what keeps `origin: snow` unambiguous while the carrier is Snowflake, and it is currently asserted in a comment with nothing behind it. (3) THE PRECISION QUESTION, which is the point of the item rather than a rider: the sample query is a hand-built REPORT — it filters to one company, one application state set, one SEAL id and one named CI. That is not an ingestion contract. Decide what DryDocs should actually pull, and justify it against the PUBLIC ServiceNow CMDB documentation (the tables are stock ServiceNow, so their canonical columns, `sys_class_name` hierarchy and CI-relationship model are all publicly documented and can be read from the web without touching the estate) — the vendor doc is the baseline, the replica is the instance, and where they disagree the difference is a company extension worth naming. Specifically rule whether the CI-relationship tables (`cmdb_rel_ci` and the `cmdb_rel_*` family visible in the navigator) belong in the pull, since a CMDB without its relationship rows is a node list rather than a graph. Output is an analysis document plus, if warranted, a DRAFT dataset row for the registry under the `snow@[db].[schema].<servicenow_table>` grammar with `confirmed: false`. NO source is activated, no loader is built and no gate is signed inside this item — a real pull scope is a gate decision.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-09 (desktop) on SME direction, from DBeaver screenshots of the replica the SME will query. WHY THE LAPTOP: the screenshots live there, and they are Internal — moving them to reach a different session is the wrong direction of travel. CONTEXT THIS ITEM DEPENDS ON, so it is not re-derived: ServiceNow metadata is NOT read from ServiceNow. It is read from an AWS Snowflake REPLICA, which is the same shape as Control-M being read from the Oracle `psgmgr` replica rather than from the orchestrator. So `snowflake` is the CARRIER and `snow` keeps the ORIGIN slot — recorded on both system entries in config/source-registry.yaml 2026-08-09 with guards, after the SME flagged SNOW/Snowflake as an IMPORTANT confusion. The v2 grammar already ruled this ("replica grammar: origin catalog, carrier snowflake"). WHY THE PUBLIC-DOC LEG IS WORTH THE TIME rather than shortcutting to the replica: these are STOCK ServiceNow tables, so the vendor documents the canonical schema publicly. That gives a baseline the estate cannot supply — it tells us which columns are ServiceNow's and which are local extensions (the `u_` prefix and the `x_<scope>_` scoped app are the two local classes visible in the sample), and a column we invent a meaning for because we only ever saw it in one hand-built report is exactly the kind of assumption T10/T13 exist to prevent. Route the vendor lookup through the reference-librarian agent and register what it finds in reference/REGISTRY.yaml, the same way BMC and Oracle are held. RELATIONSHIP TO THE OPEN TOM GATES: G35 (TOM-roles enumeration, in progress) and seal-tom-attribution-reshape both reason about role classes and cardinality from the SEAL side. This item supplies the ServiceNow-side evidence they have been arguing without — the `tom_roles` join and its `active` flag are the live shape of exactly what G35 is trying to enumerate. Those are CARRIER artifacts of the data-lake replication, not vendor schema — exactly the vendor-baseline-vs-instance difference clause (3) exists to name, now with a concrete first example. (c) `delete_flag` MAKES SOFT DELETES AN INGESTION CONTRACT QUESTION, not a detail: if rows persist in the replica after deletion in ServiceNow, then any pull that ignores the flag ingests dead CIs and dead edges as live ones. Rule it explicitly. The D7 tombstone idiom is the obvious precedent — we already distinguish removed-from-source from never-existed, and this is the same problem arriving from a different source. (d) THE SERVICENOW AUDIT ENVELOPE IS PRESENT: `sys_created_by` / `sys_created_on` / `sys_updated_by` / `sys_updated_on` map cleanly onto the four frozen envelope property names, so a `config/audit-fields.yaml` entry for any snow dataset is a real mapping rather than another stub — unlike most sources ruled at audit-envelope-phase4. `dwintel_dl_snapshot_dt` is replication time and is EXCLUDED under the standing CAPTURE_DATE rule.
