K25Cross-application run_as: detect and count jobs whose run-as account belongs to a DIFFERENT application than the folder that runs them
configP9taskp2sonnet / main
seal-attribution
depends on: K16

Acceptance: SME direction 2026-08-19, raised with the two-source FID evidence: a job's run_as account can belong to a different application than the folder's own attribution, and that case needs an item of its own rather than a footnote. The gate's §G MALCOLM counterexample already proved one INSTANCE (registered-to-platform, attributed-to-product); this item makes the CLASS measurable. (a) A detection over the census join: for every Control-M run_as owner resolvable through the id-owner listing (doc 09 Source B), compare the FID's application assignment against the folder's confirmed attribution; emit counts by outcome — same application / different application / unresolvable — never a row dump (the K16 discipline; the output is Internal and lands company-side). (b) The different-application bucket is broken down by the gate's §G5 readings (different subjects both correct / stale directory / wrong folder attribution) the same parked-until-ruled way the census handles disagreements: every case starts unruled, a human rules each, and the unruled count is itself reportable. (c) NOTHING is written to the graph and no edge is proposed here — if the SME wants cross-application run_as expressed as an edge or a property, that is a K17-gate amendment, and this item's output is the evidence it would cite. (d) The known-legitimate shared-platform case (the 171-way agent account measured 2026-08-19) is handled as a NAMED expectation, not a finding: a shared platform FID serving many applications' folders is the EXPECTED shape of that account class, so the detector must separate account-class-expected sharing from genuine cross-application anomalies, or the report drowns. SME CLARIFICATION 2026-08-19, and it upgrades (d) from a filter to a CLASSIFICATION: the 171-way name IS the Control-M platform user — the account jobs run as when they run as Control-M itself — and the class is cross-platform (Informatica carries several platform accounts under which business-application jobs run). So the detector's first cut is run_as CLASS (application FID / platform-user account / unresolvable), the platform-user bucket is EXPECTED to disagree with folder attribution by construction and resolves through the platform's own attribution chain instead of the directory, and the by-class counts are themselves a deliverable (how much of the estate runs as the platform is a number nobody has). How a platform account is RECOGNIZED (curated list vs the directory's type/purpose columns) is a K17 §D/§G ruling this item must not preempt — it may propose, with evidence. JOB-GRAIN EVIDENCE 2026-08-19 (SME captures, a live legacy-LOB folder): the class splits INSIDE one folder — the FileWatcher job runs as the platform account while the folder default (the payload jobs) runs as the application's account. So (e) the detector classifies PER JOB, never per folder, and reports run_as class BY JOB TYPE: FileWatcher x platform-account is the designed pattern (file watching is a platform service); the countable anomaly is a PAYLOAD job running as the platform. A folder-grain read would have reported this folder as application-run and missed the split entirely.

Notes: Direct add 2026-08-19 (desktop, SME direction at the K16 two-source evidence session). depends_on K16 because the detection runs over the same census join the counts come from — building it before the census has real rows would validate it against nothing. Sonnet: the acceptance is a written pass/fail over a defined join. Priority p2 with K16: this is the measurable half of the §G registration-vs-attribution problem, and the gate's §G3 ruling on the K2 FID tier will want these numbers in front of it. DONE 2026-08-26 (desktop). THE STATUS CALL, made explicitly because K16 — the dependency — sits in_progress on the same company-side event: K16's acceptance demands REAL COUNTS, which this repo structurally cannot produce; K25's acceptance asks for A DETECTION, and every clause (a)-(e) is implemented and synthetic-tested, so done is the honest state HERE while the numbers themselves remain company-side. The runner is docs/company-prompts/k25-run-as-detection-company-prompt.md, and its run is the SAME event K16's 0-counts row awaits — doc 09's phase table now carries a 0-K25 method row saying exactly that. `drydocs/run_as_detect.py` (fid_census's sibling: pure, stdlib-only for the same porting reason, counts-only BY RETURN TYPE — int/bool/str->int fields, a row dump unexpressible, pinned structurally and by a serialized-output sweep that asserts no injected identifier escapes; job-TYPE strings are the one deliberate non-count content, they are TASK_TYPE vocabulary not identifiers). THE FIRST CUT IS RUN_AS CLASS per the 2026-08-19 SME clarification: platform_user / application_fid / unresolvable, per JOB and never per folder — the fixture reproduces the SME's live in-folder split (FileWatcher on the platform account beside payload jobs on the application account) and asserts a folder-grain read could not express it. FileWatcher x platform is the DESIGNED pattern (PLATFORM_EXPECTED_JOB_TYPES, a declared constant with the ruling cited); the countable anomaly is a PAYLOAD job on the platform, broken down by job type. INTERPRETATION STATED for "resolves through the platform's own attribution chain": platform-class jobs are COUNTED AND EXCLUDED from the directory comparison — no platform-chain resolution is built here and no input for one exists; the by-class counts (how much of the estate runs as the platform) are the deliverable the SME named. PLATFORM RECOGNITION IS NOT PREEMPTED (the K17 §D/§G fence): platform_accounts is an INJECTED set — the seam whatever K17 rules feeds — and doc 09's S3 spread-ranking + SME confirmation is the standing evidence-backed proposal for filling it; an empty set is legal and tested. Platform wins over directory presence (the 171-way name IS a directory row — that is WHY recognition cannot be "is it registered") and the overlap is a visible counter. OUTCOMES (a): same / different / unresolvable for application-class jobs only, with unresolvable counted BY REASON (folder_unattributed vs job_carried_no_folder — different facts). §G5 (b): the different bucket splits at CASE grain — a distinct (account, attributed application) pair, so fifty jobs sharing one disagreement are ONE case for a human — every case parks unruled, rulings are injected, an unknown reading is refused, and the unruled count is itself reportable. (c): nothing touches the graph, no edge proposed; the output is the evidence a K17 amendment would cite. Case handling: trim-only normalization with the caller-normalizes contract (the K16 2026-08-12 ruling), and case-only near-misses are counted on BOTH joins — directory AND platform set — after the review pass caught the platform-side silent-miss gap. TESTS: 13 in tests/unit/test_run_as_detect.py, synthetic throughout; THREE MUTATIONS all caught (directory-before-platform recognition; unruled silently inferred as different_subjects; the designed-pattern set emptied). MODULE_MAP row + module-boundary registration (drydocs-review, beside fid_census, same reasoning). Suite 2540 passed / 11 skipped, ruff clean, CLI gates green.

TWO FACTS TO KNOW BEFORE OPENING THE FILE, both verified at the groom. This is one of the few surfaces where an artifact-design pass is legitimate. PLACEMENT: no target-state section exists today. Nearest existing homes are "The loop that makes it a system, not an inventory" (the operational-outcome section) and "Honest about the gaps" (for (c)); a short section of its own is also reasonable. DEPENDENCY-FREE ON PURPOSE: stating a goal needs neither the report (G58) nor a formal term. If a coined term ever lands, it rides a gate and the overview follows it, not the other way round. CLOSED 2026-08-07 (laptop) as overview rev 8. THREE DECISIONS TAKEN AT THE BUILD, recorded because the acceptance left each open. (b) MANUAL rows carry `format: csv | ascii | json` plus `drop_dir:`, whose COMMITTED value is the landing-zone CONVENTION -- DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT-relative, the `controlm-xml/` precedent, resolved by drydocs_core/data_root.py. The real directory lives ONLY in the internal twin (the `locator.extract: ~` discipline, unchanged): no real path, host or share name is ever committed (Scan D / J27 class). (c) AUTOMATED rows carry `via: api | db` plus the pull's coordinates BY REFERENCE, never restated -- for `db` the row's own dataset id already names the qualified object ({origin}@{db}.{schema}.{table}); for `api` the row names the CALL SURFACE, with the G96 Control-M adapter (drydocs_core/adapters/controlm/api.py) as the worked example. SYSTEM rows are unchanged, and the doc corpora in config/doc-source-registry.yaml are OUT of scope here (they already carry `connector:`); extending the field to that ledger is a separate call. (g) TWO FENCES. This item RECORDS mode -- it builds NO watcher, mover or copier for the drop directories. And it does NOT rule the FLIP (who flips manual -> automated, on what evidence, and how that relates to the override -> source-corrected flip): that ruling is N13's, via the gate. Full suite green.

(a) FIRST CONCRETE SURFACE, NAMED: the seal-contact override domain -- drydocs/loaders/seal_contacts.py reading the SEAL contact extract against the `seal_contact_override` rows O24 materializes from config/overrides/seal-contact-overrides.csv. (b) TWO HANDS, STRUCTURALLY (§B2/§B3): the load PROPOSES and a STEWARD confirms. It rides the draft mechanism that already exists rather than inventing a second one -- drydocs_core.mapping_store.add_draft and the commit-by-replace override draft path -- so an unattended run can only ever leave an OPEN DRAFT. Auto-retire was offered at the gate and DECLINED (coincidental agreement must not silently retire a correction that was masking a different defect), so a test asserts a detection run leaves every `seal_contact_override.status` value untouched. (c) HISTORY IS KEPT (§B4): confirming a candidate ARCHIVES the override row dated with its agreement evidence (which load run, which source value, observed when) -- the row is never deleted and the correction stays readable afterwards. Today's status CHECK is ('active','corrected-in-seal'); extending that enum and/or the evidence columns is part of this item and rides the committed-CSV -> mapping.db materialization, so the committed list stays the source of record and the store stays rebuildable. (d) FENCES: the detection writes NO graph (§A3; O24's rule that overrides never write the graph is unchanged), never fails a load, never blocks CI, and never treats "no candidates" as an error (§C3 class). The K7 §E2 permanent-by-nature domains are not scanned at all -- the app-code mapping store has no corrected-in-source lifecycle BY RULING (§D1). (e) SCOPE FENCE ON UI: this item builds the detection, the proposal record and the read path a surface can consume. Rendering the candidate flag on the /mappings pane or as a column in N14's union report is a FOLLOW-ON, not this item. Tests cover agreement detected, disagreement ignored, an already corrected-in-seal row skipped, and the no-flip assertion. Full suite green.

EXACTLY ONE resolution lands, recorded in the close note (the A4 idiom): (a) WIDEN AND ENFORCE -- the field becomes a declared enum covering the values actually in use, with a test that a loader cannot ship an undeclared one; (b) RE-DEFINE -- the field means the acquisition CARRIER rather than the file format, and the format values move to where N12's `acquisition.format` already records them, so the two ledgers stop describing the same fact differently; (c) RETIRE THE COMMENT -- the field is free text by design, the comment goes, and what the value is FOR is written down instead. Whatever is ruled must state the collision so a reader of either does not import the other's meaning. (ii) THE VALUE REACHES THE GRAPH: base.py sets `run.source = $source_label` on the run envelope, so this is not a code-local label -- it is provenance a consumer reads. O27QuerySpec authoring conventions: consume gated edges not raw staging columns; canonical external ref grammar; no graph element ids on external surfaces
drydocs-apiP12chorep3sonnet / main
web-console

Acceptance: A conventions section (drydocs_api/ docstring or a sibling doc, discoverable from query_specs.py) records three rules with rationale: (a) specs read gate-confirmed materialized edges and properties, never re-derive meaning from raw staged columns (precedence resolution lives in the loaders — the Backstage consume-the-relation-not-the-spec-field rule); (b) a canonical external ref grammar kind:namespace/name (namespace = data center where names collide across the 4 DCs) is defined for deep links and export manifests; (c) graph-internal element ids / uids never appear in URLs, manifests, or exports (documented as unstable). Existing registry specs are audited against (a) with violations fixed or flagged; a registry invariant or unit test enforces (c) where mechanical.

Notes: Groomed 2026-07-22 from assessment T2+T3 (one conventions home: two consumption rules + the ref grammar). p3 — largely codifies what O11 already does. CLOSED 2026-08-01. drydocs_api/AUTHORING.md holds the three rules with rationale, linked from query_specs.py's module docstring. The audit found the registry ALREADY compliant on all three — which was the point worth writing down: compliance was a property of careful authoring, not of the system, so nothing would have caught the first violation. Three things the work changed relative to how the item was framed: (1) The ref-grammar namespace is NOT the data center. O27 was groomed "namespace = data center where names collide across the 4 DCs"; checked against drydocs_core/schema/constraints.cypher that holds for exactly ONE node kind (ControlMHostGroup's (data_center, name) NODE KEY). ControlMJob and Condition — the two kinds most likely to appear in a deep link — are FOLDER-scoped ((folder_id, job_id) and (folder_id, name)). The rule shipped as "namespace = the declared uniqueness scope", which yields the data center where the key says so and the folder where it does not, and self-maintains because a new loader's NODE KEY already states its namespace. The doc's table is held to the constraint file by test_authoring_doc_namespace_table_matches_declared_keys — otherwise it would be a record checkable only against itself. (2) Rule (a) needed its NON-violations stated, or it would push authors into worse Cypher. explorer.conditions.v2's property join looks like a violation and is not: folder_id is a declared NODE KEY component, so the join resolves identity rather than re-deriving a relationship. Flagged not fixed — no folder->condition edge exists (conditions attach to JOBS via REQUIRES_IN_CONDITION/EMITS_OUT_CONDITION), and materialising one is an ontology decision for the gate, never a read-spec edit. (3) The element-id guard went where the RISK is, not where the item pointed. The acceptance said "a registry invariant"; the registry is hand-authored and reviewed and had zero violations, while the ephemeral path (R4) carries LLM-authored Cypher into the same export/manifest code. Guarding only the registry would have put the check on the path that cannot fail. Both paths now call one guard.ensure_no_element_ids — placed in guard.py beside ensure_read_only, which also earns it _code_regions' comment/string stripping (RETURN 'id(' as data cannot false-positive; the ADR 0003 lesson) and its lower-casing, which is what makes the check case-insensitive across ElementId( / ID( spellings. The text2cypher prompt carries the rule too: the prompt prevents, the guard catches. Zero first-party elementId uses exist repo-wide, so all of it is regression-only. Suite 1277 passed / 5 skipped (was 1272); ruff check + format clean.

O28Node status envelope for the inspector + hub health glyphs: per-source namespaced status items, derived never hand-authored (status.items pattern)
drydocs-webP12requirementp3sonnet / main
web-console

Acceptance: A documented node-status envelope — a list of per-source items {type (source-namespaced), level (info|warning|error), message, error?}, always DERIVED by a producing system, never hand-authored — is adopted as the contract for the inspector sidebar's status section and the landing hub's spoke health glyphs; at least ONE real producer is wired end-to-end (first candidate: the loader per-run WARN/reject stream attaching to its :JobRun / loaded nodes) through a QuerySpec returning that shape; the envelope doc records the Backstage status.items precedent and the rule that new sources add namespaced types, never new shapes.

Notes: Groomed 2026-07-22 from assessment T5. Requirement (future capability) — the layer-4 context-graph surface in the UI; p3 until a module needs live health. CLOSED 2026-08-01. Contract in knowledge/standards/node-status-envelope.md (Backstage status.items precedent recorded, plus the two rules: always DERIVED by a producing system, and new sources add NAMESPACED TYPES never new shapes). Producer = BaseLoader._close_run via status_items_for(), a PURE function of the run summary — which is what makes "always derived" a testable property rather than a promise (8 tests, no database). Wire = loads.status-items.v1, live end-to-end as the /loads Status frame: loader derives -> rides the :JobRun -> spec unwinds -> SpecGrid renders. UI adoption via one shared component (StatusItems + HealthGlyph) used by BOTH the Explorer inspector's status section and the landing hub's spoke glyphs, so a new producer lights both with no UI change. Four design decisions worth keeping: (1) A PROPERTY on :JobRun, not a node + relationship. A relationship type is an ontology decision that goes through the HITL gate (CLAUDE.md §1), and a derived health signal has no ontological meaning to gate — modelling it as an edge would have made every future producer's rollout gate-bound for no semantic gain. This is why O28 could close without a gate session. (2) JSON strings, not parallel lists. Neo4j cannot hold a map inside a list property; parallel lists (status_types/status_levels/...) would put the envelope's integrity in the ALIGNMENT of three lists, where one mismatched append silently mislabels an item's severity. One string per item cannot desynchronise. (3) NO all-clear item. A clean run stores an empty list, so "healthy" (a producer ran, nothing to report) stays distinguishable from "unknown" (no :JobRun at all). Collapsing them is how a dashboard ends up green because nothing is watching — the hub renders every spoke except loads as UNKNOWN today, deliberately, rather than a false green. (4) The demo inspector is fed through the SAME parser as the live path (demoStatus.ts authors JSON strings, parseStatusItems reads them), so a shape change breaks the demo surface loudly instead of leaving it rendering a format nothing produces. Scope note: the Explorer inspector's items are demo-derived because that canvas is the SYNTHESIZED demo graph — wiring it to live data needs a demo->live selection bridge that does not exist. That is graph plumbing, not contract work; the acceptance's "at least ONE real producer wired end-to-end" is met by the /loads Status frame, which is fully live. The O42 component-ledger guard fired on the new component and was answered rather than silenced: StatusItems is registered UNBOUND (26/63) because it serves two modules, so binding it to either would misstate it. Suite 1285 passed / 5 skipped; ruff clean; tsc + vite build clean.

Notes: Found 2026-07-31 while answering "which React components are part of the UI": the answer had to be assembled with `find`, because nothing inventories them. Verified, not assumed — (1) the latest snapshot's scan list is Python roots only: drydocs, drydocs_core, drydocs_api, drydocs_remediation, drydocs_lineage, drydocs_deepdoc, tests; (2) MODULE_MAP.md has no web/tsx entry, and the modules registry says so explicitly — drydocs-web is "not a Python package, so absent from MODULE_MAP.md/test_module_boundary.py"; (3) the software registry is the THIRD-PARTY ledger, so first-party components correctly do not belong there (that file's own scope note: the catalog long tail stays out). That is exactly the class of defect Epic U was created to find in the Python tree; the front end simply was never in the scan. Option (b) is a legitimate answer, not a cop-out: the front end may not earn a graph. But it must be a decision rather than an omission. PARTIALLY ANSWERED 2026-07-31, same session (user directive: "create another sub-ledger for only our UI that links from the first"): config/taxonomy/ui-components.yaml now inventories all 62 components by area, joined to the software registry's `react` product through a RECIPROCAL pointer (ledger -> framework/stack, product -> components), the same shape as `documentation:` on the controlm product. A bidirectional drift guard (tests/unit/test_ui_components.py) fails when a component is added without being registered OR when an entry names a missing file — PROVEN by adding a probe component and watching the suite go red. The inventory half of this item is therefore CLOSED. WHAT REMAINS, and why this item stays open: the ledger records WHAT EXISTS AND WHERE, not what imports what. There are still no import edges for the front end, so questions the Python code graph answers routinely — blast radius, orphan detection, coupling — remain unanswerable for web/. That needs a real TS resolver in the depgraph instrument; size it against the U6 multi-root work before committing. Worth recording as evidence for why the guard was built: the ledger was generated from a `find` whose output truncated at 60 of 62 files, so the first hand-read of the tree silently missed ThinkingLogicPanel and TokenMemoryChart. A machine-checked inventory catches exactly that.

drydocs-webP12taskp2sonnet / main

depends on: Q16

Acceptance: A `/software` route, registered in web/src/modules/registry.ts with `access: 'sme'` (steward + admin) and route-guarded in App.tsx, renders four tabs — Products, Vendors, Documentation coverage, Corpora — over the generated software-registry.json plus the `doc-corpus` rows of load-map.json, with exactly ONE live graph read (the registered QuerySpec `software.doc-coverage.v1`) for the in-graph column. It is a JOIN surface, not a second corpus browser: /docs already browses corpora, and the cells worth rendering are the intersections (a product whose declared corpus can never produce an edge; a product with no docs at all; corpora no product names). FOUR HONESTY RULES hold, each of which a naive build gets wrong: (1) gate state and edge state are INDEPENDENT columns, never one chip — a corpus can be both gate-blocked and permanently edge-less, and one "blocked" chip would falsely imply that signing the gate produces coverage; (2) a deliberately withheld edge renders as a RULING (teal, citing G32), never as a red gap; (3) a database the page cannot read never shows "0 documents" — an unprovisioned dddocs reads "not queried", because 0 is a false claim of absence; (4) an undeclared link is REPORTED, never inferred — the page does not derive bmc-docs -> controlm from taxonomy_path, since no file maps a taxonomy path to a product id. Ledger rows land with the code (ui-components.yaml, ui-tests.yaml and their coverage pins); `npm run build` (tsc -b) and oxlint are clean and the full suite is green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-07 as ALREADY DONE — the retro-groom case. software-registry.json and load-map.json were generated, drift-guarded and committed with ZERO consumers, five vendor icons sat in web/public/vendor-icons/ referenced by nothing, and no backlog item had ever claimed a page for either: the gap was invisible rather than deferred, which is precisely the state an item exists to prevent. O64Ask loses the last completed question and answer on any navigation away and back — persist one completed turn per persona in browser-local storage
drydocs-webP12bugp1sonnet / main
web-console

Acceptance: Navigating from Ask to Explorer and back restores the LAST COMPLETED turn — the question as asked and the answer as returned — instead of an empty panel. `AskRoute` keeps turns in component state today, so React unmounts the route and the turn is gone. Scope, stated as three boundaries because each one is a way to get this wrong: (1) **One completed turn per persona**, keyed by persona, not a growing history — this phase is restoring what the user just saw, not building a transcript feature. (2) **Completed turns only.** An in-progress turn (request in flight) and a FAILED turn are never persisted: restoring a spinner that no request is behind, or re-presenting a stale error as if it were current, are both worse than the empty panel this fixes. (3) **Browser-local storage for this phase**, and the existing TTL-bound explore-ref behavior stays explicit rather than being absorbed into the new store — if a persisted turn references an expired explore-ref, the turn still renders and the reference degrades visibly. A test drives ask → navigate away → navigate back and asserts the completed turn is restored, that a failed turn is not, and that switching persona shows that persona's turn (or nothing) rather than the other's. `config/taxonomy/ui-components.yaml` and `ui-tests.yaml` rows updated per the standing console convention. `npm run build` and oxlint clean.

CONNECTOR SHAPE (merged 2026-08-02, from the company-side answer to tracker T21): the two generic connectors are ACQUISITION ONLY — `fetch(source) -> list[RawPage]`, with cleaning and hashing downstream — over a `Connector` protocol plus a `RawPage` model and an unavailable-source error; `web` speaks public http(s) through stdlib urllib with an INJECTABLE TRANSPORT and an SSRF scheme allow-list; `filedrop` reads a file or a directory of md/txt/html through pathlib. The transport injection and the allow-list are NON-NEGOTIABLE, not preferences: the first is what makes the Track-1 offline tests real rather than network-dependent, and the second is the same guardrail Q12 exists to enforce. Reproduction is producer-authored against that protocol shape — never a copy of the other tree's files.

Q7Reconcile the doc-source registry against what is actually loaded: per-corpus declared / loaded / stale / missing status
drydocs-loadP14taskp2sonnet / main
docmeta

Acceptance: A `drydocs docs-verify` (name at implementer's discretion) reports one row per config/doc-source-registry.yaml entry: the declared target_db, whether that corpus is present in that database, its loaded Document/Chunk counts, and a status of loaded | missing | stale | wrong-db. `stale` = the registry's recorded sha256/captured_at no longer matches what the graph carries (the ADR 0006 §4 gate-preserving freshness rule); `wrong-db` = the corpus is present in a database OTHER than its declared target_db. Exits non-zero on any wrong-db row. Covers every corpus kind the registry admits — scraped web pages, filedrop PDFs, .msg/email extracts — because the check is registry- driven, not per-loader. A unit test drives it against a fake client.

Notes: DONE 2026-08-01 (laptop, concurrent with a desktop R-epic session — claimed in a module that session was not touching). `drydocs docs-verify` + drydocs/docs_verify.py (pure; `run(database, cypher, params)` is the only I/O seam) + 16 offline tests. Suite 1330. . THE DESIGN PROBLEM THE ITEM DID NOT KNOW ABOUT: the registry is corpus-keyed and THE GRAPH IS NOT. Only the Q13 vendor-docs loader writes `corpus_id`; bmc_docs identifies pages by repo-relative `path` and essential_graphrag writes one Document whose `doc_id` IS the corpus id. A "registry-driven, not per-loader" check (the acceptance's own words) is therefore impossible unless the registry says HOW to find each corpus — so every entry now carries `graph_locator: {match: corpus_id|doc_id|path_prefix|none, value: ...}`, guarded by a new test_doc_registry case. Teaching the verifier three loader shapes instead would have made it a per-loader registry that rots silently. . SIX STATUSES, NOT THE FOUR NAMED — two live situations cannot be described by loaded|missing|stale|wrong-db, and calling either "missing" would be a FALSE diagnosis: (a) `db-absent` — bmc-docs and bmc-controlm-utilities declare target_db `dddocs`, which schema/provisioning/01_databases.cypher HAS NEVER CREATED (it makes drydocs, ddlineage, ddcontext, ddall). That is not a load failure, it is G32's open topology ruling, so it reports and does not fail. (b) `unshaped` — jpmc-reports loaded as :DataAsset slices, never on the Document->Chunk spine; its documents are not missing, they were never documents. Only wrong-db exits non-zero, per the acceptance. . LIVE RUN — laptop, container `neo4jtest` (localhost:7687), 2026-08-01: 2 db-absent (both dddocs entries) · 1 loaded (essential-graphrag in ddcontext, 1 Document / 43 Chunks) · 2 unshaped. Exit 0. NOTE THE MACHINE: bmc-docs reports "not found in any existing database either" HERE, which is a statement about this laptop's graph, not about the corpus — the two machines hold separate graphs and git syncs neither. . Two accuracy defects in the first cut, both caught by reading the live output rather than the tests: `unshaped` said "no graph_locator declared" for entries that declared `match: none` on purpose (a ruling read as a silence), and `db-absent` short-circuited before probing, so it never reported WHERE the corpus actually is — the more useful half. Both fixed; the second is now the difference between "your target is unprovisioned" and "...and it is sitting in drydocs meanwhile". . Freshness is never silently reported as fresh: the older loaders write no captured_at, and the row says "uncheckable" rather than implying a comparison that did not happen. . User-requested 2026-07-26 ("we'll need to have a registry comparison or status to check if it's loaded into the db... scraped pages - pdf - etc"). The gap is real: doc-source-registry.yaml DECLARES corpora and test_doc_registry.py enforces the declaration's shape, but nothing anywhere checks that a declared corpus was ever actually loaded, or that it landed in the database it declared. The `wrong-db` case is the one worth the non-zero exit — it is the G30 failure class at corpus granularity. MODULE CHOICE: drydocs-load, not drydocs-docmeta, because the verb lives in cli.py beside m1-verify/m3-verify and must work BEFORE the docmeta component exists (Q6). Re-home it to docmeta if that component takes over corpus state. Startable now against the corpora that exist today (bmc-docs, essential- graphrag, jpmc-reports); the multi-DB cases arrive with G32.

Notes: MEASURED 2026-07-26, drydocs/loaders/cypher/bmc_docs.cypher:97 — `OPTIONAL MATCH (sp:SoftwareProduct {product_id: row.subject_product_id})` guarded by `FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN sp IS NOT NULL ...)`. The assignment edge (email Document → ControlMFolder / process) is NEW relationship semantics and goes through the HITL gate: registered `status: planned` in relationship_vocabulary.yaml with a gate-prompt spec, and no loader writes it until the gate confirms. The SME assignment surface itself may be a later slice — this item's floor is "ingested, unassigned, and gate-registered".

Notes: User source 2026-07-26: "we get emails that reference a failure or activity and I've extracted those as json files and save the original msg format... it may require an SME assigning it to a particular folder or process if it's not extractable from the email." RETENTION, and it is the reason the source pair matters: Outlook purges at 6-18 months, but the extracts are deliberately preserved on a file server until the PROCESS OR PROJECT retires — so after ~18 months the file server holds the only copy and becomes a system of record with a backup obligation, not a cache. Purge is therefore project/process-scoped (a property-scoped delete), NOT a database drop — which is why retention did NOT end up being an argument for a separate database, contrary to the initial guess in that session. Same instinct as the "always keep the original requirement" rule. CLASSIFICATION: production-failure email almost certainly Internal- Confidential (real names, real folder names, incident detail). The .msg/JSON originals live OUTSIDE the repo — the gitignored-PDF precedent — and only mechanism-level references are committed. Distinct from the 2026-07-22 email-DL contact-point idea already in IDEAS: that one is about DL membership as an ontology mapping; this is the email BODY as a document corpus. SIBLING CORPUS NOW EXISTS — READ BEFORE BUILDING (2026-08-05, user flagged the relation): `adhoc-sme-email` was registered in config/doc-source-registry.yaml for a one-off SME evidence email, with connector: email and citation-only shape. This item's acceptance says "a doc-source-registry entry declares THE email corpus", singular, so the first decision here is EXTEND vs ADD — not a discovery to make mid-build. Four properties differ (shape: citation-only vs the ACTIVE Document→Chunk spine; cadence: one-off vs recurring feed; retention: only Q10's extracts carry the post-purge backup obligation; assignment: only Q10 needs the email→folder/process edge), which is why they are two entries today. If the SME folds them, the shape difference becomes a per-Document property — cheap now, expensive once either has loaded.

The point that decided this is its own item rather than a rider on the database question: QUARANTINING DOES NOT DISAMBIGUATE. Putting all three versions in an unstructured-content database leaves all three versions sitting together, still ambiguous — the separation protects OTHER corpora from them, it does not tell you which one is current. Q12Doc-capture scale guardrail: the web connector refuses a bulk scrape above a threshold instead of silently fetching thousands of vendor pages
drydocs-docmetaP14taskp2sonnet / main
docmeta
depends on: Q6

Acceptance: The web-capture entrypoint resolves its FULL target page list from the publisher's own manifest (e.g. the Author-it `toc.json`) BEFORE issuing any content request, and prints tree, page count, and estimated bytes + wall-clock at the configured delay. It REFUSES to proceed (non-zero exit, count named in the message) when the resolved count exceeds a configured threshold unless an explicit opt-in flag is passed; the threshold and the per-request delay are config values, never hardcoded literals. A `--dry-run` prints the same plan and exits 0 having fetched no content. Unit tests drive refusal-above and pass-below against a fixture manifest with NO network (the Track-1 portable rule). No capture script may land before this guard exists — Q6's acceptance carries the same clause.

Notes: User-requested 2026-07-31 after a live feasibility probe of the BMC help trees: "stop or warn the user if they try to scan that many with the script." The numbers are the argument, and they were measured, not estimated — documents.bmc.com publishes a machine-readable `toc.json` per tree, so the page count is knowable BEFORE fetching anything, which is exactly what makes a pre-flight refusal cheap and a post-hoc abort unnecessary: /supportu/INC/ (INCONTROL mainframe) = 10,912 pages ~210 MB raw; /supportu/9.0.20/ (distributed, complete) = 3,860 pages ~74 MB; /supportu/9.0.21/ (distributed, trimmed — no Utilities book) = 1,965 pages ~38 MB. Sampled pages averaged ~19 KB raw / ~6.9 KB extracted text. Two distinct harms the guard prevents, both real: hammering a third-party vendor site (robots.txt ALLOWS these paths, so politeness is entirely on us — there is no server-side backstop), and committing tens of MB of vendor copyright into a repo that is private-but-sometimes-published. A THIRD hazard motivated the request and belongs in the warning text: the operator can pick the wrong tree entirely and not notice. /supportu/INC/ is the INCONTROL MAINFRAME family (Control-D, Control-O, Control-M/Tape, JCL Verify) — its "Control-M" subtree at 40498.htm is Control-M **for z/OS** administration (CTMPLEX/Sysplex, started tasks, user exits, allocated datasets), NOT the distributed estate DryDocs models. So the pre-flight summary must name the TREE and its top-level books, not just a number — a count alone would not have caught this. . DONE 2026-08-04 (LAPTOP), and it closed in two halves rather than one build. THE REFUSAL ITSELF ALREADY EXISTED: scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py shipped it 2026-07-31 (e549f07) with --dry-run, the manifest-resolved page list, the book-by-book pre-flight naming the tree, and 14 offline tests — built ahead of this item's dependency because the capture needed it that day. What was NOT met was the acceptance's other clause, and it is the one that matters for a guardrail: "the threshold and the per-request delay are config values, never hardcoded literals". They were module constants (DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES = 600, DEFAULT_DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0). . WHY THAT CLAUSE IS NOT PEDANTRY, and the reason this closed WITH Q6 rather than before it: Q6 gave the repo a SECOND door to the same third party — the component's web connector. Two doors with two literals is two different notions of "too many pages", decided by which entrypoint the operator happened to use. So the numbers moved to config/doc-capture.yaml (schema drydocs.doc-capture.v1: max_pages, delay_seconds, timeout, retries, user_agent, and the SSRF scheme allow-list), both consumers read it, and a test asserts BOTH files reference CapturePolicy so a future third door cannot quietly re-hardcode. The refusal type moved with it — one rule, one exception class, raised from one place. . The scraper's own fetch() now also enforces the scheme allow-list, which it never did: it would have followed a file:// URL in a tree definition. . Registered as an enforcement-matrix surface (config/doc-capture.yaml -> scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py + drydocs_docmeta/connectors/web.py), so the config-surface guard covers it like every other governed config file.

Q13STANDALONE repeatable vendor-docs ingestion + loader: capture -> convert -> load a NAVIGABLE spine (TOC hierarchy + page_role + abstract), taxonomy only
drydocs-loadP14taskp2sonnet / main
docmeta

Acceptance: A STANDALONE, REPEATABLE pipeline — its own converter, loader, cypher and `drydocs` verb, NOT a widening of load-bmc-docs (user ruling 2026-07-31: "unique enough to use a stand alone, but repeatable ingestion and loader"). It reads the capture manifest as its contract, so capture / convert / load are three re-runnable stages and re-running any of them is idempotent (MERGE on doc_id; a second full run reports zero net change). The converter strips the Author-it/ExtJS navigation chrome and emits body markdown; the loader writes :Document with doc_id, title, breadcrumb, source_url, sha256, captured_at, a deterministic `abstract` (first paragraph) and a derived `page_role`; the toc.json hierarchy loads as IN_SECTION / SUBSECTION_OF; chunks keep the established (:Chunk)-[:PART_OF]->(:Document) + NEXT_CHUNK shape. A TOC node bearing a fragment (`page` + `anchor` in the manifest) attaches to the EXISTING document as a section — it must NOT mint a second :Document. `page_role` derivation is an explicit title rule, NEVER an LLM, and the run REPORTS its unclassified count rather than defaulting pages silently (the G16 values-decide pattern). Every node carries doc_version and version_verified=false. NO meaning edges — no :ControlMUtility, no DOCUMENTS, no SEE_ALSO (Q14's gate). Counts reported per role.

Notes: Layer 1 of knowledge/upgrade-plans/vendor-docs-agent-navigation.md, and the half that needs NO ruling because it only transcribes the publisher's own structure — the taxonomy-before-ontology rule in CLAUDE.md §1. Worth doing alone: hierarchy + role + abstract already beats similarity-search-only, which is all the corpus supports today. STANDALONE, decided 2026-07-31: load-bmc-docs cannot be stretched to cover this and should not be. It consumes hand-written markdown, splits on H2, and infers a provenance TIER from heading text — a heuristic that exists only because that corpus is our lossy paraphrase. This corpus is VERBATIM throughout, so there is no tier to infer, and its real structure (TOC hierarchy, page_role, anchors) has nowhere to go in that loader's model. Two loaders with honest contracts beat one with a mode flag. REPEATABLE means the capture manifest is the contract between stages: scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py already emits it (sha256 per document, page/anchor per TOC node), so a recapture after a version bump re-runs the same convert+load with no code change. MODULE: drydocs-load beside bmc_docs.py, not drydocs-docmeta — the Q7 precedent (it must work BEFORE the docmeta component exists at Q6). The version properties are load-bearing, not bookkeeping: the capture is 9.0.20 (BMC ships NO Utilities book in the trimmed 9.0.21 publication) while the estate runs 9.0.21.300, so the graph must make "the 9.0.20 docs say X, unverified for your estate" the only answer it can produce. The config-side half of that already exists — see Q16. . DONE 2026-08-04 (LAPTOP). The pipeline itself landed 2026-07-31 in 9713118 — converter, loader, cypher, both CLI verbs, 41 offline tests — and the status was never flipped, so the repo went on advertising Q13 in next_ready for four days. This close is the VERIFICATION that flip should have carried, and it found three defects. None of them would fail a test or a load; all three are the "succeeds loudly, does nothing" reporting class this epic hit at G29, G30 and Q8. . (1) THE LOADER COULD NOT REPORT A CHANGE. vendor_docs.cypher had no WAS_GENERATED_BY provenance tail, and BaseLoader derives rows_changed by counting the edges a run attached — so it reported rows_changed=0 on a FIRST load exactly as on a no-op re-run, which makes this item's own idempotence evidence ("a second full run reports zero net change") unfalsifiable. `to_params` had been computing row_checksum all along and nothing read it. Fixed with the delta-only tail (bmc_docs / controlm_folders idiom), placed ABOVE the SUBSECTION_OF block because that block's UNWIND of an empty list drops every row at TOC depth <= 1 from the rest of the statement — the tail-ordering trap bmc_docs.cypher documents, and a test now pins the ordering. . (2) A CAPTURE IS NOT A CORPUS, and the loader wrote the wrong one. It set corpus_id to the CAPTURE id (bmc-controlm-9.0.20-utilities) while this item's own input, config/doc-source-registry.yaml, declares `graph_locator: {match: corpus_id, value: bmc-controlm-utilities}` — so Q7's `docs-verify` would have reported a fully loaded corpus as MISSING. A false negative in the one check built to stop false claims. It survived because nothing has ever run both halves together. Now every row carries BOTH: corpus_id resolved REGISTRY-DRIVEN (the entry naming this capture in its `manifest:` path — never a string transform of the capture id, and an unregistered capture refuses per docmeta invariant 1), and capture_id for which fetch produced the row. A test asserts the loaded id equals what the registry's locator searches for, so the two can no longer drift apart. . (3) doc_id WAS THE BARE TOPIC STEM ("16200"), globally unique across every capture. Author-it reuses topic ids across publications, so loading the already-registered 9.0.21 Parameters tree would have MERGEd onto the 9.0.20 Utilities documents and overwritten doc_version — silently destroying the one distinction this corpus exists to carry. doc_id and section_id are now capture-scoped. "MERGE on doc_id" stays literally true; it is doc_id that got an honest identity. Free to change because nothing is loaded anywhere yet — the build-order argument G31 makes. . Also closed the literal acceptance gap: doc_version + version_verified now ride :Chunk and :DocSection, not only :Document, so a chunk that surfaces alone in a retrieval result still carries the version caveat (Q15 returns chunk-grain rows; this is what lets those rows cite honestly). . NO LIVE RUN — ON EITHER MACHINE, and this is the honest state rather than an untested one (J18). Two independent blocks: the registry entry is `confirmed: false`, so `_gate_loader` refuses the write until an SME gate signs the doc-graph shape; and the 1016-page capture lives in the DESKTOP's data root (DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT is machine-local and git syncs none of it), so this laptop has no payload to convert. Evidence here is offline and reproducible anywhere: 60 tests over a fixture capture, including two full loads through a recording client proving the checksums are identical across runs — which is precisely the condition under which the new delta-only tail fires zero times. The graph-side count stays unproven until a machine holding the capture runs it post-gate. . Registry entries for the two remaining trees: the 9.0.21 Parameters tree in scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py has NO doc-source-registry entry, so convert refuses it by design rather than inventing a corpus id.

Notes: Layer 2 of the plan. Depends on Q13 so the gate argues from loaded evidence rather than from a proposal — the pattern that made the K2/P2 gates decidable in one sitting. Layer 3 is deliberately NOT its own item: Q8's close note established that a relationship cannot span Neo4j databases, and ADR 0006 re-targets doc corpora to dddocs while the software registry keeps writing drydocs, so the estate join would silently drop every edge. Acceptance: Four registered QuerySpecs — docs.utility-lookup.v1 (exact name -> docs grouped by page_role), docs.section-browse.v1 (section -> siblings, one hop), docs.role-siblings.v1 (doc -> same-subject docs of another role), and docs.search.v1 (full-text/vector, explicitly the FALLBACK for "I don't know the name"). Notes: Section 4 of the plan. The point is that an agent usually arrives already knowing the noun ("how do I use exportdefjob?"), and a vector search for a known exact identifier is both slower and less reliable than an indexed exact match — so similarity search is demoted to the fallback path rather than being the only door in. Chunk-free by default because agent context is the scarce resource: triage on abstract + page_role, spend context on text only after choosing. Specs over raw Cypher per the R4/R5 design (ephemeral specs + citations carrying trust and classification) — this keeps doc answers citable and keeps agents off /raw-cypher. Q16Software -> documentation coverage: every product's docs, their residency, their load state and their blockers - including version drift
drydocs-loadP14taskp2sonnet / main
docmeta
depends on: Q13

Acceptance: (a) A COVERAGE REPORT — its own verb, `drydocs docs-coverage` — prints one row per software-registry product, WHETHER OR NOT it carries a `documentation:` block. A product with no documentation at all is the row this report exists to print: exactly one product of thirteen carries that block today, so the original documentation-block-only scope could not answer "what documentation do we hold for Airflow". Each row states the product's coverage against a ladder whose first match governs (no-corpus | unregistered-corpus | ungated | cross-db-blocked | no-locator | not-loaded | product-node-absent | loaded-no-edge | traversable-until-move | traversable | not-probed), a `blockers` list naming EVERY wall rather than only the governing one, and the currency columns: runtime `versions`, `docs_version`, every runtime version NOT in `current_for`, and a currency of current | drifted | unverified | no-docs. `cross-db-blocked` sits ABOVE every load state in the ladder, so a corpus that cannot reach an edge is never reported as merely `not-loaded`. Exits non-zero on drifted and on unregistered-corpus so a version bump or a broken pointer cannot pass unnoticed in CI — and DELIBERATELY NOT on no-corpus or cross-db-blocked, which are true statements about the world that G32 owns; failing CI on an open design ruling trains people to ignore the verb (the test_software_registry.py known-state-pin precedent). (a2) Two further sections, so nothing is counted only from the product side: one row per doc-source-registry corpus that no product names, and one row per source-registry SYSTEM with no product row — which is where Snowflake appears, being absent from the software registry entirely. (a3) The report must work with the database SWITCHED OFF: the cross-DB determination is arithmetic on two YAML fields, so a pure declaration layer answers "is an edge even POSSIBLE" without Neo4j. Graph probing is an optional injected second layer, and every graph-derived field is None (`not-probed`) when it does not run — never 0, which would be a false claim of absence. (b) The pointer reaches the GRAPH so an agent can traverse from the product it is asked about to the documentation describing it, carrying docs_version + the currency status — via the term Q14's gate confirms (DESCRIBES is already registered for :Document -> :SoftwareProduct; this may need nothing new, which is the cheapest possible answer and should be checked FIRST). Nothing is written until that gate signs. (c) `current_for` is only ever set by a human confirming a capture against a runtime version — never derived by parsing version strings. (d) The two never-silent tails are reported rather than dropped: a corpus no product declares, and a DESCRIBES edge that exists in the graph with no declaration behind it. The second is a live case, not hypothetical — see the notes. (e) The report projects a CLOSED field set — ids, enum states, integer counts, declared classification labels, repo-relative paths already committed in publishable config. It never emits `source:` / `notes:` / `source_url:` free text from either registry, because three corpora are classification Internal and their prose describes internal systems. Those entries are still counted and named by id — dropping them would itself be a silent default — but their prose never reaches the output.

Notes: User requirement 2026-07-31: "we do need a pointer to it from the software registry which should contain external-vendor version number, so that when our ingestion process moves to the next major version, we know we need to update the docs." THE CONFIG HALF IS ALREADY BUILT (same session): the `controlm` product in software-registry.yaml carries `documentation: {corpus, docs_version, current_for}` beside its existing `versions:`, and two guards in test_software_registry.py enforce that the corpus id resolves to a real doc-source-registry entry and that the drift is COMPUTABLE (both sides present and typed). The mechanism is deliberately declaration-based: when the estate moves to a new version it lands in `versions:` and is absent from `current_for`, so the gap falls out with no version-string heuristics — because "does 9.0.20 documentation still describe 9.0.21.300?" is a judgement, not a string comparison. The drift-pinning guard asserts the KNOWN state rather than failing on it: drift is a true statement about the world today (9.0.20 docs, 9.0.21.300 runtime), not a code defect, so a red suite would be dishonest. What the test prevents is the drift changing SILENTLY. The operational alarm is this item's report. Home chosen beside `versions:` on the product rather than only on the doc corpus so the comparison is LOCAL — the two numbers a human must compare sit on adjacent lines. ACCEPTANCE WIDENED 2026-08-07 (laptop) at the claim, from the user's question "when we have a tool like Apache Airflow or Snowflake and the internal runs AWS MWAA with its own reference documentation, what connects them all with a Cypher query?". Answering it exposed that (a) was scoped to products CARRYING a `documentation:` block — exactly ONE of thirteen — so the report could not have printed the Airflow row, which is the row the question was about. Widened rather than groomed as a second item: same join, same inputs, same dependency, and two half-reports over one join would grow two status vocabularies that drift. WHAT THE ANSWER TURNED OUT TO BE, recorded because it is the report's subject matter. ONE edge connects them: (:Document)-[:DESCRIBES {target_version}]->(:SoftwareProduct), status active, written by bmc_docs.cypher. There is NO Document->Vendor edge; the vendor hop rides MADE_BY. It resolves for exactly one product — 27 Documents, all controlm. Airflow is a product node with zero docs; SNOWFLAKE IS NOT IN THE SOFTWARE REGISTRY AT ALL. THE FOUR BREAKS, none of which is a bug: (1) the product->corpus pointer is YAML-only — software_registry.py's rows() never reads the `documentation:` block, which is this item's own (b); (2) the doc-source registry has NO graph representation — :DocSource is not a live label and HAS_DOCUMENT is planned with loader ~; (3) the 1016-page vendor-docs corpus is staged and gate-blocked, and vendor_docs.cypher DELIBERATELY writes no DESCRIBES edge because a relationship cannot span Neo4j databases (the Q8 finding) while the registry writes drydocs and ADR 0006 re-targets corpora to dddocs; (4) therefore NO corpus can currently declare its way to a traversable edge — target_db is constrained to {dddocs, ddcontext} by the doc-registry guard and the registry writes drydocs. G32 owns that residency ruling. THE FINDING THAT MAKES THE REPORT WORTH MORE THAN A QUERY: the one working traversal is UNREPRODUCIBLE FROM THE LEDGER. Those 27 edges come from a corpus no product declares, attributed by a hardcoded Python constant (bmc_docs.py SUBJECT_PRODUCT_ID = "controlm"), resident in a database it did not declare (bmc-docs declares dddocs, lives in drydocs). It works BECAUSE OF the residency accident G32 exists to end — so acceptance (d) requires reporting it, and the report must NOT infer the declaration from taxonomy_path, since no file maps a taxonomy path to a product id. (b) IS UNCHANGED AND STILL BLOCKED behind Q14's gate, which is behind G32. The widening touches (a) only. . CLOSED 2026-08-07 (laptop) as a PARTIAL close, said out loud rather than implied. WHAT SHIPPED: `drydocs docs-coverage` + drydocs/docs_coverage.py (555 lines) + 25 tests, commit b297268 — the eleven-state first-match ladder, the `blockers` list naming every wall, the currency columns, the two tail sections (a2), the database-off declaration layer with `not-probed` rather than 0 (a3), the human-only `current_for` (c), both never-silent tails (d) and the closed field set (e). Non-zero on drifted and on unregistered-corpus only, per the acceptance. docs_coverage is classified `load` in test_module_boundary (default-deny) and listed in MODULE_MAP.md. Two follow-on commits from the same session: 0ddf880 emits the doc-governance + product-documentation fields into web/src/generated/software-registry.json and load-map.json, and 9b4cf59 builds the /software console page over them — that page is groomed as its OWN item, O56, because no item had ever claimed it. WHAT DID NOT SHIP, and is the reason this close is qualified: clause (b). No DESCRIBES edge is written from a registry declaration, because the term is Q14's gate to confirm and the residency that makes any such edge possible is G32's ruling to make — target_db is constrained to {dddocs, ddcontext} while the software registry writes drydocs, so today NO corpus can declare its way to a traversable edge. Writing one anyway would be exactly the "invent a relationship during import" failure CLAUDE.md §1 forbids. (b) therefore needs a SUCCESSOR ITEM once G32 rules; the nearest live piece of it — replacing bmc_docs.py's hardcoded SUBJECT_PRODUCT_ID with a `describes_product:` registry field — is parked in the IDEAS.md inbox as Idea-88 rather than groomed, because it touches a loader and a gated corpus behind those same two rulings. WHERE (b) IS NOW TRACKED, added 2026-08-07 on the user's ruling so it is not traceable only by this prose: G32's notes carry a CLOSE CHECKLIST whose first entry is exactly this clause — when that ruling signs, it must either mint (b)'s successor item or record (b) as declined. That puts the pickup on the item that unblocks it rather than on a reader happening to re-open this close note. VENUE (J18): the report is sample-reproducible — `drydocs docs-coverage` runs against the committed YAML with the database OFF and reproduces every declaration-layer row; the graph-probed columns in this session's run were taken on the laptop, `neo4jtest`, `drydocs` DB.

Acceptance: The build the SIGNED gate email-folder-assignment (config/gate-log.md 2026-08-19, 8/8) authorized and did not build: the writer that lands the assignment edge Q10 registered and fenced. (a) THE EDGE, EXACTLY AS RULED: (:Document)-[:CONCERNS]->(:ControlMFolder | :ETLProcess). The spelling is CONCERNS (§A1 -- ASSIGNED_TO was offered and declined: it names the workflow act rather than the meaning), two endpoint classes with one meaning, and the endpoint CLASS recorded on the edge (§A2, the rua §B2 convention this reuses). (b) NO ANONYMOUS ASSIGNMENT (§A3): every write carries `assigned_by` (sme | source-signal) AND an evidence pointer -- the extract line, or the ruling note. A write missing either is refused, and a test asserts the refusal rather than documenting it. (c) THE §B1 BAR IS STRUCTURAL, not prose: only a folder or process name in a STRUCTURED FIELD of the extract may PERFORM an edge. Mentions anywhere in prose -- body OR subject line -- are candidates surfaced to the SME, never edges. The assumed extract contract (the G47 synthetic samples under drydocs/data/samples/email-extracts/) has no such field, so the source-signal path ships with no live producer: a test asserts an extraction pass over the bundled samples writes ZERO edges. (d) THE FLIP LANDS HERE AND ONLY HERE (N13 §B1 -- the build flips, intent never flips anything): docs_email_concerns in 45-local-docs.yaml goes status: planned -> active in this commit, citing the gate. The map row email-concerns-subject was already flipped to confirmed at the gate and is not re-touched. (e) THE FENCE MOVES, IT DOES NOT LIFT: tests/unit/test_email_extracts.py forbids the tokens CONCERNS / ControlMFolder / ETLProcess / ASSIGNED in the LEXICAL loader's cypher. That fence stays on email_extracts.cypher FOREVER -- the lexical loader never gains the write. This item's new cypher file is exempted BY NAME; widening the check to the directory would discharge the fence instead of moving it. (f) UNASSIGNED IS FIRST-CLASS AND NEVER DECAYS (§B3): no sweep, no best-match backfill, no default. This item exposes the unassigned COUNT on a read path; wiring that count into the pending-source-correction union report is a RIDER ON N14, not scope here -- N14 is still todo and a prose dependency on an unbuilt report would strand this build. (g) THE K7 §A1 FENCE STANDS (§C1): this edge says what an email is ABOUT. It never authors folder-to-application attribution, ownership or support routing, and no derived edge may ever cite a CONCERNS edge as its basis -- traversing email -> folder -> application is legitimate READING. Retention rides the assignment (§C2): nothing here deletes, expires or purges an unassigned email. Vocabulary regenerations that ride a flip (schema graph, enforcement matrix, the SQLite mirror) land in the same commit. Full suite green.

Acceptance: A VERBATIM trust claim on a `doc-source-registry` row traces to a RUN ID rather than to prose. The gap, found at the 7c18ff4b port review: the `cdo-frameworks` row was upgraded to VERBATIM on 2026-08-19 on the strength of a run keyed by a Confluence SPACE plus a free-text `--purpose` string — neither of which is a registry id — so the SME had to pick the space by hand because the tie-in to the row was not expressible. The join precedent already exists ONE ROW OVER: `bmc-docs-controlm-utilities` carries `captured_at`, a `manifest:` path to its `capture-manifest.json` whose capture id is stamped by `scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py`, and a `graph_locator` keyed by `corpus_id`. (a) The scrape tool takes a `--registry-id` (or resolves `--purpose` to exactly one row and fails when it is ambiguous) and writes that id into the run manifest. An unresolvable or absent id is an error, not a warning — a run that cannot say which row it fulfils is the case this item exists to remove. (b) The registry row gains `captured_at` and `manifest` at capture time, and `graph_locator` at load time, following the `bmc-docs-controlm-utilities` shape rather than a new one. (c) A test asserts the round trip: a run against a fixture row produces a manifest naming that id, and the row's `manifest` path resolves to it. PORT BOUNDARY, and it is why this item cannot just widen the schema: J51 ruled `config/doc-source-registry.yaml` PER-ENTRY with a FIELD split, and `captured_at` / `manifest` / `graph_locator` are COMPANY-OWNED facts that never cross at a port, while producer fields do. Whatever this item adds must stay inside that split — the producer defines the FIELD and the mechanism; it does not carry the company's VALUES. `tests/unit/test_port_manifest.py` and `test_port_reconcile_guards.py` stay green, and the J16 fall-through guard must see no new default. `poetry run pytest -q`, ruff clean.

Q26The fold's blast-radius scoping is not true of the loaded graph: bmc-docs and essential-graphrag write no corpus_id, so all 28 live :Document rows group under null
drydocs-loadP14bugp2sonnet / main
docmeta

Acceptance: G32 §A ruled that "load-separation and blast-radius are satisfied by corpus_id scoping". The loaded graph does not carry the property that claim rests on. This item makes the signed claim true as written. (a) THE MEASUREMENT, reproducible before and after: `MATCH (d:Document) RETURN coalesce(d.corpus_id, '(none)') AS corpus, count(*) ORDER BY corpus` returns NO rows in the `(none)` bucket on a machine whose corpora are loaded. The close note carries the venue (J18) and the before/after counts. The reading this item was raised on: 2026-08-21, laptop, `neo4jtest`, `drydocs` DB — all 28 rows (27 bmc-docs + 1 essential-graphrag) grouped under `corpus_id: null`. (b) BOTH LOADERS STAMP IT: `bmc_docs.cypher` and `essential_graphrag.cypher` write `corpus_id` on every `:Document` and `:Chunk` they MERGE, equal to that corpus's `id` in `config/doc-source-registry.yaml` (`bmc-docs`, `neo4j-docs-essential-graphrag`) — read from the registry row, not a literal invented at the loader — and the write is idempotent (a re-run changes no other property, and `rows_changed` is ZERO on the second run). (c) EXISTING LOADS ARE MADE TO MATCH, per machine and J18-tagged: state which of reload-or-backfill each machine takes, and do it. G102's R3 clause already ran a full bmc-docs delete+reload once per machine, so a reload IS the sanctioned vehicle and no new mechanism is needed — but it must actually be re-run AFTER (b) lands, because a stamp that exists in the loader and not in the graph is the exact shape of the defect being fixed. (d) THE REGISTRY SAYS WHAT IS TRUE: `bmc-docs`'s `graph_locator` either moves to `match: corpus_id` / `value: bmc-docs`, or keeps `match: path_prefix` with the reason for keeping it written on the row. Its comment today reads "pre-dates corpus_id"; once (b) lands that sentence is false, so one of the two must change. `docs_verify.py`'s header prose ("only the Q13 vendor-docs loader writes corpus_id") is corrected in the same pass. (e) THE SENTINEL FOLLOWS THE FACTS: `docs_coverage.EDGE_CORPUS_UNKNOWN` is documented as "A REAL, EXPECTED state" because `bmc_docs.cypher` writes no corpus. If (b)+(c) make that unreachable for the loaded corpora, the comment says so and names what could still produce the bucket. The constant is NOT deleted on the strength of one machine's counts — the other machine's graph is independent. (f) NO ONTOLOGY CHANGE AND NO GATE: `corpus_id` is a provenance PROPERTY on labels that already exist — no new edge, no vocabulary entry, nothing flipped from planned to active. This item does not reinterpret a signed ruling; it makes it hold. If (b) turns out to be wrong for bmc-docs (the corpus is genuinely path-identified and the gate's scoping claim is narrower than it reads), that is an ESCALATION to the gate, not a decision this item takes.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY HANDLED, since two surfaces look like they handle it: the registry gives bmc-docs `match: path_prefix` and `docs_coverage.py` carries an explicit `(no corpus_id)` sentinel — so `docs-verify` and `docs-coverage` both work today. What does NOT work is the governance claim above them: G32 §A named corpus_id scoping as the mechanism that replaced the three-database wall, and 28 of 28 live Documents carry no corpus. The verifier having a workaround is not the same as the scoping being real. TIMING, and why the natural vehicle already fired: G102 (done) ran R3's delete + reload live on the laptop (27 -> 0 -> 27 DESCRIBES, 374 chunks) AFTER the fold — and the reloaded documents still carry no corpus_id, because the loader does not stamp one. A future reload is the second chance, which is why clause (c) makes re-running it explicit rather than assuming it. Module drydocs-load: both cypher files live in `drydocs/loaders/`. Epic docmeta / phase 14 by the Q7/Q13/Q24 precedent. p2 and sonnet: the change is small and the acceptance is written, but it touches two loaders plus a per-machine graph action. DONE 2026-08-27 (laptop, Lane B) — WITH THE LIVE HALF RUN, venue-stamped (J18: laptop, neo4jtest, `drydocs` DB). (a) MEASURED BEFORE: 28 Documents / 417 Chunks, ALL in the (none) bucket (corpus_id not even a known property key — the server said so). MEASURED AFTER: Document bmc-docs 27 + neo4j-docs-essential-graphrag 1; Chunk 374 + 43; the (none) bucket EMPTY on both grains. (b) both cyphers stamp corpus_id on :Document AND :Chunk, read from the registry row (bmc adapter: reg.get(name).id beside the Q18 read; graphrag: to_params resolves source_id through SourceRegistry once per instance) — never a loader literal. THE BUILD'S OWN CATCH, now a guard: the first live reload silently DROPPED the bmc stamp because BmcDocChunkRow's extra=ignore swallowed the adapter's new key — the field is now REQUIRED on the row model, the test pins is_required(), and the same pass removed the model's subject_product_id="controlm" shadow default (the Q18 defect one layer down). Idempotence: rows_changed 374 on the stamping reload, ZERO on the re-run (both corpora). (c) LAPTOP: scoped delete + reload executed (the G102 R3 vehicle; 27+374 and 1+43 deleted then reloaded stamped). DESKTOP: pre-Q26 graph stays unstamped until its own reload — handed to the desktop session to ride its Q24 load (which reloads corpora there anyway). (d) the registry KEEPS match: path_prefix WITH THE REASON ON THE ROW: the locator file is shared while the two graphs are independent, so a corpus_id locator would read MISSING on any machine whose reload has not run; the row names the switch condition (both reloads landed) — and docs_verify.py's "only the Q13 loader writes corpus_id" header prose is corrected in the same pass. docs-verify run live: bmc-docs + graphrag both PRESENT. (e) EDGE_CORPUS_UNKNOWN stays, its comment recast: unreachable for a freshly loaded corpus, still real for the other machine's pre-Q26 graph and for any future loader that forgets the stamp. (f) no ontology change, no gate, no flip — a provenance property on existing labels, exactly as fenced. Suite 2596 passed / 11 skipped; ruff clean.

Acceptance: The loop engages only when Tier-1 context is insufficient; hard caps enforced (iterations <=2, next-step vote x3, fix loop <=2, per-question token budget) with a forced-solve fallback so every run terminates with an answer or an explicit "cannot answer"; the enhance branch writes ONLY the task-scoped context graph named by the R1 ruling (never drydocs / ddlineage — a test proves it); per-iteration snapshots are captured and renderable in the existing d3 graph pane; the R3 ledger records per-iteration cost so caps are tunable from data.

Notes: CLOSED 2026-08-01. tier2.py is a PURE controller taking llm/retrieve callables rather than the pipeline, so the whole loop is testable with fakes and the private coupling stays in pipeline.py; retrieval REUSES Tier 1, which is why the <=2 fix loop and the read-only pre-flight are inherited rather than reimplemented — there is exactly one path that runs Cypher, and a test pins the executed sequence. Two bounding decisions the acceptance did not settle, both stated in the module docstring: (1) a tie or unparseable vote counts as SOLVE — the failure mode of voting is not a wrong answer, it is a loop that will not stop, so ambiguity resolves toward terminating; (2) the token budget bounds EXPLORATION, not the whole run — once spent the loop stops enhancing, but evidence already bought still gets one final answer call, deliberately over budget and recorded as budget.exhausted. Refusing that last call would spend the budget gathering evidence and then discard it unanswered. With NO evidence and no budget the run makes zero calls. The R1 residency proof is STRUCTURAL, not behavioural: task_graph.py has no driver, session, database name or Cypher in it, and the test reads the source and fails if any appears. A comment saying "do not persist this" is not a control; a module with nothing to persist with is. Also fixed a real gap the acceptance named only in passing — the ledger recorded iteration=1 for EVERY call, so per-iteration cost was unavailable and the caps were untunable from data. The loop now drives the iteration counter and a test pins round 2's calls to round 2. Every cap reports whether it BIT (forced_solve, budget.exhausted), and the budget is reported on runs it never touched — a limit you can only see once it has bitten is one nobody can tune before it does. Web: rather than a second d3 copy, the deterministic placement engine moved to lib/forceLayout.ts and GraphExplorer now consumes it; the new ask/TaskGraphPane keeps its OWN visual language on purpose, because a viewer who mistakes a synthesized sub-question for a real graph node has been actively misled. Snapshots are cumulative per phase (start / iteration N / final) so any frame renders alone. Suite 1315; tsc + build clean; O42 ledger 27/64 (TaskGraphPane bound to ask/).

The specs' vocabulary is taken FROM the schema and the relationship-vocabulary registry, never invented here: if the audit finds a spec that needs a term the registry does not carry, that term is not added in this item — it routes through the HITL gate like every other edge-meaning question, and the spec stays marked unavailable until the gate rules. `poetry run pytest -q`, ruff clean.

R21Neo4j warnings are discarded at three points, so a query built on retired vocabulary presents as an empty answer — carry notifications through the runner into AgentRun and surface them on the admin path

Acceptance: A Neo4j notification raised by a query the console ran is visible to an admin afterwards. Today it is dropped three times over — Ask renders only rows and errors, the API runner discards the driver's notifications, and `AgentRun` telemetry has no field to hold them — so the 2026-08-20 incident produced FOUR non-fatal warnings about retired vocabulary and presented as a clean empty result. (1) The API runner stops discarding the driver's notification/summary payload and carries it alongside rows. (2) `AgentRun` telemetry persists it (a warnings payload with, per notification, its code, title, position and severity), written by `agents/common/agent_run_writer.py` on the same run record that already counts the executed Cypher. (3) The ADMIN review path displays it. The end-user Ask answer is NOT changed into an error: a non-fatal warning is not a failure, and turning it into one trades a silent defect for a noisy one. The user-facing surface may show at most a neutral "this answer has diagnostics" affordance; the diagnostics themselves live on the admin path. The existing exposure boundary holds unchanged: the console shows router decision, generated Cypher, rows, timings and source — never model prompts or chain-of-thought. Notifications are Neo4j's own output about the query, so they sit on the safe side of that line; the acceptance says so explicitly because "surface more diagnostics" is exactly where that boundary erodes. Tests: a run whose Cypher raises a known non-fatal notification (an unknown label is the cheap one) produces an `AgentRun` carrying it, and the admin surface renders it; a clean run carries an empty payload rather than a missing field. Where the test needs a live database it SKIPS naming the venue (J18). `poetry run pytest -q`, `npm run build` and oxlint clean for the admin surface.

R22"how many towers are there" answers 0 by silently proxying the synthesized UI term Tower onto the :TOMRole graph label — give Tower a declared source contract that text2cypher cannot cross
drydocs-apiP15bugp1fable / main
agentic-qa

Acceptance: Ask can no longer answer a question about **Tower** by quietly reaching for a different concept that happens to share a word. What happened (2026-08-20): `how many towers are there` matched no registered spec, correctly escalated to Tier 1, and the text2cypher model chose the real graph label `:TOMRole` as a proxy for the UI term — `MATCH (t:TOMRole) WHERE t.name CONTAINS 'Tower' ...` — returning `0`. But `/explorer` defines Tower as a SYNTHESIZED UI concept backed by the in-repo `TOWERS` definitions (`web/src/data/towers.ts`), not by any graph label. The answer was not merely wrong; it crossed from UI taxonomy into TOM ontology without saying so. Three things are owed: (a) **A declared source contract for Tower** — Tower is written down as a UI-taxonomy concept whose authority is the in-repo definitions, with its source, its cardinality and its relationship (or absence of one) to `:TOMRole` stated in words. It lives where the console's other declared taxonomy lives under `config/taxonomy/`, so it is a fact a tool can read rather than a convention in a component. (b) **A registered count spec** so the question resolves at Tier 0 against the declared source and returns the real number with its provenance ("from the Explorer Tower definitions, not from the graph"). (c) **A guard against the silent proxy** — schema grounding must not let a term with a declared non-graph source be answered by a graph label chosen for lexical similarity. Where the model cannot ground a term, the answer says the term is not a graph concept and names where it IS defined, rather than reporting a count of zero. **VIA THE GATE — the hard boundary of this item.** Any BINDING between the UI Tower concept and graph vocabulary — a `:Tower` label, an edge from Tower to `:TOMRole` or to anything else, or a mapping asserting the two are the same subject — is an ontology decision and routes through the HITL gate (`docs/restructure/03-hitl-sme-flow.md`) with `status: planned` until confirmed. This item may declare that Tower's source is NOT the graph (that is a statement about a UI concept, and it is what unblocks (b) and (c)); it may not decide what Tower means in the ontology. If the SME rules Tower is a graph concept, that ruling supersedes (a) and the spec is rebuilt against it. Tests: the question returns the declared count with its stated source; a question naming any declared non-graph term never produces Cypher against a lexically similar label; `poetry run pytest -q`, ruff clean, `npm run build` clean if the definitions move.

Third thread of the same incident as R20/R21 and deliberately separate: R20 is stale spec vocabulary, R21 is discarded warnings, and this one is a CATEGORY error — a synthesized UI term answered from the ontology. Fixing the first two would not have prevented it. Model fable, unlike its two siblings, because the item sits on the taxonomy/ontology boundary: deciding that a term's authority is a UI definition rather than the graph is exactly the kind of call CLAUDE.md routes to the top tier and fences with the gate. Module drydocs-api (the spec registry, verified at this groom) with the definitions half in web/ and config/taxonomy/. The console's existing exposure boundary is unchanged and is not part of the fix: it already shows router, generated Cypher, rows, timings and source, and never model prompts or chain-of-thought. DONE 2026-08-21 (desktop). (a) config/taxonomy/ui-concepts.yaml (drydocs.ui-concepts.v1): Tower declared as a UI-taxonomy concept -- source web/src/data/towers.ts#TOWERS (in-repo definitions, verbatim port of the dark-landing mockup), cardinality 4, members home/auto/cards/shared with titles, graph_binding: none, and its relationship to :TOMRole stated in words (a ROLE vocabulary that shares the word "CTO"; Tower is not a TOMRole, CatalogLOB or ProductLine). The header writes the hard boundary: the file may say the source is NOT the graph; any binding (a :Tower label, an edge, a sameness mapping) is an ontology decision for the HITL gate, status: planned, and a confirmed binding supersedes the row (graph_binding != none hands the term back to the graph path). Reader: drydocs_core/ui_concepts.py. (b) NOT a Cypher spec -- a spec is Cypher and the declared source is not the graph -- but the same Tier-0 outcome: agents/graph_qa/declared_terms.py answers a question naming a declared term BEFORE the router, deterministically, with provenance ("from the Explorer Tower definitions ... not from the graph"), tier `declared`, StepRecord kind `declared` with cypher None and rows = cardinality, SourceRecord config/taxonomy/ui-concepts.yaml#Tower, zero LLM calls, zero reads. (c) THE GUARD: the short-circuit means text2cypher is never reached for such a term; as the second line, build_schema_prompt appends a "NOT graph concepts" section naming each declared term, its source and the refused proxy, instructing an empty cypher. TESTS tests/unit/test_ui_concepts.py (7): declaration == towers.ts in both directions (keys, titles, count, source exists); count question -> "There are 4 towers: Home Lending, Auto, Credit Cards, Shared Services ... not from the graph"; whole-word + alias matching (watchtower does not match); the pipeline answers with NO read and NO LLM call and the only step is `declared`; the schema prompt carries the section; a planned/confirmed binding returns the term to the graph path. npm build not needed: no web file changed (towers.ts is read, not moved). Suite green.
