Acceptance: (a) THE VALUE STOPS REACHING DISK: after an Ask run, the `api_token` VALUE appears nowhere in `agents/graph_qa/.adk/session.db`. Either the control part is stripped from the event before ADK persists it, or the value is redacted on write and the live token is held only in process memory for the turn. Observed 2026-08-21 (desktop, session `ask-jdoe4821-wjtacr8x`): the raw bearer token appears verbatim in all three user events in the `events` table, because `askApi.ts` sends it as an in-band message part and ADK writes every part as given. (b) A REGRESSION TEST ASSERTS IT — a run (real ADK, or the stubbed runtime the handshake was designed to allow) leaves no `api_token` value in the store. This is the clause that keeps it fixed. `control.py`'s own docstring says the in-band shape was chosen so it is "testable without an ADK runtime", so the test costs little. (c) THE HANDSHAKE STILL WORKS — R5's observable behavior is unchanged: the agent still registers each executed Cypher as an ephemeral spec owned by the ASKING session, Open-in-Explorer and Export still work for that user, and a foreign session still 404s. (d) THE STORES ALREADY ON DISK ARE PURGED, per machine and J18-tagged. The tokens sitting there stay REPLAYABLE for the life of the API process — `InMemorySessionStore.issue` (drydocs_api/sessions.py) mints `secrets.token_urlsafe(24)` with no expiry, and only `revoke` or a restart ends one — and nothing prunes the store, so they accumulate. The close note names each machine whose `.adk/session.db` was purged. This is disk hygiene, NOT history rewriting: `.adk/` is gitignored (`.gitignore`, the "ADK local runtime state" block), so nothing reached the repo. (e) THE CHANNEL SAYS WHAT IT PROMISES: `control.py` states that control parts never reach the LLM — which holds — and says nothing about persistence. That silence is how this shipped. The fixed file states the persistence property beside the LLM one. No ontology change and no gate: this is a credential-handling defect in an existing mechanism.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-22 (laptop) from Idea-155, which was filed branch-side on `feat/ui-workstream` as that branch's Idea-151 and re-filed at 155 on main (151 there is the unrelated stale-render entry, groomed to Y5 — R18's notes cite the branch number and are corrected to point here in the same commit as this item). p1, above the two siblings that read the same store, because it is a live credential at rest with no expiry: a copy taken from the file replays for the life of the API process. Two things make it worse than a stray log line — the accumulation, and the contradiction one row over. `Envelope` deliberately reduces question text and caller identity to sha256-plus-length so neither is persisted, while the credential beside them is written raw; the repo already decided how it feels about persisting sensitive fields on this path. DONE 2026-08-25 (laptop `NewThinkpad`). Fixed at the ONE choke point every session service persists through -- `append_event` -- rather than at any single backend, so local SQLite, a database URI and the in-memory service are covered identically. `graph_qa/control.py` gains the pure rule (`redact_control_text`, `SECRET_CONTROL_FIELDS`, `REDACTED_VALUE`), `common/session_redaction.py` the duck-typed `RedactingSessionService`, and `serve.py` installs it by replacing the one ADK function `fast_api` calls to build the service -- verified patched and idempotent in the agents venv (google-adk 2.3.0). THE THING THAT MADE THIS SUBTLE, and the reason clause (c) has its own test: upstream, the persisted event's `content` IS the object the agent reads as `ctx.user_content` (`Runner._append_user_event` passes it straight through). Redacting in place would have taken the token away from the very turn that needs it and Open-in-Explorer would have quietly stopped working. So nothing is mutated: an event with nothing secret is returned BY IDENTITY, and one with a token is replaced by a deep copy that is written instead. (a) VALUE STOPS REACHING DISK -- the field survives, the value does not. A deletion was rejected: the R5 trail is read for "did this turn carry control", which a deletion silently answers no. `api_url` is deliberately NOT in the secret set -- it is configuration, and redacting it would cost readability for no security gain. (b) `tests/unit/test_session_redaction.py` -- 14 passed / 1 skipped. S10The four :BusinessApplication MERGE loaders refuse to run against a pre-cutover graph, instead of minting the silent twin S3 argued about but never guarded
drydocs-loadP9bugp1sonnet / main
structure-remediation

Acceptance: Every loader that MERGEs `:BusinessApplication {app_id}` — seal_applications.v1, manual_seal_attribution.v1, pat_product_mapping.v1, software_registry.v1 — refuses up front when the target database holds any `:BusinessApplication` with a null `app_id`, i.e. a node a pre-S3 loader created. The refusal follows the established idiom (`batch_port_orchestrator._assert_endpoint_registries_present`): it runs BEFORE `super()._load`, so a refused run writes nothing at all — not even the :JobRun — and the message names the remediation (backfill `app_id = seal_id` on the pre-cutover nodes, or rebuild, and count first) rather than only the symptom. The count excludes `:SchemaMeta` exemplars, which carry the real label with no key and would otherwise red every load (the `_count_real_nodes` precedent). Unit tests cover both directions per loader against a fake client — refuses on a dirty graph, proceeds on a clean one — plus one test asserting the refusal happens before any write. Full suite green.

Notes: WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT AN ENHANCEMENT: it fired. The company ran `drydocs load seal_applications` against a graph that took the S3 CODE but never the S3 re-key and got `Neo.ClientError.Schema.ConstraintValidationFailed` mid-load — after partial commits, because batches commit per flush. S3's own §C2 states the mechanism exactly ("a uniqueness constraint IGNORES NULLS, so a loader still MERGEing on seal_id would silently create a SECOND node rather than fail") and seal_applications.cypher:23 repeats it in a comment, but nothing enforces it at load time. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH: graph-tests/business-application-identity TC-01 detects exactly this condition — but it is a POST-HOC verification run, so it reports the damage after the loader has done it. A detector that only runs when someone remembers to run graph-verify is not the guard the null-tolerance argument implies. SCOPED OUT: the four MATCH-only sites (batch_port_orchestrator, seal_attribution, seal_contacts, folder_attribution) do not mint twins — a MATCH miss writes nothing. They have the opposite failure (silent no-op), which their own registry-presence refusals already cover. Also out of scope: retiring the seal_id alias (§G3, a separate later gate) and any migration/backfill verb — this item REFUSES, it does not repair. Worth fixing in passing if trivial: `batch_port_orchestrator._assert_endpoint_registries_present` still counts on the pre-S3 key (`_count_real_nodes("BusinessApplication", "seal_id")`), which works only while the alias is dual-written. COMPANY-SIDE READ: this is producer payload that lands with the next port; it does not substitute for the T23 migration, which is live-state repair on their graph. BUILT 2026-08-05 (desktop). `drydocs/loaders/app_identity.py` carries `PreCutoverApplicationGuard`, mixed in BEFORE BaseLoader on all four MERGE-site loaders so its `_load` reaches the MRO first — the refusal lands ahead of `_preflight_indexes` as well as `_open_run`, which a test pins: a graph this broken should not be reported as an index problem. 15 tests in `tests/unit/test_app_identity_guard.py`, three of them parametrized across all four loaders (refuses dirty / proceeds clean / writes nothing), plus a message test (count + backfill + rebuild + the TC-03 pointer) and a COVERAGE test that re-derives the MERGE-site list from the .cypher files rather than trusting the enumeration — a fifth MERGE site added without the guard reds that test instead of passing by omission. Suite 1575 passed / 5 skipped. FIXED IN PASSING, as the item's own note anticipated: `batch_port_orchestrator`'s endpoint probe counted on the deprecated `seal_id`. It works today only because the alias is dual-written; it would have started reporting an empty registry against a good graph the day §G3 retires it. Now counts on `app_id`.

S12Environment-drift guard: the suite fails loudly when the interpreter's packages disagree with poetry.lock
drydocs-coreP6chorep2sonnet / main
structure-remediation

Acceptance: A session-scoped guard in tests/conftest.py reads poetry.lock, and for every locked package that is ALSO installed in the running interpreter, asserts the installed version equals the locked one. Packages absent from the interpreter are skipped, not failed — the lock carries groups and extras a given install legitimately does not select. On drift the guard fails the session ONCE, before any test runs, naming sys.prefix, the count, and the first few offenders as `name locked X, installed Y`; it must also name the usual cause (an inherited VIRTUAL_ENV taking precedence over the in-project venv) and the remedy, because the failure the guard replaces was misread as twenty broken tests. Guard on DRIFT, never on the venv PATH: a path assertion would fail Docker, tox and system-python runs that are correctly provisioned, and would miss a wrong-version install inside the right directory. Proven both ways, and the fixture for the negative case is already on this machine: DryDocs/.venv reports zero drift across 65 installed locked packages and the suite stays green, while the shared sandbox venv reports 16 — including click (locked 8.1.8, installed 8.3.2) and ruff (locked 0.5.7, installed 0.15.11). A unit test drives the comparison function over synthetic lock/installed pairs so the negative case is reproducible off this machine. CI green on both matrix versions — CI installs from the lock, so it has no drift by construction.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-18, the follow-up the S11 session's venv note (internal/repo-README.md, PR #3) deliberately left out. The note tells a reader what to do; nothing MAKES the wrong environment announce itself. What it costs today: poetry honours an already-activated VIRTUAL_ENV ahead of the in-project venv poetry.toml pins, so a shell with another environment active runs the suite against that one. Under click >= 8.3 typer 0.12's secondary flags raise TypeError and about twenty CLI tests go red — tests that are not broken. That cost a full investigation cycle during the S11 work, and it is self-concealing: the suite looks broken, CI looks green, and the two disagree for a reason nothing on screen explains. The click case is the CHEAP one. The same venv carries ruff 0.15.11 against the exact 0.5.7 pin that pyproject calls load-bearing (J10 stage 0, authority docs/ruff-format-convergence.md) because formatter output varies across versions. A `ruff format` run from the wrong environment reformats the tree to a different convention and lands a diff CI then blocks — the failure J10 exists to prevent, and the one that ran RED for 100+ consecutive runs between 2026-08-05 and 08-12 without anyone looking. That is the real argument for p2 rather than the p3 its S8/S9 siblings carry: this guard protects a gate that has already failed silently once. Placement is tests/conftest.py, not tests/unit/ — integration runs deserve the same guard, and the file already owns session-scoped concerns (the shared Neo4j driver teardown). REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: assert sys.prefix equals the repo .venv. Simpler to write and wrong — it fails correctly-provisioned runs that are not in-project, and passes a mismatched install that happens to sit in the right folder. Drift is the defect; the path is only its most common cause, and belongs in the failure MESSAGE rather than the assertion. RETRACTED 2026-08-18, and the retraction is EVIDENCE FOR THIS ITEM. These notes previously carried a second finding -- "`poetry run pytest` needs PYTHONPATH=. locally or tests/unit/conftest.py cannot import drydocs_core" -- filed as a separate defect wanting its own backlog item. It is not a defect and there is no second item. Re-run cleanly: with VIRTUAL_ENV and PYTHONPATH both unset, `poetry env info --path` resolves to DryDocs/.venv and `poetry run pytest tests/unit` is 2176 passed / 5 skipped, with `import drydocs_core` succeeding on the bare interpreter -- the package is installed in the project venv, so no PYTHONPATH was ever required. The original ModuleNotFoundError came from poetry resolving to the INHERITED sandbox venv, which has no DryDocs install: the same root cause this item guards, wearing a different mask. Kept rather than deleted because it is the sharpest argument the item has -- the wrong environment did not merely produce twenty false failures, it manufactured a phantom SECOND defect that was written down and nearly scheduled. A guard that names sys.prefix on drift would have closed the question in one line instead. DONE 2026-08-21 (desktop). tests/env_drift.py (pure: parse_lock / installed_versions / drift / report) + a pytest_sessionstart hook in tests/conftest.py that raises UsageError ONCE, before any test, naming sys.prefix, the count, the first offenders as `name locked X, installed Y`, the usual cause (inherited VIRTUAL_ENV -> agents/.venv) and the remedy (`unset VIRTUAL_ENV`, `poetry install --sync`). Drift, never path. Absent packages skipped. PROVEN BOTH WAYS on this desktop (MSI): DryDocs/.venv -> 0 drift across 66 locked packages, suite 2315 passed; negative case reproduced through DRYDOCS_LOCK_PATH pointing at a synthetic lock (click 0.0.1, rich 0.0.2) -> the session stops at collection with `ERROR: ENVIRONMENT DRIFT: 2 of 2 installed locked package(s) disagree ... click locked 0.0.1, installed 8.1.8 ...` (exit 4), and tests/unit/test_env_drift.py drives the comparison over synthetic pairs so the negative case runs anywhere. The agents/.venv on this machine has no pytest, so the 16-drift sandbox figure from the groom was not re-measured here; the synthetic path is the reproducible proof. CI installs from the lock: no drift by construction.

S13None of the six S8 command modules can be imported first: `import drydocs.cli_docs` in a fresh interpreter raises AttributeError, and the full suite hides it
drydocs-loadP6bugp2sonnet / main
structure-remediation

Acceptance: MEASURED, REPRODUCIBLE FROM THE REPO (2026-08-23, no live services, no machine-specific state -- run it in any checkout): six fresh interpreters, six failures. `python -c "import drydocs.cli_schema"` -- and the same for `cli_ingest`, `cli_verify`, `cli_variables`, `cli_docs`, `cli_plan` -- each raises `AttributeError: partially initialized module 'drydocs.<name>' has no attribute 'app' (most likely due to a circular import)` at `drydocs/cli.py:955`. Only `import drydocs.cli` succeeds, which is the ONE import CLAUDE.md's smoke test names, which is why the S8 split shipped this on 2026-08-21 and nothing went red. THE CYCLE, read at the code rather than inferred: each command module opens with `from drydocs import cli as _root` (and a `from drydocs.cli import ...` for shared state) BEFORE it executes its own `app = typer.Typer(...)`. So importing a command module first runs the ROOT's module body to completion, and the root's last statements are `COMMAND_MODULES = (cli_schema, cli_ingest, cli_verify, cli_variables, cli_docs, cli_plan)` followed by `_sub.app.registered_commands` -- reaching back into the very module that is still mid-import and has no `app` yet. Import the root first and the same code runs in an order where every `app` exists, so the cycle is invisible. (a) ALL SIX import cleanly as the first import of a fresh interpreter. (b) A GUARD THAT CAN ACTUALLY SEE IT: the check must run each import in its OWN SUBPROCESS. An in-process guard proves nothing here -- whichever module the test session touched first primes `sys.modules` and the failure vanishes, which is precisely the mechanism that hid this. Proven to FAIL on the current code before the fix lands (J26). (c) THE STANDING SYMPTOM THIS EXPLAINS, and the acceptance's cheapest witness: `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_paths.py` run ALONE is 4 failed / 45 passed today, while the same tests inside the full suite are green (2328 passed, 9 skipped at commit 81f1eb08) -- a targeted run gives a FALSE RED that costs a session its afternoon. After the fix, that module passes standalone and in the suite. (d) THE S8 CONTRACT SURVIVES, all three clauses `drydocs/cli_docs.py`'s own header states: the root remains the composition root and the only module that may wire other components; the sub-apps still merge FLAT, so `drydocs --help` lists exactly the same verb names (diff the help output before and after); and `_client` still resolves THROUGH the root at call time, so tests that monkeypatch `drydocs.cli._client` keep working. (e) The `python -c "import drydocs.cli"` line in CLAUDE.md's working agreements widens to cover the command modules, or the new guard is named there -- a smoke test that checks one of seven entry points is how this class returns. CANDIDATE SHAPES, none mandated -- the acceptance is the behavior, not the design: move the root's merge loop out of the module body into the function that builds/runs the app; or have each command module import the root lazily inside its functions instead of at module scope; or hoist the shared state (`console`, `_REPO_ROOT`, `_gate_loader`, the chain constants) into a third module both sides import, which is the ADR 0002-A shape and the only option that removes the cycle rather than reordering it.

Notes: Found 2026-08-23 (laptop) during a groom, while checking which Ready-to-pull items were safely dispatchable -- not from the inbox. The trail: running `tests/unit/test_repo_paths.py` in a partial selection produced four failures that the full suite does not produce, which looked like an order-dependent test until the six-interpreter probe showed the import itself is broken and the test was reporting it faithfully. WHY IT IS p2 AND NOT p1: the shipped CLI is unaffected -- `drydocs --help` and every verb work, because the real entry point imports the root first, and `drydocs_core` is untouched. What is broken is every OTHER way in: a targeted pytest run, an editor's test runner, an agent importing one command module to read its verbs, and any future consumer that does `from drydocs.cli_docs import ...`. Cheap to fix, and it decays badly -- each further split adds another module that only works if something else imported first. RELATION TO S8 (done, 2026-08-21): this is S8's residue, not a reversal of it. The split was right and the module boundary it drew is the one MODULE_MAP.md line 77 records; the defect is purely that the composition root reaches back into its parts at import time. Same family as the standing repo theme in J26/G80/J47 -- a thing is declared, and the check that would notice it is missing or looks in a place where it cannot fail. CROSS-CITE 2026-08-28 (grooming): S15 (groomed 2026-08-26 from Idea-159) is THE SAME DEFECT captured twice — neither cited the other until now. S13 is the CLAIM SURFACE: whoever fixes this closes S15 in the same commit (S15 now depends_on S13 so the board never offers both). S15's narrower acceptance clauses (file-alone runs shown, sibling modules checked, coupling named where the next reader meets it) fold into this item's acceptance as written. DONE 2026-08-27 (laptop, Lane B; closes S15 in this commit). SHAPE: the hoist — the acceptance's third candidate, the only one that removes the cycle rather than reordering it. New drydocs/cli_shared.py holds every constant and stateless helper the six command modules consume (loader registry, chains, gate/adapter/opt helpers, console); the command modules import cli_shared and NEVER the root at module scope; the root imports both. Mutable state stays on the root as the tested patch surfaces: _client unchanged, and the _registry cache is read/written by cli_shared._source_registry() THROUGH drydocs.cli at call time (function-local import — the _client idiom), so monkeypatch targets drydocs.cli._client and drydocs.cli._registry both keep working, untouched tests prove it. (a) all eight CLI modules import first-cleanly. (b) tests/unit/test_cli_import_order.py: subprocess-per-import, plus a second parametrized guard asserting drydocs.cli never lands in sys.modules when a non-root module imports first (removed-not-reordered as a tested property). RED first at 1c77e539: 14 failed / 1 passed. (c) test_repo_paths.py standalone: 4 failed / 45 passed before -> 49 passed after; green in the full suite both sides (2560 passed / 11 skipped after). (d) drydocs --help byte-identical before/after (non-tty capture both sides); composition root still the only ENTRYPOINT_MODULES exemption — the list is untouched; flat merge unchanged at the root bottom. (e) CLAUDE.md working-agreements line widened to name the guard and the eight entry points. MODULE_MAP.md row added; drydocs.cli_shared classified load in test_module_boundary (default-deny caught it first, as designed). Root re-exports the moved names (__all__ compat surface) so every existing drydocs.cli.X consumer — tests, scripts/render_load_map.py, the company port — keeps its import path.

G33Load the DryDocs code-dependency snapshot into the graph under a Project root, using the seeded-but-unused software ontology
drydocs-loadP16requirementp2fable / main
self-documentation

Acceptance: A `drydocs load-code-snapshot` verb reads the newest knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/*.json (schema depgraph-machine-first/v1) and MERGEs it idempotently into `drydocs`, so it survives the wipe-and-rebuild cycle like every other loader and is re-runnable from committed files with zero data loss (the ADR 0002 D3 stateless test). Everything hangs off an explicit (:Project {project_id:'drydocs'}) root so "is this our own code?" is one hop, and modules carry a label that CANNOT collide with the software registry's :SoftwareProduct nodes. The new node classes and relationships plus their binding to the SWO terms are registered `status: planned` and go through the HITL gate; no loader writes them until it confirms. snapshot.ps1 stays DECOUPLED — the session ritual must keep working with no database running. GATE SIGNED OFF 2026-07-27 (config/gate-prompts/self-documentation-code-graph.yaml, 36/36, 0 edits) — THIS ITEM IS NOW CLEARED TO BUILD and the acceptance is tightened to what was ruled. FIVE registrations already exist at `status: planned`, not the four this text originally named: node classes :Project and :CodeModule, edges HAS_MODULE, IMPORTS and IS_ENCODED_IN (the third added by the §E1(b) SWO ruling). Build to these rulings: (1) ONE :Project root; the snapshot's SIX scan roots are a `project` PROPERTY on :CodeModule, never sibling nodes (§B1a). (2) :CodeModule is keyed on `file_id`, the repo-relative path — the only non-colliding key (§C1a/§C4). (3) `circular` loads as a property (§C3). (4) edges carry the M2 pull-provenance fields first_seen_at / last_seen_at / last_run_id like every other loader (§D3). (5) IS_ENCODED_IN targets the already-seeded SwoClass Python, value derived from node.extension (§E1b). (6) the :CodeModule / :SoftwareProduct exclusion is a GRAPH-TEST, not a constraint — Neo4j cannot declare label mutual-exclusion (§F1). (7) the loader DISCRIMINATES ON meta.tree and REFUSES tree-mode input (§G1a) — BUILD NOTE 2026-07-27, post-sign-off review finding: the tree-mode files carry NO `meta` key AT ALL (verified: top-level keys are schema/projects/nodes/edges/stats/rels), so there is no `tree: true` to refuse on — and a naive `*.json` name-sort picks tree-this-version.json as "newest" ('t' > 'd'). A literal negative check (`meta.get('tree')` truthy → refuse) would therefore ACCEPT the tree files. Implement as a POSITIVE assertion: select `drydocs-*.json` only, require `meta` PRESENT and `meta.tree == false`, refuse loudly on anything else. The §G1(a) ruling stands; this fixes only its literal reading. SECOND selection subtlety, found LIVE at the first build run: a date-only name (drydocs-20260727.json, a one-off) sorts ordinally AFTER every timed name of the same day ('.' > '-'), so raw string sort picked the stale 12:42 capture over the 17:33 one. "Newest by filename timestamp" (§H2) must PARSE the drydocs-YYYYMMDD[-HHMM] timestamp, date-only keyed as 0000. (8) `abs_path` is DROPPED; load rel_path / file_id only (§H4). (9) a refusal must be LOUD — see the "succeeds loudly, does nothing" family. (10) register the source in config/source-registry.yaml with classification Internal-Public (§H6).

Notes: User source 2026-07-26: load the DryDocs project code snapshot under the software ontology, "which may prevent missing code fixes", plus "a way to distinguish it's for drydocs project and not the products metadata". Cheap because both halves already exist and neither is used: ontology.cypher seeds 7 SwoClass + 6 SwoProperty terms (Python, Shell, SQL, "is encoded in", "implements", "has specified data input/output", "uses platform") with ZERO consumers anywhere in the tree, and snapshot.ps1 already writes a code dependency graph every session that never enters Neo4j — it is JSON plus a viewer.html. *** THREE PREMISES IN THIS NOTE WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED HERE (gate self-documentation-code-graph, 2026-07-27). All three came from describing the artifact without opening it, and finding them was the gate's main value: (i) it said the depgraph schema "already carries a `projects` key (=1), so the Project root matches the producer's own shape rather than inventing one". IT CARRIES SIX — drydocs, drydocs_core, drydocs_deepdoc, drydocs_lineage, drydocs_remediation, tests — and 142 of the 183 nodes declare a project that is NOT 'drydocs'. The single root was a modelling CHOICE presented as a read-off; §B1 made it a choice and ruled (a). (ii) it said "664 nodes / 86 edges at the latest". That figure belongs to tree-this-version.json, a one-off TREE-mode capture (540 files + 124 dirs, projects: ['drydocs1'], a CONTAINS relationship). The rolling dependency snapshots are 183 files / 98 edges — the real load is about a QUARTER the size this note implied. (iii) both shapes declare the SAME schema string depgraph-machine-first/v1, so a loader keying on it alone mis-reads one; §G1 ruled discrimination on meta.tree. *** TARGET IS `drydocs`, NOT dddocs, and the stated purpose is what decides it: "prevent missing code fixes" means traversing from a DryDocs module to the loader to the Control-M job it loads. That is a path query, so they must share a database — and code is not reference material ABOUT a system, it IS one, deterministically derived from source we control with no authority ambiguity. Same character as folders and jobs. The Project root is what keeps it from polluting product metadata. RE-PHASED 2026-07-26, same day, on the user's call. Groomed into phase 6 / component-topology with the marginal fit flagged rather than hidden; the user ratified it as a NEW CAPABILITY — "similar to a major version change of the snapshot ritual" — so it moved to the new phase 16 (self-documentation) and the new epic of the same name. The framing that earned the phase: the depgraph ritual's output stops being a JSON file a human reads and becomes a queryable :Project subgraph, which is a different KIND of thing, not a bigger version of the same thing. ID KEPT AS G33 DELIBERATELY. It no longer matches its epic letter, which is the lesser of two evils: ids are stable references (groom rule, git-readme §backlog id allocation) and G33 is already named in commit a37043a, which cannot be amended. Epic U is therefore the first epic whose opening item carries another letter's id — historical, not a pattern to copy. New items in this epic take U1, U2, … (T is NOT free: it is the port-turn series, e.g. docs/port-T12-*.md). Load only the LATEST snapshot as current state; the ~70 dated files (not ~20) are a time series available later if code evolution is ever wanted — §A5 scoped that out. "Do not build it" is DISCHARGED as of 2026-07-27: it meant "not before the gate", and the gate is signed. Build to the ten rulings in `acceptance`. WHAT THIS ITEM STILL DOES NOT DELIVER, stated so it is not judged against a promise it never made (§H5): the motivating query — traverse from a DryDocs module to the loader to the Control-M job it loads — needs an edge NOTHING in a dependency snapshot knows, because that mapping lives in the loaders' Cypher, not in their imports. This item lands the code subgraph and the shared database that make the join possible; the join itself is a separate Epic U item.

Acceptance: The tech-writer persona's staleness ranking states which commit it ranks on — the commit the document CLAIMS to reflect (DesignDoc.commit, an author's assertion transcribed from the doc's own prose) or the commit that last TOUCHED the file (a git fact) — the plan records the rule WITH its reason, the query matches the rule, and the known divergence is used as the worked example: drydocs-startup-refresh-runbook carries a135a6d (2026-07-20) while its last touch is 554a4e8 (2026-07-31, Rev 5). If both readings are wanted, both are surfaced under distinct names; what may not survive is an undefined ranking.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-07 (pm) from Idea-48. Both readings are defensible — which is precisely why the undefined state is the defect — so the item is allowed to pick, provided the reason is written where the next reader finds it. Epic U rather than L: the ranking belongs to the U1-U3 code-graph review personas, even though the :DesignDoc node itself is Epic L infrastructure. DONE 2026-08-09 (desktop): RULED — the re-verify queue ranks on the CLAIM, with the git fact reported beside it and the gap between them named as its own measure. Three names now exist where one word did: claim_lag (cited commit -> HEAD, the ranking key), touch_lag (last-touching commit -> HEAD, reported, never ranked on), citation_lag (cited -> last-touching, the 'edited but never re-verified' measure). WHY THE CLAIM WINS: the mandate is the status of documents joined to the code they CLAIM to describe, and a reader trusts the citation; ranking on touch_lag answers a different question and would hide this unit's own subject, since a doc edited ten times without ever being re-checked ranks as FRESH under it. WORKED EXAMPLE, re-measured at 4ecfca0 rather than copied from the item (the divergence widened a month): drydocs-startup-refresh-runbook cites a135a6d (2026-07-20, squash day), last touched by 180f4ae (2026-08-06) — claim_lag 792, touch_lag 122, citation_lag 670. The two readings put the SAME document at opposite ends of the queue, which is the entire argument for naming the key. The item's Rev-5/554a4e8 figures were the Idea-48-era snapshot and are superseded. citation_lag ratifies the label Run 2 had to invent in-flight ('stale cite, fresh content'). THREE DEGENERATE CASES RULED rather than left to whoever writes the query: no citation -> rank unknown, never fresh, never silently substitute touch_lag; citation unreachable from HEAD -> rank maximum, because an uncheckable claim is worse than one measured far behind; and the trap — a citation can RESOLVE and still not be an ancestor. VERIFIED, and machine-dependent (J18: desktop): all five pre-squash cites Run 2 listed (807e050, ac2ea2e, 97ee81c, 24d6a4b, 0e036ff) resolve as objects here because the local archive/old-history-2026-07-20 tag keeps them alive, and NONE is an ancestor of HEAD — so `git cat-file -t` passes them on this desktop and fails them on a fresh clone, and `rev-list --count` returns a meaningless number across the disjoint history. The check must be `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. No query-pack file exists for Phase 3 (the A1-A6 pack is Phase 1's, in the tech-debt skill; the documentation skill carries no graph queries), so the plan IS the query spec and now names the exact measures and commands. New guard file tests/unit/test_code_graph_review_plan.py (5 tests): the three measures are named, the ranking key is stated, the conflation cannot return, each degenerate case is ruled, the reachability check is ancestry not object existence. All five PROVEN to fail against the original Unit 2 text before being trusted (J26) — and that exercise caught a real defect in the first draft of the conflation guard: it was line-scoped, while the original defect spanned a line break, so it would have passed the very text it exists to catch.

The fix belongs in the SIBLING depgraph extractor rather than in a producer wrapper — U16 is sizing exactly that in-house-vs-sibling trade, and if this can only be done here as a fourth post-processing wrapper step, that IS the trigger U16 names for forcing the call; say which one it turned out to be in the close note. THE RULE IS THE INTERPRETER'S, not a heuristic: walk up from the file while the directory is a package (__init__.py present); the first ancestor that is not is what Python puts on sys.path. That yields the script's own directory for a loose script and the non-package parent for a module inside a package, which is exactly what `python -m pkg.mod` makes importable. DESIGN CHOICE worth the record: the extra root is APPENDED after the project roots, a deliberate departure from Python, which searches the script directory FIRST. Precedence only matters when one name resolves both ways, and there the existing answer is what every committed snapshot was built from — appending makes the change purely additive, so it can create a missing edge and cannot move one that already resolved. Pinned by a test with shared.py present at both locations rather than left to a comment. U21IMPORTS edges are never retracted, so fan-in inflates permanently and test debt under-reports — the code-snapshot load sweeps nodes but not edges
drydocs-loadP16bugp1sonnet / main
self-documentation

Acceptance: After a `drydocs load-code-snapshot` run, the graph's IMPORTS edges EQUAL the loaded snapshot's IMPORTS edges for every module that snapshot CONTAINED. Today they do not, and the edge only ever grows. THE DEFECT, reproduced 2026-08-13 (desktop, neo4jtest, drydocs DB) against the graph freshly reloaded from that day's snapshot: `drydocs/loaders/seal_attribution.py` still carries an IMPORTS edge to `drydocs/loaders/base.py`; the file contains ZERO occurrences of the string "base" (K8 removed the import at 4df4df2) and the snapshot records no such edge. The edge SURVIVED a full re-run, so this is not staleness and a refresh does not fix it. Size at that reading: 985 live IMPORTS edges against 982 in the snapshot -- three ghosts, one of which put `loaders/base.py` at fan-in 32 where the tree says 31, i.e. it distorts the repo's most-cited change-risk metric. A5 is affected in the DANGEROUS direction: a module whose test import was DELETED keeps the ghost edge and still counts as tested, so test debt reads better than it is. THE FIX. (a) PER-SOURCE RETRACTION, NEVER A GLOBAL DELETE. For each module the loaded snapshot INCLUDED, the edges this loader wrote that the snapshot no longer asserts are retracted; edges touching a module the snapshot did NOT include are untouched, and edges written by any other loader are untouched. The scoping discipline already exists one file away -- base.py's D7 mark pass refuses to run without either `full_extract` or a scope property, logging why -- and this clause is that discipline applied to relationships. (b) DECIDE AND RECORD: marked or deleted. The node half MARKS (removed_from_source_at + removed_by_run_id) rather than deleting, which is what makes U13's "every query pack filters tombstones" rule necessary. Whichever this item picks, it states the reason, and if edges are marked then the read paths that consume IMPORTS (the tech-debt skill's A3/A5 queries, the review-plan seed queries) filter them the same way U13 made node queries filter -- a tombstoned edge that no query excludes is the same defect wearing a property. (c) THE COUNT IS REPORTED, never silent: edges retracted (and reactivated, if marked) appear in the load summary beside nodes_marked_removed, per the STG_PARSE_QUALITY house rule the node pass already follows. (d) GUARDS, both of them: loading snapshot A (edge present) then snapshot B (edge absent for a module B contains) leaves no live edge; and loading a snapshot that OMITS a module entirely leaves that module's edges alone. The first proves the sweep works, the second proves it cannot over-reach. (e) VERIFY ON THE REAL GRAPH at close, venue named per J18: live IMPORTS count equals the newest snapshot's, the seal_attribution -> base ghost is gone, and the A3 top fan-in is RE-MEASURED rather than re-typed.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-13 (targeted groom -- node labels and Cypher loaders) from Idea-118. SAME FAMILY AS U13, one grain down: the D7 sweep tombstones removed MODULES and nothing sweeps removed EDGES, so the import graph is append-only by construction. The repo holds exactly one edge-retraction precedent -- `drydocs/loaders/cypher/stale_edge_cleanup.cypher` (D1: delete condition edges for changed jobs before re-asserting them) -- and a grep of the tracked tree on 2026-08-13 finds NO live caller for it, so the pattern exists as a file rather than as a mechanism. Worth reading it anyway: it is the shape (scope to the keys this run touched, delete, re-assert) this item generalizes. MODULE drydocs-load: the change is in the loader and its Cypher, not in the depgraph instrument -- the snapshot is CORRECT, the load is what never subtracts. PAIRS WITH U22, found in the same session and from the same cross-check (the loaded graph vs the snapshot it was loaded from): U22 detects a load that never RAN, this fixes a load that runs and never RETRACTS. Neither substitutes for the other -- U22's freshness check would have reported this graph as current, because it was. DONE 2026-08-21. (a) CodeSnapshotLoader._retract_stale_edges, run right after the D7 node mark pass: MATCH (m:CodeModule)-[r:IMPORTS|IS_ENCODED_IN|HAS_MEDIA_TYPE]->() WHERE m.last_run_id = $run_id (the snapshot's own coverage, module by module) AND r.source = 'depgraph-snapshot' (this loader's edges only) AND r.last_run_id <> $run_id (not re-asserted this run) -> delete, count. A module the snapshot omits keeps every edge; another loader's edge is never a candidate; like the mark pass it refuses without full_extract and logs why. (b) RULING: DELETED, not marked, reason recorded in the loader docstring + code_snapshot.cypher header + the tech-debt skill: a snapshot edge carries no curated state, is fully re-derivable and comes back by MERGE on the next snapshot, while marking would have pushed the U13 filter onto every IMPORTS consumer (A1-A6, review-plan seeds, m1-verify) -- a tombstoned edge one query forgets is this defect wearing a property. Follows the D1 stale_edge_cleanup precedent (scope to touched keys, delete, re-assert). (c) edges_retracted on LoadSummary, as_dict, the O28 status envelope (drydocs.loader/edges-retracted, info) and the :JobRun property, beside nodes_marked_removed. (d) tests/unit/test_code_snapshot_retraction.py (query shape, ordering, full_extract refusal, template stamps) + tests/integration/test_code_snapshot_retraction.py against a throwaway EE container, PASSED 2/2 (2026-08-21): A then B leaves no a->base edge while c->base (c omitted from B) survives and c is node-tombstoned; reload A re-creates the edge; a hand-curated IMPORTS edge between two touched modules survives a full re-load. (e) LIVE (desktop, neo4jtest, drydocs DB, snapshot drydocs-20260821-0340.json): BEFORE the load the graph was STALE at 891 IMPORTS vs 1032 in the snapshot (U22's symptom, not this item's) and the seal_attribution->base ghost was already absent -- the graph had been rebuilt since the 08-13 reading, so this run could not re-kill it; what it proves instead is the equality clause: AFTER `drydocs load-code-snapshot` (run 91d03d0e, nodes_marked_removed 4, edges_retracted 0) live IMPORTS = 1032 = snapshot, and the per-edge set is IDENTICAL once the tree-mode `drydocs/` prefix is normalised (0 live-only, 0 snapshot-only). U26snapshot.ps1 counts three directory hops to find the depgraph sibling, so the session ritual's last step dies in every git worktree — resolve the main working tree instead
graph-infraP16bugp2sonnet / main
self-documentation

Acceptance: `knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/snapshot.ps1` writes its JSON when run from a git WORKTREE, not only from the main checkout. The defect: the script resolves the instrument by counting hops — `(Resolve-Path "$here\..\..\..\depgraph")` (line 177 at this groom) — three levels up from `knowledge/depgraph-snapshots`. From the main checkout that lands on the real sibling and is correct; from `.claude/worktrees/<name>` the same three hops land on `.claude/worktrees/depgraph`, which does not exist, and the script dies with `Resolve-Path : Cannot find path`. That makes the ritual's last step unavailable to exactly the sessions CLAUDE.md tells to use worktrees. The fix resolves the repo's MAIN working tree rather than counting directories: `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` returns the SHARED `.git`, whose parent is the main checkout, and it gives the same answer from a worktree and from the checkout itself. Hop-counting is removed, not patched with a second special case. `tests/unit/test_probe_instrument.py` is fixed in the same pass: its skip path resolves the sibling the same wrong way and prints the same wrong location (`depgraph sibling checkout absent at ...\worktrees\depgraph`), so today the script and the test AGREE WITH EACH OTHER while both are wrong — which is why nobody caught it. After the fix the test skips only when the sibling is genuinely absent, and its message names the real path it looked in. Verified from BOTH venues and both stated: one run from the main checkout and one from a worktree, each writing its `<project>-<date>.json`. That two-venue check is the acceptance, not a nicety — this is a shared instrument and it was deliberately not fixed inside the session that found it precisely because a worktree-only verification proves nothing. Retention behavior (newest-only, U12) and the CI check are unchanged.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-21 (laptop) from Idea-150 (2026-08-20, prio proposed Med). Hit at the O57 session close: everything before the JSON write succeeded — all renders written, the script's own CI check reported GREEN at HEAD — and only the snapshot was lost, so that session produced no drift record. Module graph-infra / epic self-documentation / phase 16 by the U15, U24 and U25 precedent (the snapshot instrument's own items live there). Mechanism only, no gate. Line 177 is cited as of HEAD 28a5ccf0; the file moved during the 2026-08-20 CI-check fixes, so match on the `Resolve-Path` expression rather than the number. DONE 2026-08-21 (desktop). snapshot.ps1 resolves the instrument beside the MAIN working tree: `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` -> parent = main checkout -> ..\depgraph, with a named failure when the sibling is absent (the path it looked in, and that a worktree needs nothing of its own). Hop-counting removed, not patched. test_probe_instrument.py resolves the sibling the same way (_main_worktree(), falling back to the file's repo root only when git is unavailable) and its skip names the real path. VERIFIED FROM BOTH VENUES (desktop MSI): from a throwaway git worktree .claude/worktrees/u26-check the patched script resolved the sibling and WROTE drydocs-code-20260821.json (commit ff22f527, branch HEAD) where the old one died on Resolve-Path; from the main checkout it wrote the same and printed `ci: GREEN at HEAD ff22f52`. Found on the way: PS 5.1 reads the script as ANSI, so an em dash INSIDE a string literal decodes to bytes containing a smart quote that PowerShell honours as a string delimiter (parser error at first run) -- string literals kept ASCII, with a comment saying why. Y5The one-key claim commit goes RED in CI: the pushed-claim protocol and the roadmap stale-render guard contradict each other — RULED at the groom as tolerate status-only drift, and this item applies it
drydocs-planP8bugp2sonnet / main
backlog-sharding

Acceptance: A correct one-key claim — flipping one `items/<id>.yaml` to `in_progress`, committing and pushing BEFORE starting work, exactly as the ADR 0013 claim ritual prescribes — no longer turns CI red. It does today. First hit 2026-08-20 (laptop), the first post-shard claim: `items/D10.yaml` → `in_progress`, pushed, and `test_plan_roadmap.py::test_committed_roadmap_page_matches_its_sources` failed on CI run 32440366508 because `roadmap.html` derives item STATUSES and the claim commit ships no regen. The close-out commit went green, so the red window is precisely the work interval the claim exists to cover — every correctly-claimed item spends its whole in-flight life with CI red at the claim sha, which trains sessions to read red as noise. That is the exact habit Idea-111 was raised to break, and it cost 100+ consecutive ignored failures last time. **THE RULING, made at the 2026-08-21 groom because Idea-151 asked the groom to decide: option (b) — the stale-render guards TOLERATE STATUS-ONLY DRIFT.** Option (a), regenerating renders inside the claim commit, was rejected on a discriminating ground rather than on convenience: it puts `board.html` and `roadmap.html` into every claim commit, so two machines claiming DIFFERENT items collide in generated files — which is the shared-line conflict ADR 0013's sharding was built to remove. Sharding made a claim a one-file edit; a guard must not put it back to three. What the item delivers: (1) The committed-render guards (`test_plan_roadmap.py::test_committed_roadmap_page_matches_its_sources` and its board/ideas siblings — enumerate them; do not fix one and leave the family inconsistent) compare the committed render against its sources with item `status` NORMALIZED OUT, so a status-only change does not fail them while any other drift still does. (2) The tolerance is BOUNDED and proven: a test asserts that a title, module, phase, dependency or new-item change to the backlog still fails the guard. A guard relaxed without that test is a guard deleted. (3) Rendered pages therefore may show a stale STATUS between claim and close. That is stated plainly in `docs/restructure/backlog/README.md` — the board is a render, the item file is the claim channel, and CLAUDE.md already says roll-ups are derived — so nobody reads the board as the authority on who holds what. (4) The other rule is restated to MATCH rather than left standing as written: CLAUDE.md §0 and the backlog README say a claim is a one-key edit of one item file, committed and pushed, with no render step. Whichever of the two rules is not chosen must be amended in the same commit; the defect here is that both stood as written and contradicted. `poetry run pytest -q` green, and a claim-shaped commit (one item file, status only) verified green in CI at its own sha.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-21 (laptop) from Idea-151 (2026-08-20, prio proposed Med), whose closing line — "Groom decides; don't leave both rules standing as written" — is the authority for ruling it here rather than parking it. The ruling and its reason are written into the acceptance so the next session inherits the argument, not just the verdict. Epic backlog-sharding / module drydocs-plan / phase 8 by the Y2 precedent: Y2 built the shard, its claim mechanics and its render/validator wiring, and this is the defect that surfaced the first time that ritual ran. Scope note for whoever pulls it: the fix is in the GUARDS, not in the renderers. `roadmap.html` and `board.html` keep deriving status and keep being regenerated at session close by `scripts/render_board.py`; only the staleness ASSERTION learns that status-only drift is expected mid-flight. DONE 2026-08-21 (desktop). FAMILY ENUMERATED by experiment, not by reading: a status-only flip with no render fails exactly ONE committed-render guard -- test_plan_roadmap::test_committed_roadmap_page_ matches_its_sources. board.html has no test guard (only the ritual's git diff), gates.json / load-map / enforcement-matrix / ideas do not derive item status, so the family was already consistent and the fix is one guard. (1) MECHANISM: render_roadmap embeds `<!-- sources-fingerprint: sha256 -->` -- sha256 over roadmap.yaml + the backlog with every item's `status` normalised out + the renderer's own source bytes. The guard passes outright on an identical page, passes as STATUS-ONLY DRIFT when the committed fingerprint equals the current one, and fails on anything else. (2) BOUNDED, proven by test_status_only_drift_is_tolerated_and_nothing_else_is: todo->in_progress and ->done leave the fingerprint unchanged; a title, module, phase, depends_on, new-item or roadmap edit changes it; and by construction an edit to plan_roadmap.py itself changes it too (a renderer change without regen still fails -- the old guard's other job is kept). Proven live on the tree: flipping C27's status without rendering -> 11 passed; editing its title -> 1 failed. (3) backlog/README.md states the stale-status consequence and why the board is not the authority. (4) CLAUDE.md pull rule amended in the same commit: "a claim ships NO render". The claim commit for THIS item (pushed before the fix) is the last red claim sha; the next one-key claim after this lands is the CI proof and is recorded on that item. Suite 2295 passed. Two findings from the 2026-08-08 business-layer location experiment ride this gate as required confirmations (merged at the 2026-08-09 groom, from Idea-90): (i) real-world location data arrives at MIXED GRAIN — street address, city and country all appear as "the location" in one source — so the question is not only which levels exist but how a located node DECLARES the grain it carries; and (ii) the epistemic line between an enumerable site and an AGGREGATE PRESENCE CLAIM: a source stating "177 locations" is a claim ABOUT sites, and exploding it into 177 nodes manufactures data, so the gate rules how such a claim is held without becoming fake sites. Nothing loads before sign-off; everything ambiguous routes to the SME session.

GN1ADR 0012 — name loaders, commands and sources by the DATA, not the tool: the three-axis model and the deprecation policy
docsP6taskp1opus / main
generic-naming

Acceptance: An ADR settling the naming BEFORE any rename moves, because the alternative is renaming twice. It must carry: (a) THE MOTIVATION IN THE SME'S OWN TERMS -- company jargon entered a repo that was meant to be generic from the start (seal, pat, m1/m3 milestone ids). This is the standalone- generalization goal, not cosmetics, which is why it earns an ADR and an epic rather than a rename commit. (b) THE THREE-AXIS MODEL: the command names the SUBJECT (the data), the source registry entry carries CADENCE and ACQUISITION, and the profile is DERIVED by filtering on cadence. Today all three are collapsed into one LoadStep with hand-assigned profile tuples. (c) THE THREE BANDS: prepare / load / verify. Only the load band is source-keyed; forcing check or bootstrap into a source scheme is the same category error inverted. m1-verify and m3-verify carry the same defect as seal and pat -- milestone ids meaning nothing to a reader -- and are renamed with everything else. (d) THE SAAS QUESTION, ruled not dodged. The SME flagged ServiceNow and Jira as possible exceptions because they are widely known. The ADR should record the counter-argument and the ruling: the subject names the data (cmdb, work-items), the source id names the tool, because the SME's own CSV-to-database argument applies one level up -- if CMDB data later arrives from a different ITSM, load-servicenow is wrong and load-cmdb is still right. (e) DEPRECATION POLICY. CLI verb names are a PUBLIC CONTRACT -- company crons, scripts and the run-drydocs skill call them by name. New names ship with old ones as deprecated aliases for one port cycle, then drop. Precedent exists: cli.py already carries legacy-verb aliasing for supplements. (f) THE SOURCE-ID LAYER IS NOT A UNILATERAL PRODUCER CHANGE, and the ADR must say so or GN2 will discover it the hard way. Registry v2 is a COMPANY-CANONICAL SURFACE per the standing divergence ledger, and retired ids are governed by the D4 refusal list. Renaming pat:* source ids is a cross-repo reconciliation with new retired-id entries, not an edit. The ADR rules which of the three layers move together and which move separately. (g) The alternatives considered and rejected, with reasons -- an ADR that records only the chosen option is a design note wearing a decision's clothes.

Notes: Claimed at raise, 2026-08-11 (desktop), SME direction: "I agree with the ADR approach and everything ... the rename may require its own standalone epic, with a frozen change and port." NEW EPIC generic-naming, prefix GN. NOTE ON THE PREFIX: the free single letter was T, and it was NOT taken -- T1-T22 is the cross-repo TRACKER id space cited throughout docs/port/port-prompt.md, so T-series backlog items would collide semantically with T15/T18/T22. That is the same class of collision that produced the G70 duplicate this morning; declining it cost one letter.
